58:1.ar: قَدۡ سَمِعَ ٱللَّهُ قَوۡلَ ٱلَّتِي تُجَٰدِلُكَ فِي زَوۡجِهَا وَتَشۡتَكِيٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَٱللَّهُ يَسۡمَعُ تَحَاوُرَكُمَآۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَمِيعُۢ بَصِيرٌ
58:1.en: Allah hath heard the saying of her that disputeth with thee (Muhammad) concerning her husband, and complaineth unto Allah. And Allah heareth your colloquy. Lo! Allah is Hearer, Knower

58:2.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يُظَٰهِرُونَ مِنكُم مِّن نِّسَآئِهِم مَّا هُنَّ أُمَّهَٰتِهِمۡۖ إِنۡ أُمَّهَٰتُهُمۡ إِلَّا ٱلَّٰٓـِٔي وَلَدۡنَهُمۡۚ وَإِنَّهُمۡ لَيَقُولُونَ مُنكَرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡقَوۡلِ وَزُورࣰ اۚ وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَعَفُوٌّ غَفُورࣱ‏
58:2.en: Such of you as put away your wives (by saying they are as their mothers) - They are not their mothers; none are their mothers except those who gave them birth - they indeed utter an ill word and a lie. And lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

58:3.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يُظَٰهِرُونَ مِن نِّسَآئِهِمۡ ثُمَّ يَعُودُونَ لِمَا قَالُواْ فَتَحۡرِيرُ رَقَبَةࣲ مِّن قَبۡلِ أَن يَتَمَآسَّاۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ تُوعَظُونَ بِهِۦۚ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ خَبِيرࣱ‏
58:3.en: Those who put away their wives (by saying they are as their mothers) and afterward would go back on that which they have said, (the penalty) in that case (is) the freeing of a slave before they touch one another. Unto this ye are exhorted; and Allah is Informed of what ye do

58:4.ar: فَمَن لَّمۡ يَجِدۡ فَصِيَامُ شَهۡرَيۡنِ مُتَتَابِعَيۡنِ مِن قَبۡلِ أَن يَتَمَآسَّاۖ فَمَن لَّمۡ يَسۡتَطِعۡ فَإِطۡعَامُ سِتِّينَ مِسۡكِينࣰ اۚ ذَٰلِكَ لِتُؤۡمِنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦۚ وَتِلۡكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِۗ وَلِلۡكَٰفِرِينَ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ
58:4.en: And he who findeth not (the wherewithal), let him fast for two successive months before they touch one another; and for him who is unable to do so (the penance is) the feeding of sixty needy ones. This, that ye may put trust in Allah and His messenger. Such are the limits (imposed by Allah); and for disbelievers is a painful doom

58:5.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُحَآدُّونَ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ كُبِتُواْ كَمَا كُبِتَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡۚ وَقَدۡ أَنزَلۡنَآ ءَايَٰتِۭ بَيِّنَٰتࣲۚ وَلِلۡكَٰفِرِينَ عَذَابࣱ مُّهِينࣱ‏
58:5.en: Lo! those who oppose Allah and His messenger will be abased even as those before them were abased; and We have sent down clear tokens, and for disbelievers is a shameful doom

58:6.ar: يَوۡمَ يَبۡعَثُهُمُ ٱللَّهُ جَمِيعࣰ ا فَيُنَبِّئُهُم بِمَا عَمِلُوٓاْۚ أَحۡصَىٰهُ ٱللَّهُ وَنَسُوهُۚ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ شَهِيدٌ
58:6.en: On the day when Allah will raise them all together and inform them of what they did. Allah hath kept account of it while they forgot it. And Allah is Witness over all things

58:7.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ مَا يَكُونُ مِن نَّجۡوَىٰ ثَلَٰثَةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ رَابِعُهُمۡ وَلَا خَمۡسَةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ سَادِسُهُمۡ وَلَآ أَدۡنَىٰ مِن ذَٰلِكَ وَلَآ أَكۡثَرَ إِلَّا هُوَ مَعَهُمۡ أَيۡنَ مَا كَانُواْۖ ثُمَّ يُنَبِّئُهُم بِمَا عَمِلُواْ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءٍ عَلِيمٌ
58:7.en: Hast thou not seen that Allah knoweth all that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth? There is no secret conference of three but He is their fourth, nor of five but He is their sixth, nor of less than that or more but He is with them wheresoever they may be; and afterward, on the Day of Resurrection, He will inform them of what they did. Lo! Allah is Knower of all things

58:8.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ نُهُواْ عَنِ ٱلنَّجۡوَىٰ ثُمَّ يَعُودُونَ لِمَا نُهُواْ عَنۡهُ وَيَتَنَٰجَوۡنَ بِٱلۡإِثۡمِ وَٱلۡعُدۡوَٰنِ وَمَعۡصِيَتِ ٱلرَّسُولِۖ وَإِذَا جَآءُوكَ حَيَّوۡكَ بِمَا لَمۡ يُحَيِّكَ بِهِ ٱللَّهُ وَيَقُولُونَ فِيٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ لَوۡلَا يُعَذِّبُنَا ٱللَّهُ بِمَا نَقُولُۚ حَسۡبُهُمۡ جَهَنَّمُ يَصۡلَوۡنَهَاۖ فَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
58:8.en: Hast thou not observed those who were forbidden conspiracy and afterward returned to that which they had been forbidden, and (now) conspire together for crime and wrongdoing and disobedience toward the messenger? And when they come unto thee they greet thee with a greeting wherewith Allah greeteth thee not, and say within themselves: Why should Allah punish us for what we say? Hell will suffice them; they will feel the heat thereof - a hapless journey's end

58:9.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِذَا تَنَٰجَيۡتُمۡ فَلَا تَتَنَٰجَوۡاْ بِٱلۡإِثۡمِ وَٱلۡعُدۡوَٰنِ وَمَعۡصِيَتِ ٱلرَّسُولِ وَتَنَٰجَوۡاْ بِٱلۡبِرِّ وَٱلتَّقۡوَىٰۖ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ ٱلَّذِيٓ إِلَيۡهِ تُحۡشَرُونَ
58:9.en: O ye who believe! When ye conspire together, conspire not together for crime and wrongdoing and disobedience toward the messenger, but conspire together for righteousness and piety, and keep your duty toward Allah, unto whom ye will be gathered

58:10.ar: إِنَّمَا ٱلنَّجۡوَىٰ مِنَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِ لِيَحۡزُنَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَلَيۡسَ بِضَآرِّهِمۡ شَيۡـًٔا إِلَّا بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِۚ وَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَلۡيَتَوَكَّلِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ
58:10.en: Lo! Conspiracy is only of the devil, that he may vex those who believe; but he can harm them not at all unless by Allah's leave. In Allah let believers put their trust

58:11.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِذَا قِيلَ لَكُمۡ تَفَسَّحُواْ فِي ٱلۡمَجَٰلِسِ فَٱفۡسَحُواْ يَفۡسَحِ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡۖ وَإِذَا قِيلَ ٱنشُزُواْ فَٱنشُزُواْ يَرۡفَعِ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مِنكُمۡ وَٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡعِلۡمَ دَرَجَٰتࣲۚ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ خَبِيرࣱ‏
58:11.en: O ye who believe! when it is said unto you, Make room! in assemblies, then make room; Allah will make way for you (hereafter). And when it is said, Come up higher! go up higher; Allah will exalt those who believe among you, and those who have knowledge, to high ranks. Allah is Informed of what ye do

58:12.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِذَا نَٰجَيۡتُمُ ٱلرَّسُولَ فَقَدِّمُواْ بَيۡنَ يَدَيۡ نَجۡوَىٰكُمۡ صَدَقَةࣰۚ ذَٰلِكَ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡ وَأَطۡهَرُۚ فَإِن لَّمۡ تَجِدُواْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمٌ
58:12.en: O ye who believe! When ye hold conference with the messenger, offer an alms before your conference. That is better and purer for you. But if ye cannot find (the wherewithal) then lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

58:13.ar: ءَأَشۡفَقۡتُمۡ أَن تُقَدِّمُواْ بَيۡنَ يَدَيۡ نَجۡوَىٰكُمۡ صَدَقَٰتࣲۚ فَإِذۡ لَمۡ تَفۡعَلُواْ وَتَابَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ فَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُواْ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَأَطِيعُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥۚ وَٱللَّهُ خَبِيرُۢ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ
58:13.en: Fear ye to offer alms before your conference? Then, when ye do it not and Allah hath forgiven you, establish worship and pay the poor-due and obey Allah and His messenger. And Allah is Aware of what ye do

58:14.ar: ۞أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ تَوَلَّوۡاْ قَوۡمًا غَضِبَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِم مَّا هُم مِّنكُمۡ وَلَا مِنۡهُمۡ وَيَحۡلِفُونَ عَلَى ٱلۡكَذِبِ وَهُمۡ يَعۡلَمُونَ
58:14.en: Hast thou not seen those who take for friends a folk with whom Allah is wroth? They are neither of you nor of them, and they swear a false oath knowingly

58:15.ar: أَعَدَّ ٱللَّهُ لَهُمۡ عَذَابࣰ ا شَدِيدًاۖ إِنَّهُمۡ سَآءَ مَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
58:15.en: Allah hath prepared for them a dreadful doom. Evil indeed is that which they are wont to do

58:16.ar: ٱتَّخَذُوٓاْ أَيۡمَٰنَهُمۡ جُنَّةࣰ فَصَدُّواْ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ فَلَهُمۡ عَذَابࣱ مُّهِينࣱ‏
58:16.en: They make a shelter of their oaths and turn (men) from the way of Allah; so theirs will be a shameful doom

58:17.ar: لَّن تُغۡنِيَ عَنۡهُمۡ أَمۡوَٰلُهُمۡ وَلَآ أَوۡلَٰدُهُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ شَيۡـًٔاۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ أَصۡحَٰبُ ٱلنَّارِۖ هُمۡ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ
58:17.en: Their wealth and their children will avail them naught against Allah. Such are rightful owners of the Fire; they will abide therein

58:18.ar: يَوۡمَ يَبۡعَثُهُمُ ٱللَّهُ جَمِيعࣰ ا فَيَحۡلِفُونَ لَهُۥ كَمَا يَحۡلِفُونَ لَكُمۡ وَيَحۡسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمۡ عَلَىٰ شَيۡءٍۚ أَلَآ إِنَّهُمۡ هُمُ ٱلۡكَٰذِبُونَ
58:18.en: On the day when Allah will raise them all together, then will they swear unto Him as they (now) swear unto you, and they will fancy that they have some standing. Lo! is it not they who are the liars

58:19.ar: ٱسۡتَحۡوَذَ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ فَأَنسَىٰهُمۡ ذِكۡرَ ٱللَّهِۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ حِزۡبُ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِۚ أَلَآ إِنَّ حِزۡبَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِ هُمُ ٱلۡخَٰسِرُونَ
58:19.en: The devil hath engrossed them and so hath caused them to forget remembrance of Allah. They are the devil's party. Lo! is it not the devil's party who will be the losers

58:20.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُحَآدُّونَ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥٓ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ فِي ٱلۡأَذَلِّينَ
58:20.en: Lo! those who oppose Allah and His messenger, they will be among the lowest

58:21.ar: كَتَبَ ٱللَّهُ لَأَغۡلِبَنَّ أَنَا۠ وَرُسُلِيٓۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَوِيٌّ عَزِيزࣱ‏
58:21.en: Allah hath decreed: Lo! I verily shall conquer, I and My messengers. Lo! Allah is Strong, Almighty

58:22.ar: لَّا تَجِدُ قَوۡمࣰ ا يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِ يُوَآدُّونَ مَنۡ حَآدَّ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ وَلَوۡ كَانُوٓاْ ءَابَآءَهُمۡ أَوۡ أَبۡنَآءَهُمۡ أَوۡ إِخۡوَٰنَهُمۡ أَوۡ عَشِيرَتَهُمۡۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ كَتَبَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ ٱلۡإِيمَٰنَ وَأَيَّدَهُم بِرُوحࣲ مِّنۡهُۖ وَيُدۡخِلُهُمۡ جَنَّٰتࣲ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَاۚ رَضِيَ ٱللَّهُ عَنۡهُمۡ وَرَضُواْ عَنۡهُۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ حِزۡبُ ٱللَّهِۚ أَلَآ إِنَّ حِزۡبَ ٱللَّهِ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ
58:22.en: Thou wilt not find folk who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His messenger, even though they be their fathers or their sons or their brethren or their clan. As for such, He hath written faith upon their hearts and hath strengthened them with a Spirit from Him, and He will bring them into Gardens underneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide. Allah is well pleased with them, and they are well pleased with Him. They are Allah's party. Lo! is it not Allah's party who are the successful

ucDGF5XgqQM.title: Surat Al-Mujadilah Summary
ucDGF5XgqQM.one_line: Opening the Juz 28 cluster, Al-Mujadilah organizes relations among Muslims: ending zihar, secret councils, exclusion and misplaced loyalty.
ucDGF5XgqQM.summary: He starts a new cluster: the Medinan surahs of Juz 28, which organize Muslim society, covering spouses, gatherings, leaders, allies, enemies and unity. Al-Mujadilah deals with relations among Muslims. It opens with Khawlah, whose husband declared zihar, saying she was to him like his mother, a pre-Islamic trick that left a wife neither married nor divorced. She argued her case with the Prophet, Allah heard her, and the ruling abolished the practice and imposed an expiation. The first habit removed from the new society was the oppression of wives. Allah counts every deed even when people forget, and is the fourth of any three who talk in secret. Drawing on long experience, he calls secret councils the surest way to ruin a community: side meetings breed sin, alliances and hatred, and leave others feeling excluded. Private talk should be about good, and criticism belongs in the open meeting. Making room in gatherings means every Muslim has a place, whatever their background. Giving charity before a private consultation with the Prophet protected his time and funded society, a better model than constant fundraising. The surah ends by placing loyalty first with Muslims, warning against lying to oneself and then to Allah, and denying support to those who fight Allah and His Messenger, even close kin.

outline.heading: The Qaf to Al-Hadid cluster recapped
outline.gist: A run through the comparisons: purpose, guidance, knowledge, blessings, the three groups, and the balance between spirit and matter.

outline.heading: Juz 28: organizing Muslim society
outline.gist: These Medinan surahs organize relations with one another, non-Muslims, allies, enemies, spouses, families and leaders.

outline.heading: Al-Mujadilah: relations among Muslims
outline.gist: The surah removes pre-Islamic habits that cause oppression and hatred and sets priorities straight.

outline.heading: Khawlah and the practice of zihar
outline.gist: Her husband said she was to him like his mother, meaning no marital relations.

outline.heading: Zihar as a tool to oppress wives
outline.gist: It left a woman neither married nor divorced; Khawlah knew it could not stand in Islam and went to the Prophet.

outline.heading: She disputed, and Allah heard
outline.gist: She argued with the Prophet instead of waiting, and Allah heard the exchange and sent the ruling.

outline.heading: The expiation and the end of the first bad habit
outline.gist: Zihar became a sin requiring expiation; the oppression of wives in their homes was the first habit removed.

outline.heading: Allah counted it though they forgot
outline.gist: Everything is recorded in detail, including what we have forgotten.

outline.heading: No three confer but He is the fourth
outline.gist: Nothing said in secret is hidden from Allah; the verses turn to secret councils.

outline.heading: Secret councils ruin communities
outline.gist: If you want to destroy relationships, progress or a community, break off into side meetings after the general one.

outline.heading: Confer in righteousness; raise concerns openly
outline.gist: Private talk should be about good, and anything negative belongs in the larger meeting.

outline.heading: Secret talk wounds those left out
outline.gist: Cliques at school and work make others feel excluded and targeted; that is why it is sinful.

outline.heading: Interlude
Make room in gatherings
outline.gist: When asked to make space, do so for anyone, whatever their family, city, lineage or class.

outline.heading: Every Muslim has a place
outline.gist: Islam ended the practice of elders deciding who may enter; everyone's input is valuable.

outline.heading: Respecting the leader's time
outline.gist: Everyone wanted private time with the Prophet, and he was too kind to refuse, which exhausted him.

outline.heading: Charity before private consultation
outline.gist: Giving charity before a private talk reduced demands on the Prophet and brought wealth into society.

outline.heading: A better way to fund the community
outline.gist: Built-in giving instead of constant appeals that tire people and finish nothing.

outline.heading: Allying with those who are not of you
outline.gist: The verses criticize those who seek alliances with people under Allah's wrath.

outline.heading: Your alliances begin with Muslims
outline.gist: Your friendships, spending and direction should strengthen the Muslim community first.

outline.heading: Lying to yourself, then to Allah
outline.gist: Some lie to themselves until they believe it and will swear falsely before Allah.

outline.heading: No loyalty to those who fight Allah, even kin
outline.gist: Believers do not support those at war with Allah and His Messenger, even fathers, sons or brothers; he recaps the surah's rules.

themes.label: Community building, cooperation and the ummah
themes.note: The surah organizes relations among Muslims so the new society avoids oppression, hatred and division.

themes.label: Marriage and the relationship between spouses
themes.note: Zihar abolished as a way of oppressing wives.

themes.label: Justice and refusing oppression
themes.note: Khawlah's courage in pressing for justice in her own home.

themes.label: Accountability before Allah and goals
themes.note: Allah has counted what people forget.

themes.label: Brotherhood, companionship and friendship
themes.note: Secret councils breed hatred and leave others feeling targeted.

themes.label: Human equality and racism
themes.note: Every Muslim has a place in the gathering regardless of lineage or status.

themes.label: Leadership, governance and institutions

maxims: If you want to ruin a community, hold secret councils.

56:2.en: There is no denying that it will befall

56:4.en: When the earth is shaken with a shock

56:5.en: And the hills are ground to powder

56:6.en: So that they become a scattered dust

56:7.en: And ye will be three kinds

56:8.en: (First) those on the right hand; what of those on the right hand

56:9.en: And (then) those on the left hand; what of those on the left hand

56:10.en: And the foremost in the race, the foremost in the race

56:11.en: Those are they who will be brought nigh

56:13.en: A multitude of those of old

56:14.en: And a few of those of later time

56:17.en: There wait on them immortal youths

56:18.en: With bowls and ewers and a cup from a pure spring

56:19.en: Wherefrom they get no aching of the head nor any madness

56:21.en: And flesh of fowls that they desire

56:22.en: And (there are) fair ones with wide, lovely eyes

56:24.en: Reward for what they used to do

56:25.ar: لَا يَسۡمَعُونَ فِيهَا لَغۡوࣰ ا وَلَا تَأۡثِيمًا
56:25.en: There hear they no vain speaking nor recrimination

56:26.ar: إِلَّا قِيلࣰ ا سَلَٰمࣰ ا سَلَٰمࣰ ا
56:26.en: (Naught) but the saying: Peace, (and again) Peace

56:27.en: And those on the right hand; what of those on the right hand

56:33.en: Neither out of reach nor yet forbidden

56:35.en: Lo! We have created them a (new) creation

56:38.en: For those on the right hand

56:39.en: A multitude of those of old

56:40.en: And a multitude of those of later time

56:41.en: And those on the left hand: What of those on the left hand

56:42.en: In scorching wind and scalding water

56:45.en: Lo! heretofore they were effete with luxury

56:46.en: And used to persist in the awful sin

56:47.ar: وَكَانُواْ يَقُولُونَ أَئِذَا مِتۡنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَابࣰ ا وَعِظَٰمًا أَءِنَّا لَمَبۡعُوثُونَ
56:47.en: And they used to say: When we are dead and have become dust and bones, shall we then, forsooth, be raised again

56:49.en: Say (unto them, O Muhammad): Lo! those of old and those of later time

56:50.en: Will all be brought together to the tryst of an appointed day

56:51.en: Then lo! ye, the erring, the deniers

56:52.en: Ye verily will eat of a tree called Zaqqum

56:53.en: And will fill your bellies therewith

56:54.en: And thereon ye will drink of boiling water

56:55.en: Drinking even as the camel drinketh

56:56.en: This will be their welcome on the Day of Judgment

56:57.en: We created you. Will ye then admit the truth

56:58.en: Have ye seen that which ye emit

56:59.en: Do ye create it or are We the Creator

56:60.ar: نَحۡنُ قَدَّرۡنَا بَيۡنَكُمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتَ وَمَا نَحۡنُ بِمَسۡبُوقِينَ
56:60.en: We mete out death among you, and We are not to be outrun

56:61.ar: عَلَىٰٓ أَن نُّبَدِّلَ أَمۡثَٰلَكُمۡ وَنُنشِئَكُمۡ فِي مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
56:61.en: That We may transfigure you and make you what ye know not

56:62.ar: وَلَقَدۡ عَلِمۡتُمُ ٱلنَّشۡأَةَ ٱلۡأُولَىٰ فَلَوۡلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ
56:62.en: And verily ye know the first creation. Why, then, do ye not reflect

56:63.en: Have ye seen that which ye cultivate

56:64.en: Is it ye who foster it, or are We the Fosterer

56:65.ar: لَوۡ نَشَآءُ لَجَعَلۡنَٰهُ حُطَٰمࣰ ا فَظَلۡتُمۡ تَفَكَّهُونَ
56:65.en: If We willed, We verily could make it chaff, then would ye cease not to exclaim

56:66.en: Lo! we are laden with debt

56:68.en: Have ye observed the water which ye drink

56:69.ar: ءَأَنتُمۡ أَنزَلۡتُمُوهُ مِنَ ٱلۡمُزۡنِ أَمۡ نَحۡنُ ٱلۡمُنزِلُونَ
56:69.en: Is it ye who shed it from the raincloud, or are We the Shedder

56:70.ar: لَوۡ نَشَآءُ جَعَلۡنَٰهُ أُجَاجࣰ ا فَلَوۡلَا تَشۡكُرُونَ
56:70.en: If We willed We verily could make it bitter. Why then, give ye not thanks

56:71.en: Have ye observed the fire which ye strike out

56:72.ar: ءَأَنتُمۡ أَنشَأۡتُمۡ شَجَرَتَهَآ أَمۡ نَحۡنُ ٱلۡمُنشِـُٔونَ
56:72.en: Was it ye who made the tree thereof to grow, or were We the grower

56:73.ar: نَحۡنُ جَعَلۡنَٰهَا تَذۡكِرَةࣰ وَمَتَٰعࣰ ا لِّلۡمُقۡوِينَ
56:73.en: We, even We, appointed it a memorial and a comfort for the dwellers in the wilderness

56:74.en: Therefor (O Muhammad), praise the name of thy Lord, the Tremendous

56:75.en: Nay, I swear by the places of the stars

56:76.en: And lo! that verily is a tremendous oath, if ye but knew

56:77.en: That (this) is indeed a noble Qur'an

56:79.en: Which none toucheth save the purified

56:80.en: A revelation from the Lord of the Worlds

56:81.en: Is it this Statement that ye scorn

56:82.en: And make denial thereof your livelihood

56:83.en: Why, then, when (the soul) cometh up to the throat (of the dying)

56:84.en: And ye are at that moment looking

56:85.ar: وَنَحۡنُ أَقۡرَبُ إِلَيۡهِ مِنكُمۡ وَلَٰكِن لَّا تُبۡصِرُونَ
56:85.en: And We are nearer unto him than ye are, but ye see not

56:86.en: Why then, if ye are not in bondage (unto Us)

56:87.en: Do ye not force it back, if ye are truthful

56:88.en: Thus if he is of those brought nigh

56:89.en: Then breath of life, and plenty, and a Garden of delight

56:90.ar: وَأَمَّآ إِن كَانَ مِنۡ أَصۡحَٰبِ ٱلۡيَمِينِ
56:90.en: And if he is of those on the right hand

56:91.en: Then (the greeting) "Peace be unto thee" from those on the right hand

56:92.ar: وَأَمَّآ إِن كَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُكَذِّبِينَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
56:92.en: But if he is of the rejecters, the erring

56:93.en: Then the welcome will be boiling water

56:96.en: Therefor (O Muhammad) praise the name of thy Lord, the Tremendous

6jZYFgoP1EM.speaker: adnan
6jZYFgoP1EM.speaker_note: his daily surah-summary series at MWN; continues the comparison cluster
6jZYFgoP1EM.title: Surat Al-Waqi'ah Summary
6jZYFgoP1EM.one_line: Al-Waqi'ah replaces worldly status with Allah's criteria, sorting people into three groups, and points to belief, the Quran and death as the way.
6jZYFgoP1EM.summary: He notes that Al-Waqi'ah is much loved and widely recited, though popular claims about it have little evidence. Its comparison is about status. In this world people get a status score from wealth, degrees, profession, family name and even skin colour, and society sorts itself by class. When the Event befalls, it lowers some and raises others by a different standard: good deeds, nearness to Allah, values and worship. That is a comfort for those who had few opportunities in life. People will be in three groups: the foremost, the people of the right and the people of the left. The foremost are many from the early generations and few from the later ones, so reaching that rank today takes extra effort. He describes the delights of the first two groups and notes that two of the three groups succeed. The people of the left are there for three reasons: extravagant consumption, refusing to give to the needy, and clinging to the great lie of shirk and denial of resurrection. The last part of the surah gives the path: certainty about Allah through arguments about seed, crops, water and fire; honouring the Quran; and remembering death, which no one can turn back. He asks listeners to keep these three in front of them and aim for the first two groups.

outline.heading: A beloved surah and the myths around it
outline.gist: Part of the comparison cluster; widely recited, though popular claims about its benefits have little evidence.

outline.heading: When the Event befalls
outline.gist: Waqi'ah means something coming into reality: the Day of Judgment, which nothing can hold back.

outline.heading: How the world ranks people
outline.gist: Wealth, degrees, profession, family name and even skin colour give each person a status score and a class.

outline.heading: Abasing some, raising others
outline.gist: On that day worldly status does not carry over; rank depends on deeds, nearness to Allah, values and worship, a comfort for those denied opportunities.

outline.heading: Three groups: right, left and foremost
outline.gist: The words sound like a political race, but the criteria behind them are entirely different.

outline.heading: The foremost: many from the early, few from the later
outline.gist: Those brought nearest to Allah are mostly from earlier generations, so reaching that rank in our time takes extra effort.

outline.heading: The delights of the foremost
outline.gist: Couches, cups that do not intoxicate, fruit and meat, and nothing heard but peace.

outline.heading: The people of the right
outline.gist: Thornless lote trees, layered banana trees and fruit that is never forbidden.

outline.heading: Two of the three groups succeed
outline.gist: Only one group fares badly, which gives every listener reason for hope.

outline.heading: A large group from both eras; the people of the left
outline.gist: The people of the right come from early and later generations alike; then scorching wind, scalding water and black smoke.

outline.heading: Why the left are there
outline.gist: Extravagant consumption while others suffered, withholding the right of the needy, and persisting in the great lie of shirk and denial of resurrection.

outline.heading: Interlude
Comparison needs contrast
outline.gist: The harsh description of the third group sharpens the comparison; there are also differences between the first two groups for those who look.

outline.heading: Three keys, beginning with belief: the seed you emit
outline.gist: After the comparison the surah points to belief, the Quran and death; what part do you play in turning a drop into a person?

outline.heading: Crops, water and fire
outline.gist: You plant a seed but do not make it grow; you do not send the rain or understand how fire burns.

outline.heading: Certainty first
outline.gist: These arguments build certainty; without it nothing works, and life will expose the smallest doubt.

outline.heading: A noble Quran touched only by the pure
outline.gist: The oath by the positions of the stars; will you make denial your share of provision?

outline.heading: The soul at the throat
outline.gist: Return the soul if you can; belief, the Quran and death are the three things to keep before you.

outline.heading: Each group at death
outline.gist: The nearest go to rest and gardens of bliss, the people of the right send peace, the deniers go to scalding water and fire.

outline.heading: The certain truth: glorify your Lord
outline.gist: This is the highest certainty; glorify the name of your Lord so you may land in one of the first two groups.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: The three groups on the Day of Judgment and what each receives.

themes.label: Human equality and racism
themes.note: Worldly status from wealth, class and skin colour counts for nothing when the Event comes.

themes.label: Wealth, asceticism (zuhd), consumerism and money
themes.note: Extravagant consumption and withholding from the needy put people among those on the left.

themes.label: Eman: faith, certainty, doubt
themes.note: Arguments from creation build the certainty without which nothing works.

themes.label: Relationship with the Quran: reading, reflecting, living it
themes.note: The Quran is noble and preserved; do not trade it away.

themes.label: Mortality, death and preparing for it
themes.note: Death is near and cannot be reversed, so be ready.

hadith.gist: Reports of special benefits from reciting Al-Waqi'ah, such as protection from poverty, which he says have little evidence

maxims: Whatever status you built in the dunya won't carry over.
Life will expose the smallest doubt in your heart.
Belief, Quran, death: keep them on your billboard.
contemporary: Socioeconomic status and class as the way modern society ranks people
takeaways: Measure yourself by deeds, values and closeness to Allah, not worldly status.
Put in extra effort to be among the foremost, who are few in later times.
Avoid extravagance and give the needy their right from your wealth.
Build certainty in Allah, honour the Quran and stay ready for death.

49:1.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تُقَدِّمُواْ بَيۡنَ يَدَيِ ٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦۖ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمࣱ‏
49:1.en: O ye who believe! Be not forward in the presence of Allah and His messenger, and keep your duty to Allah. Lo! Allah is Hearer, Knower

49:2.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَرۡفَعُوٓاْ أَصۡوَٰتَكُمۡ فَوۡقَ صَوۡتِ ٱلنَّبِيِّ وَلَا تَجۡهَرُواْ لَهُۥ بِٱلۡقَوۡلِ كَجَهۡرِ بَعۡضِكُمۡ لِبَعۡضٍ أَن تَحۡبَطَ أَعۡمَٰلُكُمۡ وَأَنتُمۡ لَا تَشۡعُرُونَ
49:2.en: O ye who believe! Lift not up your voices above the voice of the Prophet, nor shout when speaking to him as ye shout one to another, lest your works be rendered vain while ye perceive not

49:3.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَغُضُّونَ أَصۡوَٰتَهُمۡ عِندَ رَسُولِ ٱللَّهِ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱمۡتَحَنَ ٱللَّهُ قُلُوبَهُمۡ لِلتَّقۡوَىٰۚ لَهُم مَّغۡفِرَةࣱ وَأَجۡرٌ عَظِيمٌ
49:3.en: Lo! they who subdue their voices in the presence of the messenger of Allah, those are they whose hearts Allah hath proven unto righteousness. Theirs will be forgiveness and immense reward

49:4.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُنَادُونَكَ مِن وَرَآءِ ٱلۡحُجُرَٰتِ أَكۡثَرُهُمۡ لَا يَعۡقِلُونَ
49:4.en: Lo! those who call thee from behind the private apartments, most of them have no sense

49:5.ar: وَلَوۡ أَنَّهُمۡ صَبَرُواْ حَتَّىٰ تَخۡرُجَ إِلَيۡهِمۡ لَكَانَ خَيۡرࣰ ا لَّهُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
49:5.en: And if they had had patience till thou camest forth unto them, it had been better for them. And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

49:6.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِن جَآءَكُمۡ فَاسِقُۢ بِنَبَإࣲ فَتَبَيَّنُوٓاْ أَن تُصِيبُواْ قَوۡمَۢا بِجَهَٰلَةࣲ فَتُصۡبِحُواْ عَلَىٰ مَا فَعَلۡتُمۡ نَٰدِمِينَ
49:6.en: O ye who believe! If an evil-liver bring you tidings, verify it, lest ye smite some folk in ignorance and afterward repent of what ye did

49:7.ar: وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ فِيكُمۡ رَسُولَ ٱللَّهِۚ لَوۡ يُطِيعُكُمۡ فِي كَثِيرࣲ مِّنَ ٱلۡأَمۡرِ لَعَنِتُّمۡ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ حَبَّبَ إِلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡإِيمَٰنَ وَزَيَّنَهُۥ فِي قُلُوبِكُمۡ وَكَرَّهَ إِلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡكُفۡرَ وَٱلۡفُسُوقَ وَٱلۡعِصۡيَانَۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلرَّٰشِدُونَ
49:7.en: And know that the messenger of Allah is among you. If he were to obey you in much of the government, ye would surely be in trouble; but Allah hath endeared the faith to you and hath beautified it in your hearts, and hath made disbelief and lewdness and rebellion hateful unto you. Such are they who are the rightly guided

49:8.ar: فَضۡلࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَنِعۡمَةࣰۚ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمࣱ‏
49:8.en: (It is) a bounty and a grace from Allah; and Allah is Knower, Wise

49:9.ar: وَإِن طَآئِفَتَانِ مِنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ ٱقۡتَتَلُواْ فَأَصۡلِحُواْ بَيۡنَهُمَاۖ فَإِنۢ بَغَتۡ إِحۡدَىٰهُمَا عَلَى ٱلۡأُخۡرَىٰ فَقَٰتِلُواْ ٱلَّتِي تَبۡغِي حَتَّىٰ تَفِيٓءَ إِلَىٰٓ أَمۡرِ ٱللَّهِۚ فَإِن فَآءَتۡ فَأَصۡلِحُواْ بَيۡنَهُمَا بِٱلۡعَدۡلِ وَأَقۡسِطُوٓاْۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُقۡسِطِينَ
49:9.en: And if two parties of believers fall to fighting, then make peace between them. And if one party of them doeth wrong to the other, fight ye that which doeth wrong till it return unto the ordinance of Allah; then, if it return, make peace between them justly, and act equitably. Lo! Allah loveth the equitable

49:10.ar: إِنَّمَا ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ إِخۡوَةࣱ فَأَصۡلِحُواْ بَيۡنَ أَخَوَيۡكُمۡۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تُرۡحَمُونَ
49:10.en: The believers are naught else than brothers. Therefore make peace between your brethren and observe your duty to Allah that haply ye may obtain mercy

49:11.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا يَسۡخَرۡ قَوۡمࣱ مِّن قَوۡمٍ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَكُونُواْ خَيۡرࣰ ا مِّنۡهُمۡ وَلَا نِسَآءࣱ مِّن نِّسَآءٍ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَكُنَّ خَيۡرࣰ ا مِّنۡهُنَّۖ وَلَا تَلۡمِزُوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۡ وَلَا تَنَابَزُواْ بِٱلۡأَلۡقَٰبِۖ بِئۡسَ ٱلِٱسۡمُ ٱلۡفُسُوقُ بَعۡدَ ٱلۡإِيمَٰنِۚ وَمَن لَّمۡ يَتُبۡ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ
49:11.en: O ye who believe! Let not a folk deride a folk who may be better than they (are), not let women (deride) women who may be better than they are; neither defame one another, nor insult one another by nicknames. Bad is the name of lewdness after faith. And whoso turneth not in repentance, such are evil-doers

49:12.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱجۡتَنِبُواْ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلظَّنِّ إِنَّ بَعۡضَ ٱلظَّنِّ إِثۡمࣱۖ وَلَا تَجَسَّسُواْ وَلَا يَغۡتَب بَّعۡضُكُم بَعۡضًاۚ أَيُحِبُّ أَحَدُكُمۡ أَن يَأۡكُلَ لَحۡمَ أَخِيهِ مَيۡتࣰ ا فَكَرِهۡتُمُوهُۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ تَوَّابࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
49:12.en: O ye who believe! Shun much suspicion; for lo! some suspicion is a crime. And spy not, neither backbite one another. Would one of you love to eat the flesh of his dead brother? Ye abhor that (so abhor the other)! And keep your duty (to Allah). Lo! Allah is Relenting, Merciful

49:13.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّا خَلَقۡنَٰكُم مِّن ذَكَرࣲ وَأُنثَىٰ وَجَعَلۡنَٰكُمۡ شُعُوبࣰ ا وَقَبَآئِلَ لِتَعَارَفُوٓاْۚ إِنَّ أَكۡرَمَكُمۡ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ أَتۡقَىٰكُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرࣱ‏
49:13.en: O mankind! Lo! We have created you male and female, and have made you nations and tribes that ye may know one another. Lo! the noblest of you, in the sight of Allah, is the best in conduct. Lo! Allah is Knower, Aware

49:14.ar: ۞قَالَتِ ٱلۡأَعۡرَابُ ءَامَنَّاۖ قُل لَّمۡ تُؤۡمِنُواْ وَلَٰكِن قُولُوٓاْ أَسۡلَمۡنَا وَلَمَّا يَدۡخُلِ ٱلۡإِيمَٰنُ فِي قُلُوبِكُمۡۖ وَإِن تُطِيعُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ لَا يَلِتۡكُم مِّنۡ أَعۡمَٰلِكُمۡ شَيۡـًٔاۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمٌ
49:14.en: The wandering Arabs say: We believe. Say (unto them, O Muhammad): Ye believe not, but rather say "We submit," for the faith hath not yet entered into your hearts. Yet, if ye obey Allah and His messenger, He will not withhold from you aught of (the reward of) your deeds. Lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

49:15.ar: إِنَّمَا ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ ثُمَّ لَمۡ يَرۡتَابُواْ وَجَٰهَدُواْ بِأَمۡوَٰلِهِمۡ وَأَنفُسِهِمۡ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلصَّٰدِقُونَ
49:15.en: The (true) believers are those only who believe in Allah and His messenger and afterward doubt not, but strive with their wealth and their lives for the cause of Allah. Such are the sincere

49:16.ar: قُلۡ أَتُعَلِّمُونَ ٱللَّهَ بِدِينِكُمۡ وَٱللَّهُ يَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ وَٱللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءٍ عَلِيمࣱ‏
49:16.en: Say (unto them, O Muhammad): Would ye teach Allah your religion, when Allah knoweth all that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth, and Allah is Aware of all things

49:17.ar: يَمُنُّونَ عَلَيۡكَ أَنۡ أَسۡلَمُواْۖ قُل لَّا تَمُنُّواْ عَلَيَّ إِسۡلَٰمَكُمۖ بَلِ ٱللَّهُ يَمُنُّ عَلَيۡكُمۡ أَنۡ هَدَىٰكُمۡ لِلۡإِيمَٰنِ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
49:17.en: They make it a favour unto thee (Muhammad) that they have surrendered (unto Him). Say: Deem not your Surrender a favour unto me; but Allah doth confer a favour on you, inasmuch as He hath led you to the Faith, if ye are earnest

49:18.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعۡلَمُ غَيۡبَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ وَٱللَّهُ بَصِيرُۢ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ
49:18.en: Lo! Allah knoweth the Unseen of the heavens and the earth. And Allah is Seer of what ye do

2ORFNbmZIJY.speaker: adnan
2ORFNbmZIJY.speaker_note: his own surah-summary series; English explanation followed by an Arabic summary
2ORFNbmZIJY.title: Surat Al-Hujurat Summary
2ORFNbmZIJY.one_line: Al-Hujurat distils the Prophet's adab: nothing before Allah and His Messenger, respect, verifying news, reconciling, social manners and an anthem against racism.
2ORFNbmZIJY.summary: Al-Hujurat closes the cluster on the Prophet. Surat Muhammad made following him the measure of accepted deeds and Al-Fath showed those who followed; Al-Hujurat gives the adab he brought and how to deal with him. For its two and a half pages it is perhaps the densest surah in commands. The first and most important: put nothing before Allah and His Messenger; in any matter, first ask what the shari'ah says, something increasingly ignored today. Do not raise your voice above his; as with parents, disrespect lowers the one who shows it, and it can void deeds unnoticed. The bedouins calling from behind his chambers teach privacy and asking permission. Then the adab of news: verify before acting or changing your heart toward someone, and if you cannot verify, refuse to listen. The Messenger is among us through the values and manners he left. When believers fight, reconciling them is a duty because believers are brothers. Social manners follow: no mockery meant to belittle, no hidden digs or hurtful nicknames, avoid suspicion, spying and backbiting. Verse 13 is the Quran's anthem against racism: diversity of peoples is a beauty meant for mutual knowing, and honour is only by taqwa, yet racism persists even within villages and families. The surah ends warning against treating one's Islam as a favour to Allah.

outline.heading: Opening
Do not put yourselves before Allah and His Messenger
outline.gist: In any matter in life, what Allah and the Prophet say comes first.

outline.heading: Disregarding the Prophet's guidance is being normalised
outline.gist: Choosing what we like over what he taught was once frowned upon; today it is increasingly normal.

outline.heading: Do not raise your voices above the Prophet's
outline.gist: Those who lower their voices have hearts tested for taqwa; loudness can void deeds unnoticed.

outline.heading: Respect reflects on you, as with parents
outline.gist: Publicly disrespecting a parent lowers the child, not the parent; respecting the Prophet builds our own manners.

outline.heading: Calling out from behind the chambers
outline.gist: Had they waited for him to come out it would have been better for them.

outline.heading: The cluster's close: the Prophet's adab
outline.gist: Muhammad gave following him as the measure of deeds, Al-Fath the examples of followers, and Al-Hujurat the manners he brought.

outline.heading: The densest surah in commands
outline.gist: Al-Ma'idah has more but is far longer; every command here is a matter of adab worth learning.

outline.heading: First ask what the shari'ah says
outline.gist: Never place Allah's word or the Prophet's after another idea; perhaps the most important command in the surah.

outline.heading: Abu Bakr and Umar raise their voices
outline.gist: The two best nearly perished when they argued loudly before him; the Prophet does not need our respect, it is for our sake.

outline.heading: Privacy and asking permission
outline.gist: Bedouins woke him at midday calling his name; knock, wait and leave if not answered, and respect elders, scholars and teachers.

outline.heading: Bad manners is not following him
outline.gist: After two surahs on following, this one gives its substance; the Prophet was all adab.

outline.heading: Verify news before you act
outline.gist: Before acting, taking a stand or changing your heart toward a person over something you heard, make sure it is true, or you will regret it.

outline.heading: Allah made faith beloved to you
outline.gist: If the Prophet followed you in many matters you would suffer; faith was beautified in your hearts.

outline.heading: Reconcile two fighting groups of believers
outline.gist: Believers are brothers, so disputes between them must be resolved by others.

outline.heading: Mockery, suspicion, spying and backbiting
outline.gist: The surah lists the social sins that damage brotherhood, ending with eating a dead brother's flesh.

outline.heading: If you cannot verify it, do not listen
outline.gist: No time to check is no excuse to act on a report; refuse to hear it instead.

outline.heading: The Messenger is among us through his values
outline.gist: Literally among the companions, he is among us through the manners he left; without them what have we taken from him?

outline.heading: Reconciling is your business
outline.gist: People in conflict cannot fix it themselves; a Muslim cannot walk away saying it is not his concern.

outline.heading: No mockery, hidden digs or hurtful nicknames
outline.gist: Not friendly banter but ridicule meant to lower someone; he asks women too to watch this when speaking of each other.

outline.heading: Good opinion, no spying, no backbiting
outline.gist: Suspicion gains you nothing and good opinion is worship, except in decisive matters like marriage or trade.

outline.heading: Peoples and tribes made to know one another
outline.gist: Diversity of cultures and nations is to be celebrated; Islam does not make everyone look the same.

outline.heading: The noblest is the most mindful of Allah
outline.gist: After adab with Allah, the Prophet, news, disputes and society comes adab with all of humanity.

outline.heading: The Quran's anthem against racism
outline.gist: All humans come from one male and female; differences of colour, language and custom are beauty, not grounds for superiority.

outline.heading: Racism in our own lands and families
outline.gist: Hateful racism persists even within one village, city or family, contradicting all the Prophet brought.

outline.heading: Do not count your Islam as a favour to Allah
outline.gist: The bedouins said they believed when they had only submitted; it is Allah who favours you by guiding you.

outline.heading: Outro

2Y0s35yPbcs.title: Surah Al-Alaq Summary
2Y0s35yPbcs.one_line: Iqra as Islam's founding principle of learning, and five traits that make a person compatible with Islam: humility, empathy, open-mindedness, objectivity, accepting truth.
2Y0s35yPbcs.summary: On a Ramadan night like the one of the first revelation, he retells Jibreel's arrival at Hira and argues that iqra is far broader than reading script: it means learn, reflect, take the expertise of others and read your own reality. Knowledge appears six times in five verses, so the deen is built on learning, and the Prophet himself stayed unlettered, proving literacy was never the point. He laments an ummah that does not read even its own history, repeating the same institutional fights in every city, and that does not understand a Quran preserved in a living language. The following verses he calls compatibility verses, explaining why there are so many Muslims and so little Islam. The Quran names the traits that block Islam from working, and their opposites are what is needed: arrogance fused with oppression when one feels self-sufficient (so humility and empathy), rejecting worship because it is new (so open-mindedness, as with the trench), refusing to ask whether the other person might be right (so objectivity, taking the good from any scholar), and turning away from known truth (so accepting truth at once, as Umar did on the minbar). He ends demanding that educating ourselves and the next generation be the community's first goal.

outline.heading: Opening
The first revelation on a night like this
outline.gist: After centuries of silence since Isa, revelation came on a Ramadan night; no one knows whether it was the 27th or the 21st.

outline.heading: Jibreel in his true form and the three embraces
outline.gist: Jibreel came without warning in his created form, and each embrace felt to the Prophet like death.

outline.heading: 'I cannot read': iqra is bigger than reciting script
outline.gist: The Prophet understood a request to read writing, but the Arabic word reaches far beyond that.

outline.heading: A command beyond jurisprudence
outline.gist: Every Quranic command becomes obligatory or recommended, except this one, which carries no ruling because it is the principle that defines a Muslim.

outline.heading: What qira'ah means: learn, reflect, take expertise
outline.gist: It means to contemplate, read between the lines and gather knowledge from every direction, then fold it into who you are.

outline.heading: Six references to knowledge in five verses
outline.gist: The deen is coded to rest on knowledge, critical thinking and the experience of past, present and future people; remove knowledge and everything nosedives.

outline.heading: Knowledge saved the Companions and will save us
outline.gist: The Companions knew nothing and learned; the Prophet was above all a teacher.

outline.heading: It never meant literacy
outline.gist: The Prophet never learned to read script, which he would have done if that was the first command; learning without ego was his character.

outline.heading: An ummah that does not read its own reality
outline.gist: We do not read our history or mistakes, so every community repeats the same fights between boards, imams and institutions.

outline.heading: Embrace the command that shook the Prophet
outline.gist: Jibreel sent him running down the mountain just to say read; change starts with embracing these words.

outline.heading: Al-Akram: the first divine name revealed
outline.gist: Read anything, and the Most Generous will give; nations that prioritize education succeed even without faith.

outline.heading: A Quran in a living language we still do not understand
outline.gist: Other scriptures survive only through dead languages and translation; Muslims have theirs in a spoken language yet know little of their faith.

outline.heading: Compatibility verses: hardware for Islam
outline.gist: Like software that will not run on an old system, Islam does nothing in a person lacking certain traits.

outline.heading: So many Muslims, so little Islam
outline.gist: Where are the compassion, integrity, care for the elderly and sick, and pursuit of education? The hardware needs fixing.

outline.heading: Incompatible trait one: arrogance fused with oppression
outline.gist: The Quran names what it does not want and leaves the opposite open; tughyan combines arrogance and oppression.

outline.heading: Feeling self-sufficient; the cure is humility and empathy
outline.gist: When people feel they need no one they stop caring; the opposite is humility, especially about one's religiosity, and quick compassion.

outline.heading: Incompatible trait two: forbidding a servant to pray
outline.gist: They opposed his worship only because it was new and unfamiliar.

outline.heading: Rejecting ideas because they are new
outline.gist: 'That's not what we used to do' closed-mindedness turns Islam into inherited custom with a label on it.

outline.heading: Open-mindedness: the trench idea
outline.gist: The Prophet was open enough to consider digging a five-kilometre trench; we need empathy, humility and openness.

outline.heading: Incompatible trait three: what if he is guided?
outline.gist: Do you give the benefit of the doubt, or label and despise people you dislike?

outline.heading: Objectivity toward your own brothers and sisters
outline.gist: We expect non-Muslims to study Islam fairly but will not do the same for fellow Muslims.

outline.heading: Bring your evidence: no quick refusals
outline.gist: Muslims argue by evidence and reason; disliking someone should not make everything they touch taboo.

outline.heading: Take the good and leave the bad: trashing scholars
outline.gist: Scholars are cursed over one political stance or opinion; no one, including your favourite, is an exception to objectivity.

outline.heading: Incompatible trait four: turning away from known truth
outline.gist: Whoever sees what is right but turns away for personal reasons forgets that Allah sees him.

outline.heading: Refusing truth leads to manipulating Islam
outline.gist: If you will not change position the moment you see what is right, the distortion you bring to Islam is immeasurable.

outline.heading: Muslim by birth, transformed by nothing
outline.gist: With these problems Islam sits unused; with their opposites it mixes with your essence and transforms you.

outline.heading: The Companions' compatible traits
outline.gist: Like small plants turning into flowers, the Companions flourished because they had empathy, humility, openness, objectivity and acceptance of truth.

outline.heading: Umar accepts correction on the minbar
outline.gist: Umar conceded to a woman even though he was not actually wrong; people are like minerals, the best before Islam are the best in it with understanding.

outline.heading: Five questions to ask yourself
outline.gist: Are you compassionate, humble, open-minded, objective, and do you accept truth unconditionally? Then Islam's trajectory for you is limitless.

outline.heading: Learning is the way out of our situation
outline.gist: Muslims fail today from lack of knowledge, and will rise by educating themselves and understanding the deen properly.

outline.heading: Knowledge should be an upright triangle
outline.gist: Ignorance is a sign of the end of time; each generation should know more than the last, or our children cannot afford our ignorance.

outline.heading: Education as the community's first goal; the lying forelock
outline.gist: If time, money and resources do not go to education, enjoy it while it lasts; the forelock, the brain's processing seat, is seized when not used to learn.

outline.heading: Let him call his associates
outline.gist: No one cares whom he summons; Allah's forces are stronger, so keep walking your road.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Community building, cooperation and the ummah

themes.note: The Companions flourished because they had the compatible traits; Umar accepted correction instantly.

People are like mines of gold and silver: the best of them before Islam are the best in Islam if they gain understanding.
Among the signs of the Hour is that ignorance spreads and knowledge decreases.

Compatibility verses
Knowledge should be an upright triangle

stories.point: The first command, delivered with overwhelming force, was simply to learn.

stories.who: The trench at the Battle of the Confederates
stories.point: Being willing even to consider a radical new idea is the open-mindedness Islam needs.

stories.who: Umar ibn al-Khattab corrected on the minbar
stories.point: Accept correction instantly, even when you may not be wrong.

Scholars cursed over a single political stance or opinion
takeaways: Treat learning, reflection and reading your own history as a lifelong obligation.
Check yourself on humility, empathy, open-mindedness, objectivity and accepting truth.
Give people, including scholars you dislike, the benefit of the doubt: take the good, leave the bad.

48:1.ar: إِنَّا فَتَحۡنَا لَكَ فَتۡحࣰ ا مُّبِينࣰ ا
48:1.en: Lo! We have given thee (O Muhammad) a signal victory

48:2.ar: لِّيَغۡفِرَ لَكَ ٱللَّهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِن ذَنۢبِكَ وَمَا تَأَخَّرَ وَيُتِمَّ نِعۡمَتَهُۥ عَلَيۡكَ وَيَهۡدِيَكَ صِرَٰطࣰ ا مُّسۡتَقِيمࣰ ا
48:2.en: That Allah may forgive thee of thy sin that which is past and that which is to come, and may perfect His favour unto thee, and may guide thee on a right path

48:3.en: And that Allah may help thee with strong help

48:4.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنزَلَ ٱلسَّكِينَةَ فِي قُلُوبِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ لِيَزۡدَادُوٓاْ إِيمَٰنࣰ ا مَّعَ إِيمَٰنِهِمۡۗ وَلِلَّهِ جُنُودُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمࣰ ا
48:4.en: He it is Who sent down peace of reassurance into the hearts of the believers that they might add faith unto their faith. Allah's are the hosts of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is ever Knower, Wise

48:5.ar: لِّيُدۡخِلَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِ جَنَّٰتࣲ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا وَيُكَفِّرَ عَنۡهُمۡ سَيِّـَٔاتِهِمۡۚ وَكَانَ ذَٰلِكَ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ فَوۡزًا عَظِيمࣰ ا
48:5.en: That He may bring the believing men and the believing women into Gardens underneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide, and may remit from them their evil deeds - That, in the sight of Allah, is the supreme triumph

48:6.ar: وَيُعَذِّبَ ٱلۡمُنَٰفِقِينَ وَٱلۡمُنَٰفِقَٰتِ وَٱلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ وَٱلۡمُشۡرِكَٰتِ ٱلظَّآنِّينَ بِٱللَّهِ ظَنَّ ٱلسَّوۡءِۚ عَلَيۡهِمۡ دَآئِرَةُ ٱلسَّوۡءِۖ وَغَضِبَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَلَعَنَهُمۡ وَأَعَدَّ لَهُمۡ جَهَنَّمَۖ وَسَآءَتۡ مَصِيرࣰ ا
48:6.en: And may punish the hypocritical men and the hypocritical women, and the idolatrous men and the idolatrous women, who think an evil thought concerning Allah. For them is the evil turn of fortune, and Allah is wroth against them and hath cursed them, and hath made ready for them hell, a hapless journey's end

48:7.ar: وَلِلَّهِ جُنُودُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَزِيزًا حَكِيمًا
48:7.en: Allah's are the hosts of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is ever Mighty, Wise

48:8.ar: إِنَّآ أَرۡسَلۡنَٰكَ شَٰهِدࣰ ا وَمُبَشِّرࣰ ا وَنَذِيرࣰ ا
48:8.en: Lo! We have sent thee (O Muhammad) as a witness and a bearer of good tidings and a warner

48:9.ar: لِّتُؤۡمِنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ وَتُعَزِّرُوهُ وَتُوَقِّرُوهُۚ وَتُسَبِّحُوهُ بُكۡرَةࣰ وَأَصِيلًا
48:9.en: That ye (mankind) may believe in Allah and His messenger, and may honour Him, and may revere Him, and may glorify Him at early dawn and at the close of day

48:10.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُبَايِعُونَكَ إِنَّمَا يُبَايِعُونَ ٱللَّهَ يَدُ ٱللَّهِ فَوۡقَ أَيۡدِيهِمۡۚ فَمَن نَّكَثَ فَإِنَّمَا يَنكُثُ عَلَىٰ نَفۡسِهِۦۖ وَمَنۡ أَوۡفَىٰ بِمَا عَٰهَدَ عَلَيۡهُ ٱللَّهَ فَسَيُؤۡتِيهِ أَجۡرًا عَظِيمࣰ ا
48:10.en: Lo! those who swear allegiance unto thee (Muhammad), swear allegiance only unto Allah. The Hand of Allah is above their hands. So whosoever breaketh his oath, breaketh it only to his soul's hurt; while whosoever keepeth his covenant with Allah, on him will He bestow immense reward

48:11.ar: سَيَقُولُ لَكَ ٱلۡمُخَلَّفُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡأَعۡرَابِ شَغَلَتۡنَآ أَمۡوَٰلُنَا وَأَهۡلُونَا فَٱسۡتَغۡفِرۡ لَنَاۚ يَقُولُونَ بِأَلۡسِنَتِهِم مَّا لَيۡسَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمۡۚ قُلۡ فَمَن يَمۡلِكُ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ شَيۡـًٔا إِنۡ أَرَادَ بِكُمۡ ضَرًّا أَوۡ أَرَادَ بِكُمۡ نَفۡعَۢاۚ بَلۡ كَانَ ٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ خَبِيرَۢا
48:11.en: Those of the wandering Arabs who were left behind will tell thee: Our possessions and our households occupied us, so ask forgiveness for us! They speak with their tongues that which is not in their hearts. Say: Who can avail you aught against Allah, if He intend you hurt or intend you profit? Nay, but Allah is ever Aware of what ye do

48:12.ar: بَلۡ ظَنَنتُمۡ أَن لَّن يَنقَلِبَ ٱلرَّسُولُ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ إِلَىٰٓ أَهۡلِيهِمۡ أَبَدࣰ ا وَزُيِّنَ ذَٰلِكَ فِي قُلُوبِكُمۡ وَظَنَنتُمۡ ظَنَّ ٱلسَّوۡءِ وَكُنتُمۡ قَوۡمَۢا بُورࣰ ا
48:12.en: Nay, but ye deemed that the messenger and the believers would never return to their own folk, and that was made fairseeming in your hearts, and ye did think an evil thought, and ye were worthless folk

48:13.ar: وَمَن لَّمۡ يُؤۡمِنۢ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ فَإِنَّآ أَعۡتَدۡنَا لِلۡكَٰفِرِينَ سَعِيرࣰ ا
48:13.en: And so for him who believeth not in Allah and His messenger - Lo! We have prepared a flame for disbelievers

48:14.ar: وَلِلَّهِ مُلۡكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ يَغۡفِرُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيُعَذِّبُ مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣰ ا رَّحِيمࣰ ا
48:14.en: And Allah's is the Sovereignty of the heavens and the earth. He forgiveth whom He will, and punisheth whom He will. And Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful

48:15.ar: سَيَقُولُ ٱلۡمُخَلَّفُونَ إِذَا ٱنطَلَقۡتُمۡ إِلَىٰ مَغَانِمَ لِتَأۡخُذُوهَا ذَرُونَا نَتَّبِعۡكُمۡۖ يُرِيدُونَ أَن يُبَدِّلُواْ كَلَٰمَ ٱللَّهِۚ قُل لَّن تَتَّبِعُونَا كَذَٰلِكُمۡ قَالَ ٱللَّهُ مِن قَبۡلُۖ فَسَيَقُولُونَ بَلۡ تَحۡسُدُونَنَاۚ بَلۡ كَانُواْ لَا يَفۡقَهُونَ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣰ ا
48:15.en: Those who were left behind will say, when ye set forth to capture booty: Let us go with you. They fain would change the verdict of Allah. Say (unto them, O Muhammad): Ye shall not go with us. Thus hath Allah said beforehand. Then they will say: Ye are envious of us. Nay, but they understand not, save a little

48:16.ar: قُل لِّلۡمُخَلَّفِينَ مِنَ ٱلۡأَعۡرَابِ سَتُدۡعَوۡنَ إِلَىٰ قَوۡمٍ أُوْلِي بَأۡسࣲ شَدِيدࣲ تُقَٰتِلُونَهُمۡ أَوۡ يُسۡلِمُونَۖ فَإِن تُطِيعُواْ يُؤۡتِكُمُ ٱللَّهُ أَجۡرًا حَسَنࣰ اۖ وَإِن تَتَوَلَّوۡاْ كَمَا تَوَلَّيۡتُم مِّن قَبۡلُ يُعَذِّبۡكُمۡ عَذَابًا أَلِيمࣰ ا
48:16.en: Say unto those of the wandering Arabs who were left behind: Ye will be called against a folk of mighty prowess, to fight them until they surrender; and if ye obey, Allah will give you a fair reward; but if ye turn away as ye did turn away before, He will punish you with a painful doom

48:17.ar: لَّيۡسَ عَلَى ٱلۡأَعۡمَىٰ حَرَجࣱ وَلَا عَلَى ٱلۡأَعۡرَجِ حَرَجࣱ وَلَا عَلَى ٱلۡمَرِيضِ حَرَجࣱۗ وَمَن يُطِعِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ يُدۡخِلۡهُ جَنَّٰتࣲ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُۖ وَمَن يَتَوَلَّ يُعَذِّبۡهُ عَذَابًا أَلِيمࣰ ا
48:17.en: There is no blame for the blind, nor is there blame for the lame, nor is there blame for the sick (that they go not forth to war). And whoso obeyeth Allah and His messenger, He will make him enter Gardens underneath which rivers flow; and whoso turneth back, him will He punish with a painful doom

48:18.ar: ۞لَّقَدۡ رَضِيَ ٱللَّهُ عَنِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ إِذۡ يُبَايِعُونَكَ تَحۡتَ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ فَعَلِمَ مَا فِي قُلُوبِهِمۡ فَأَنزَلَ ٱلسَّكِينَةَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَأَثَٰبَهُمۡ فَتۡحࣰ ا قَرِيبࣰ ا
48:18.en: Allah was well pleased with the believers when they swore allegiance unto thee beneath the tree, and He knew what was in their hearts, and He sent down peace of reassurance on them, and hath rewarded them with a near victory

48:19.ar: وَمَغَانِمَ كَثِيرَةࣰ يَأۡخُذُونَهَاۗ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَزِيزًا حَكِيمࣰ ا
48:19.en: And much booty that they will capture. Allah is ever Mighty, Wise

48:20.ar: وَعَدَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ مَغَانِمَ كَثِيرَةࣰ تَأۡخُذُونَهَا فَعَجَّلَ لَكُمۡ هَٰذِهِۦ وَكَفَّ أَيۡدِيَ ٱلنَّاسِ عَنكُمۡ وَلِتَكُونَ ءَايَةࣰ لِّلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَيَهۡدِيَكُمۡ صِرَٰطࣰ ا مُّسۡتَقِيمࣰ ا
48:20.en: Allah promiseth you much booty that ye will capture, and hath given you this in advance, and hath withheld men's hands from you, that it may be a token for the believers, and that He may guide you on a right path

48:21.ar: وَأُخۡرَىٰ لَمۡ تَقۡدِرُواْ عَلَيۡهَا قَدۡ أَحَاطَ ٱللَّهُ بِهَاۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣰ ا
48:21.en: And other (gain), which ye have not been able to achieve, Allah will compass it, Allah is Able to do all things

48:22.ar: وَلَوۡ قَٰتَلَكُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَوَلَّوُاْ ٱلۡأَدۡبَٰرَ ثُمَّ لَا يَجِدُونَ وَلِيࣰّ ا وَلَا نَصِيرࣰ ا
48:22.en: And if those who disbelieve join battle with you they will take to flight, and afterward they will find no protecting friend nor helper

48:23.ar: سُنَّةَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّتِي قَدۡ خَلَتۡ مِن قَبۡلُۖ وَلَن تَجِدَ لِسُنَّةِ ٱللَّهِ تَبۡدِيلࣰ ا
48:23.en: It is the law of Allah which hath taken course aforetime. Thou wilt not find for the law of Allah aught of power to change

48:24.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي كَفَّ أَيۡدِيَهُمۡ عَنكُمۡ وَأَيۡدِيَكُمۡ عَنۡهُم بِبَطۡنِ مَكَّةَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ أَنۡ أَظۡفَرَكُمۡ عَلَيۡهِمۡۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ بَصِيرًا
48:24.en: And He it is Who hath withheld men's hands from you, and hath withheld your hands from them, in the valley of Mecca, after He had made you victors over them. Allah is Seer of what ye do

48:25.ar: هُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَصَدُّوكُمۡ عَنِ ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡحَرَامِ وَٱلۡهَدۡيَ مَعۡكُوفًا أَن يَبۡلُغَ مَحِلَّهُۥۚ وَلَوۡلَا رِجَالࣱ مُّؤۡمِنُونَ وَنِسَآءࣱ مُّؤۡمِنَٰتࣱ لَّمۡ تَعۡلَمُوهُمۡ أَن تَطَـُٔوهُمۡ فَتُصِيبَكُم مِّنۡهُم مَّعَرَّةُۢ بِغَيۡرِ عِلۡمࣲۖ لِّيُدۡخِلَ ٱللَّهُ فِي رَحۡمَتِهِۦ مَن يَشَآءُۚ لَوۡ تَزَيَّلُواْ لَعَذَّبۡنَا ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنۡهُمۡ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا
48:25.en: These it was who disbelieved and debarred you from the Inviolable Place of Worship, and debarred the offering from reaching its goal. And if it had not been for believing men and believing women, whom ye know not - lest ye should tread them under foot and thus incur guilt for them unknowingly; that Allah might bring into His mercy whom He will - If (the believers and the disbelievers) had been clearly separated We verily had punished those of them who disbelieved with painful punishment

48:26.ar: إِذۡ جَعَلَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ ٱلۡحَمِيَّةَ حَمِيَّةَ ٱلۡجَٰهِلِيَّةِ فَأَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُۥ عَلَىٰ رَسُولِهِۦ وَعَلَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَأَلۡزَمَهُمۡ كَلِمَةَ ٱلتَّقۡوَىٰ وَكَانُوٓاْ أَحَقَّ بِهَا وَأَهۡلَهَاۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءٍ عَلِيمࣰ ا
48:26.en: When those who disbelieve had set up in their hearts zealotry, the zealotry of the Age of Ignorance, then Allah sent down His peace of reassurance upon His messenger and upon the believers and imposed on them the word of self-restraint, for they were worthy of it and meet for it. And Allah is Aware of all things

48:27.ar: لَّقَدۡ صَدَقَ ٱللَّهُ رَسُولَهُ ٱلرُّءۡيَا بِٱلۡحَقِّۖ لَتَدۡخُلُنَّ ٱلۡمَسۡجِدَ ٱلۡحَرَامَ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ ءَامِنِينَ مُحَلِّقِينَ رُءُوسَكُمۡ وَمُقَصِّرِينَ لَا تَخَافُونَۖ فَعَلِمَ مَا لَمۡ تَعۡلَمُواْ فَجَعَلَ مِن دُونِ ذَٰلِكَ فَتۡحࣰ ا قَرِيبًا
48:27.en: Allah hath fulfilled the vision for His messenger in very truth. Ye shall indeed enter the Inviolable Place of Worship, if Allah will, secure, (having your hair) shaven and cut, not fearing. But He knoweth that which ye know not, and hath given you a near victory beforehand

48:28.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَرۡسَلَ رَسُولَهُۥ بِٱلۡهُدَىٰ وَدِينِ ٱلۡحَقِّ لِيُظۡهِرَهُۥ عَلَى ٱلدِّينِ كُلِّهِۦۚ وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ شَهِيدࣰ ا
48:28.en: He it is Who hath sent His messenger with the guidance and the religion of truth, that He may cause it to prevail over all religion. And Allah sufficeth as a Witness

48:29.ar: مُّحَمَّدࣱ رَّسُولُ ٱللَّهِۚ وَٱلَّذِينَ مَعَهُۥٓ أَشِدَّآءُ عَلَى ٱلۡكُفَّارِ رُحَمَآءُ بَيۡنَهُمۡۖ تَرَىٰهُمۡ رُكَّعࣰ ا سُجَّدࣰ ا يَبۡتَغُونَ فَضۡلࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرِضۡوَٰنࣰ اۖ سِيمَاهُمۡ فِي وُجُوهِهِم مِّنۡ أَثَرِ ٱلسُّجُودِۚ ذَٰلِكَ مَثَلُهُمۡ فِي ٱلتَّوۡرَىٰةِۚ وَمَثَلُهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡإِنجِيلِ كَزَرۡعٍ أَخۡرَجَ شَطۡـَٔهُۥ فَـَٔازَرَهُۥ فَٱسۡتَغۡلَظَ فَٱسۡتَوَىٰ عَلَىٰ سُوقِهِۦ يُعۡجِبُ ٱلزُّرَّاعَ لِيَغِيظَ بِهِمُ ٱلۡكُفَّارَۗ وَعَدَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ مِنۡهُم مَّغۡفِرَةࣰ وَأَجۡرًا عَظِيمَۢا
48:29.en: Muhammad is the messenger of Allah. And those with him are hard against the disbelievers and merciful among themselves. Thou (O Muhammad) seest them bowing and falling prostrate (in worship), seeking bounty from Allah and (His) acceptance. The mark of them is on their foreheads from the traces of prostration. Such is their likeness in the Torah and their likeness in the Gospel - like as sown corn that sendeth forth its shoot and strengtheneth it and riseth firm upon its stalk, delighting the sowers - that He may enrage the disbelievers with (the sight of) them. Allah hath promised, unto such of them as believe and do good works, forgiveness and immense reward

FZELNw-ZR0A.title: Surat Al-Fath Summary
FZELNw-ZR0A.one_line: Al-Fath shows the companions who followed the Prophet through Hudaybiyyah: tranquility, Allah's pleasure and victory come to those who stand firm, in time.
FZELNw-ZR0A.summary: Al-Fath continues Surat Muhammad by showing those who did follow the Prophet and what they received. Revealed after the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, its opening refers to the treaty, not the conquest of Makkah. He sets the scene: hard years after Uhud, low morale, a dream of umrah, being turned away from Makkah, the rumour of Uthman's death and the pledge to fight. The treaty seemed grossly unfair and the companions, Umar above all, were furious, but the Prophet cared only for ten years of peace. Within two years the number of Muslims soared, and Umar regretted his objection for life. Lesson: following him bears fruit over time. No surah praises the companions more: Allah's hand was over their hands at the pledge under the tree, and He was pleased with them for what was in their hearts though no fight came. Their reward begins with sakinah, a calm certainty that you are on the right path however fierce the storm, not a promise that nothing hard will happen. The bedouins who wanted only the spoils show those present only in easy times; young Muslims standing firm at school are the opposite. Faced with tribal racism, the believers kept to taqwa. Promises came true twenty years in, some never living to see them, like a seed slowly becoming a sturdy plant.

outline.heading: Al-Fath continues Surat Muhammad
outline.gist: Muhammad said follow him; Al-Fath shows those who did and what they received.

outline.heading: The opening refers to the treaty, not the conquest
outline.gist: Revealed after Hudaybiyyah, before Makkah was conquered, and that is why the surah matters.

outline.heading: A clear opening that no one was happy with
outline.gist: Forgiveness, guidance and victory are promised, yet only the Prophet welcomed the treaty, which is why it belongs in a cluster about following him.

outline.heading: Hudaybiyyah: the hard years and the dream of umrah
outline.gist: After Uhud the Muslims faced assassinations, hunger and stalled growth; the Prophet led them to umrah and they were turned away despite custom.

outline.heading: Hudaybiyyah: Uthman's rumoured death and the unfair terms
outline.gist: They pledged to fight though they came without arms; the first clause sent them home without umrah.

outline.heading: Hudaybiyyah: the companions' anger and ten years of peace
outline.gist: Umar tried to rally objection; the Prophet cared only for the peace clause, accepting even one-sided return terms.

outline.heading: Following him takes time to bear fruit
outline.gist: Individuals, families and societies do not change at once; success under his way takes time.

outline.heading: Two years later the numbers soared
outline.gist: Peace let the message spread; Umar admitted the Prophet's vision was right and regretted that day until he died.

outline.heading: Sent as a witness, bringer of good news and warner
outline.gist: People measure themselves against his example so they believe, honour and exalt Allah.

outline.heading: The pledge under the tree: Allah's hand above theirs
outline.gist: No surah praises the companions as much; Allah Himself took part in their pledge, an honour unmatched in prophetic history.

outline.heading: Real followers who came through
outline.gist: Surat Muhammad asked for readiness to give one's life; Al-Fath shows people who actually did it, so his example is not only individual.

outline.heading: Allah was pleased with them and knew their hearts
outline.gist: No battle came, but their sincere readiness was what He wanted them to prove.

outline.heading: Sakinah: what following him gives first
outline.gist: Tranquility through any storm, from a deep understanding that you are on the right path; it does not mean nothing hard will happen.

outline.heading: The bedouins' excuses
outline.gist: They claimed work and family kept them back, but they expected the Prophet's party to be killed.

outline.heading: There only for the spoils
outline.gist: When there was booty they wanted to join; they were present only for the good times.

outline.heading: Are you there when it is hard?
outline.gist: Young Muslims looked at differently at school prove their following by holding to their deen; it is easy only when everyone around is Muslim.

outline.heading: Promised spoils they could not imagine
outline.gist: Khaybar and the great tribes of Hunayn were gains none of them pictured at the time.

outline.heading: Allah's law: stand firm and it works out in time
outline.gist: It may not happen immediately or even in your lifetime, but it will.

outline.heading: The fervour of ignorance: racism and bigotry
outline.gist: Quraysh filled their hearts with tribal hatred and generalisation; the danger is answering it with the same.

outline.heading: Holding to the word of taqwa
outline.gist: With tranquility the believers did not stoop to racism, knowing all of Allah's creation is equal.

outline.heading: The dream fulfilled, twenty years on
outline.gist: Entering the Mosque in safety was promised, yet companions died before seeing it; the promise may outlast your lifetime.

outline.heading: From sakinah to fath: the religion of truth above all
outline.gist: Their path ran from tranquility through guidance and forgiveness to conquest and an unparalleled civilisation.

outline.heading: Interlude
Muhammad and those with him
outline.gist: Firm against oppressors, compassionate to one another, the mark of prostration on their faces.

outline.heading: Like a seed that slowly grows sturdy
outline.gist: Growth comes with ups and downs over time, and Allah promises it will work out for those who follow.

themes.label: Obedience to Allah and the Messenger
themes.note: The surah is the model of those who followed the Prophet even when they could not see his wisdom.

themes.label: Seerah events and their lessons
themes.note: Hudaybiyyah: the journey, the pledge, the treaty and its results.

themes.label: Patience (sabr) and perseverance
themes.note: Results of following him take time, sometimes beyond one's lifetime.

themes.label: The companions and the early generations
themes.note: The companions of the tree as the clearest example of sincere followers whom Allah praised.

themes.label: Spirituality, khushoo and the inner life
themes.note: Sakinah as calm certainty in the storm, not freedom from hardship.

themes.label: Hypocrisy (nifaq)
themes.note: Bedouins present only when there were spoils.

themes.label: Muslim identity and life in the West / Canada
themes.note: Young Muslims holding to their deen when others view them differently.

themes.label: Human equality and racism
themes.note: Respond to tribal and national contempt with taqwa, not counter-racism.

hadith.gist: Umar questioned whether the treaty was really a victory, and later said he did good deeds for the rest of his life in repentance for how he acted that day.

maxims: Sakinah is not things always going your way
Are you there when it is hard?
It takes time, but it will work out

stories.point: A deal that looked unfair became the opening; long-term vision beats short-term reaction.
He objected, later admitted he was wrong and regretted it for life.
Sincere readiness to sacrifice earned Allah's pleasure even without a battle.
Present only for good times and spoils.

contemporary: Muslim youth facing prejudice at school
takeaways: Follow the Prophet's guidance even when you cannot see its wisdom yet
Expect results of doing right to take time, even beyond your lifetime
Stand by your deen in hard times, not just easy ones
Answer racism and contempt with taqwa and calm, never with the same
Seek sakinah through certainty in the path rather than in easy outcomes

50:2.ar: بَلۡ عَجِبُوٓاْ أَن جَآءَهُم مُّنذِرࣱ مِّنۡهُمۡ فَقَالَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرُونَ هَٰذَا شَيۡءٌ عَجِيبٌ
50:2.en: Nay, but they marvel that a warner of their own hath come unto them; and the disbelievers say: This is a strange thing

50:3.ar: أَءِذَا مِتۡنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَابࣰ اۖ ذَٰلِكَ رَجۡعُۢ بَعِيدࣱ‏
50:3.en: When we are dead and have become dust (shall we be brought back again)? That would be a far return

50:4.ar: قَدۡ عَلِمۡنَا مَا تَنقُصُ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ مِنۡهُمۡۖ وَعِندَنَا كِتَٰبٌ حَفِيظُۢ
50:4.en: We know that which the earth taketh of them, and with Us is a recording Book

50:5.ar: بَلۡ كَذَّبُواْ بِٱلۡحَقِّ لَمَّا جَآءَهُمۡ فَهُمۡ فِيٓ أَمۡرࣲ مَّرِيجٍ
50:5.en: Nay, but they have denied the truth when it came unto them, therefor they are now in troubled case

50:6.ar: أَفَلَمۡ يَنظُرُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَوۡقَهُمۡ كَيۡفَ بَنَيۡنَٰهَا وَزَيَّنَّٰهَا وَمَا لَهَا مِن فُرُوجࣲ‏
50:6.en: Have they not then observed the sky above them, how We have constructed it and beautified it, and how there are no rifts therein

50:7.ar: وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ مَدَدۡنَٰهَا وَأَلۡقَيۡنَا فِيهَا رَوَٰسِيَ وَأَنۢبَتۡنَا فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ زَوۡجِۭ بَهِيجࣲ‏
50:7.en: And the earth have We spread out, and have flung firm hills therein, and have caused of every lovely kind to grow thereon

50:8.en: A vision and a reminder for every penitent slave

50:9.ar: وَنَزَّلۡنَا مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰ مُّبَٰرَكࣰ ا فَأَنۢبَتۡنَا بِهِۦ جَنَّٰتࣲ وَحَبَّ ٱلۡحَصِيدِ
50:9.en: And We send down from the sky blessed water whereby We give growth unto gardens and the grain of crops

50:10.en: And lofty date-palms with ranged clusters

50:11.ar: رِّزۡقࣰ ا لِّلۡعِبَادِۖ وَأَحۡيَيۡنَا بِهِۦ بَلۡدَةࣰ مَّيۡتࣰ اۚ كَذَٰلِكَ ٱلۡخُرُوجُ
50:11.en: Provision (made) for men; and therewith We quicken a dead land. Even so will be the resurrection of the dead

50:12.ar: كَذَّبَتۡ قَبۡلَهُمۡ قَوۡمُ نُوحࣲ وَأَصۡحَٰبُ ٱلرَّسِّ وَثَمُودُ
50:12.en: The folk of Noah denied (the truth) before them, and (so did) the dwellers at Ar-Rass and (the tribe of) Thamud

50:13.en: And (the tribe of) A'ad, and Pharaoh, and the brethren of Lot

50:14.ar: وَأَصۡحَٰبُ ٱلۡأَيۡكَةِ وَقَوۡمُ تُبَّعࣲۚ كُلࣱّ كَذَّبَ ٱلرُّسُلَ فَحَقَّ وَعِيدِ
50:14.en: And the dwellers in the wood, and the folk of Tubb'a: every one denied their messengers, therefor My threat took effect

50:15.ar: أَفَعَيِينَا بِٱلۡخَلۡقِ ٱلۡأَوَّلِۚ بَلۡ هُمۡ فِي لَبۡسࣲ مِّنۡ خَلۡقࣲ جَدِيدࣲ‏
50:15.en: Were We then worn out by the first creation? Yet they are in doubt about a new creation

50:16.ar: وَلَقَدۡ خَلَقۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ وَنَعۡلَمُ مَا تُوَسۡوِسُ بِهِۦ نَفۡسُهُۥۖ وَنَحۡنُ أَقۡرَبُ إِلَيۡهِ مِنۡ حَبۡلِ ٱلۡوَرِيدِ
50:16.en: We verily created man and We know what his soul whispereth to him, and We are nearer to him than his jugular vein

50:17.ar: إِذۡ يَتَلَقَّى ٱلۡمُتَلَقِّيَانِ عَنِ ٱلۡيَمِينِ وَعَنِ ٱلشِّمَالِ قَعِيدࣱ‏
50:17.en: When the two Receivers receive (him), seated on the right hand and on the left

50:18.ar: مَّا يَلۡفِظُ مِن قَوۡلٍ إِلَّا لَدَيۡهِ رَقِيبٌ عَتِيدࣱ‏
50:18.en: He uttereth no word but there is with him an observer ready

50:19.ar: وَجَآءَتۡ سَكۡرَةُ ٱلۡمَوۡتِ بِٱلۡحَقِّۖ ذَٰلِكَ مَا كُنتَ مِنۡهُ تَحِيدُ
50:19.en: And the agony of death cometh in truth. (And it is said unto him): This is that which thou wast wont to shun

50:20.ar: وَنُفِخَ فِي ٱلصُّورِۚ ذَٰلِكَ يَوۡمُ ٱلۡوَعِيدِ
50:20.en: And the trumpet is blown. This is the threatened Day

50:21.ar: وَجَآءَتۡ كُلُّ نَفۡسࣲ مَّعَهَا سَآئِقࣱ وَشَهِيدࣱ‏
50:21.en: And every soul cometh, along with it a driver and a witness

50:22.ar: لَّقَدۡ كُنتَ فِي غَفۡلَةࣲ مِّنۡ هَٰذَا فَكَشَفۡنَا عَنكَ غِطَآءَكَ فَبَصَرُكَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ حَدِيدࣱ‏
50:22.en: (And unto the evil-doer it is said): Thou wast in heedlessness of this. Now We have removed from thee thy covering, and piercing is thy sight this day

50:23.ar: وَقَالَ قَرِينُهُۥ هَٰذَا مَا لَدَيَّ عَتِيدٌ
50:23.en: And (unto the evil-doer) his comrade saith: This is that which I have ready (as testimony)

50:24.ar: أَلۡقِيَا فِي جَهَنَّمَ كُلَّ كَفَّارٍ عَنِيدࣲ‏
50:24.en: (And it is said): Do ye twain hurl to hell each rebel ingrate

50:26.ar: ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا ءَاخَرَ فَأَلۡقِيَاهُ فِي ٱلۡعَذَابِ ٱلشَّدِيدِ
50:26.en: Who setteth up another god along with Allah. Do ye twain hurl him to the dreadful doom

50:27.ar: ۞قَالَ قَرِينُهُۥ رَبَّنَا مَآ أَطۡغَيۡتُهُۥ وَلَٰكِن كَانَ فِي ضَلَٰلِۭ بَعِيدࣲ‏
50:27.en: His comrade saith: Our Lord! I did not cause him to rebel, but he was (himself) far gone in error

50:28.ar: قَالَ لَا تَخۡتَصِمُواْ لَدَيَّ وَقَدۡ قَدَّمۡتُ إِلَيۡكُم بِٱلۡوَعِيدِ
50:28.en: He saith: Contend not in My presence, when I had already proffered unto you the warning

50:29.ar: مَا يُبَدَّلُ ٱلۡقَوۡلُ لَدَيَّ وَمَآ أَنَا۠ بِظَلَّٰمࣲ لِّلۡعَبِيدِ
50:29.en: The sentence that cometh from Me cannot be changed, and I am in no wise a tyrant unto the slaves

50:30.ar: يَوۡمَ نَقُولُ لِجَهَنَّمَ هَلِ ٱمۡتَلَأۡتِ وَتَقُولُ هَلۡ مِن مَّزِيدࣲ‏
50:30.en: On the day when We say unto hell: Art thou filled? and it saith: Can there be more to come

50:31.en: And the Garden is brought nigh for those who kept from evil, no longer distant

50:32.ar: هَٰذَا مَا تُوعَدُونَ لِكُلِّ أَوَّابٍ حَفِيظࣲ‏
50:32.en: (And it is said): This is that which ye were promised. (It is) for every penitent and heedful one

50:33.ar: مَّنۡ خَشِيَ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنَ بِٱلۡغَيۡبِ وَجَآءَ بِقَلۡبࣲ مُّنِيبٍ
50:33.en: Who feareth the Beneficent in secret and cometh with a contrite heart

50:34.en: Enter it in peace. This is the day of immortality

50:35.ar: لَهُم مَّا يَشَآءُونَ فِيهَا وَلَدَيۡنَا مَزِيدࣱ‏
50:35.en: There they have all that they desire, and there is more with Us

50:36.ar: وَكَمۡ أَهۡلَكۡنَا قَبۡلَهُم مِّن قَرۡنٍ هُمۡ أَشَدُّ مِنۡهُم بَطۡشࣰ ا فَنَقَّبُواْ فِي ٱلۡبِلَٰدِ هَلۡ مِن مَّحِيصٍ
50:36.en: And how many a generation We destroyed before them, who were mightier than these in prowess so that they overran the lands! Had they any place of refuge (when the judgment came)

50:37.ar: إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَذِكۡرَىٰ لِمَن كَانَ لَهُۥ قَلۡبٌ أَوۡ أَلۡقَى ٱلسَّمۡعَ وَهُوَ شَهِيدࣱ‏
50:37.en: Lo! therein verily is a reminder for him who hath a heart, or giveth ear with full intelligence

50:38.ar: وَلَقَدۡ خَلَقۡنَا ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَمَا بَيۡنَهُمَا فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامࣲ وَمَا مَسَّنَا مِن لُّغُوبࣲ‏
50:38.en: And verily We created the heavens and the earth, and all that is between them, in six Days, and naught of weariness touched Us

50:39.ar: فَٱصۡبِرۡ عَلَىٰ مَا يَقُولُونَ وَسَبِّحۡ بِحَمۡدِ رَبِّكَ قَبۡلَ طُلُوعِ ٱلشَّمۡسِ وَقَبۡلَ ٱلۡغُرُوبِ
50:39.en: Therefor (O Muhammad) bear with what they say, and hymn the praise of thy Lord before the rising and before the setting of the sun

50:40.en: And in the night-time hymn His praise, and after the (prescribed) prostrations

50:41.ar: وَٱسۡتَمِعۡ يَوۡمَ يُنَادِ ٱلۡمُنَادِ مِن مَّكَانࣲ قَرِيبࣲ‏
50:41.en: And listen on the day when the crier crieth from a near place

50:42.ar: يَوۡمَ يَسۡمَعُونَ ٱلصَّيۡحَةَ بِٱلۡحَقِّۚ ذَٰلِكَ يَوۡمُ ٱلۡخُرُوجِ
50:42.en: The day when they will hear the (Awful) Cry in truth. That is the day of coming forth (from the graves)

50:43.ar: إِنَّا نَحۡنُ نُحۡيِۦ وَنُمِيتُ وَإِلَيۡنَا ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
50:43.en: Lo! We it is Who quicken and give death, and unto Us is the journeying

50:44.ar: يَوۡمَ تَشَقَّقُ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ عَنۡهُمۡ سِرَاعࣰ اۚ ذَٰلِكَ حَشۡرٌ عَلَيۡنَا يَسِيرࣱ‏
50:44.en: On the day when the earth splitteth asunder from them, hastening forth (they come). That is a gathering easy for Us (to make)

50:45.ar: نَّحۡنُ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَا يَقُولُونَۖ وَمَآ أَنتَ عَلَيۡهِم بِجَبَّارࣲۖ فَذَكِّرۡ بِٱلۡقُرۡءَانِ مَن يَخَافُ وَعِيدِ
50:45.en: We are Best Aware of what they say, and thou (O Muhammad) art in no wise a compeller over them. But warn by the Qur'an him who feareth My threat
