o9giLOKrMhk.title: Surat Qaf Summary
o9giLOKrMhk.one_line: Qaf opens the cluster of comparisons: it flashes forward through creation, death, resurrection and judgment, then returns us to life to choose again.
o9giLOKrMhk.summary: Qaf begins the cluster running from Qaf to Al-Hadid, in which every surah compares two things and offers a choice. Qaf holds perhaps the most important comparison, and people love it because of its movement: it is a flash forward that takes us to the end, returns us to choose, then takes us forward again. The disbelievers wonder at a warner from among them and deny resurrection; Allah answers that He knows what the earth takes from their bodies. Creation itself, the sky, the earth, rain reviving dead land, is the model of resurrection, and Allah was not wearied by the first creation. Three verses summarise life: we are created, our selves whisper to us, Allah is closer than the jugular vein, and two recorders note every word. Then the stupor of death arrives, the thing we fled all our lives. The pivotal verse names heedlessness, whether real or chosen, and today the cover is lifted and sight is sharp. The companion disowns the person, Hell asks for more, Paradise is brought near, and there is more for the people of Paradise too. Like a pious man who would lie in a grave in his room and then rise to a second chance, the surah returns us to life: a reminder for whoever has a heart or truly listens. He urges making the choice now.

outline.heading: Opening
A beloved surah of choices
outline.gist: Qaf is recited often in prayer and was used by the Prophet in sermons, loved for how it is structured.

outline.heading: Not a flashback but a flash forward
outline.gist: It shows us the end, brings us back to choose, then takes us forward again.

outline.heading: Look at the sky and the earth
outline.gist: The signs of creation are laid out for every servant who turns back to Allah.

outline.heading: The cluster from Qaf to Al-Hadid: comparisons and choices
outline.gist: After the cluster on the Prophet, each surah compares two matters and gives two choices covering the great issues of the deen.

outline.heading: Amazed at a warner, denying the return
outline.gist: They find it strange that a warner came from among them and that dust could live again.

outline.heading: We know what the earth takes from them
outline.gist: Every part of the body is known and restored; the surah moves us between the future and the present to choose.

outline.heading: As creation happened, so will resurrection
outline.gist: Rain revives dead land and feeds all life; so is the coming forth, and Allah was not wearied by the first creation.

outline.heading: Closer than the jugular vein, and two recorders
outline.gist: Allah knows what the self whispers; two angels sit to the right and left writing every word.

outline.heading: The stupor of death and the lifted cover
outline.gist: Death is so overwhelming one is not oneself; today your sight is sharp.

outline.heading: The whispering self and Allah's nearness
outline.gist: Life is hours spent resisting or obeying what the self urges; Allah knows what we have not even noticed in ourselves.

outline.heading: Three verses that summarise life, then death
outline.gist: Every word is counted for or against us; death is what we fled and avoided talking about all our lives.

outline.heading: The pivotal verse: heedlessness
outline.gist: Ghaflah may be genuine or chosen; either way the cover is removed and reality is seen without doubt.

outline.heading: The companion's record and Hell asking for more
outline.gist: The companion presents what is ready, the stubborn are cast in, the companion disowns him and Allah forbids disputing.

outline.heading: Paradise brought near
outline.gist: For everyone who turns back, guards his duty and fears the Most Merciful unseen.

outline.heading: Only some can listen with their heart
outline.gist: The reminder benefits the one who understands with his heart and comes back.

outline.heading: A driver and a witness with every soul
outline.gist: An angel drives and a witness testifies; the companion says this is all we have, then denies leading him astray.

outline.heading: The tiring comparison: Hell's 'is there more'
outline.gist: Even those who have not memorised Qaf know the verse; the surah builds to it and it shakes the heart.

outline.heading: More in both outcomes
outline.gist: Hell asks for more and Allah has more for Paradise; the story ends and we are returned to life with a chance.

outline.heading: The pious man with a grave in his room
outline.gist: He would lie in it in the dark, imagine the questioning, then rise and tell himself he had been given another chance; the surah does the same to us.

outline.heading: A reminder for whoever has a heart or lends an ear
outline.gist: One who truly listens and witnesses benefits; one who passes by lets it go no further than his ears.

outline.heading: Six days without fatigue: we are time
outline.gist: Allah needed no time; creation needed it, and the lesson is for us, since all we are is time.

outline.heading: Be patient and glorify your Lord
outline.gist: Praise Him before sunrise, before sunset and at night.

outline.heading: The day of the cry and the earth splitting
outline.gist: The resurrection is easy for Allah; He knows what they say and the Prophet is not a compeller.

outline.heading: Make your choice now
outline.gist: Remind with the Quran whoever fears the warning; stop avoiding thinking about what comes next.

outline.heading: Outro

51:1.en: By those that winnow with a winnowing

51:2.en: And those that bear the burden (of the rain)

51:3.en: And those that glide with ease (upon the sea)

51:4.en: And those who distribute (blessings) by command

51:5.en: Lo! that wherewith ye are threatened is indeed true

51:6.en: And lo! the judgment will indeed befall

51:7.en: By the heaven full of paths

51:8.en: Lo! ye, forsooth, are of various opinion (concerning the truth)

51:9.en: He is made to turn away from it who is (himself) averse

51:11.en: Who are careless in an abyss

51:12.en: They ask: When is the Day of Judgment

51:13.en: (It is) the day when they will be tormented at the Fire

51:14.ar: ذُوقُواْ فِتۡنَتَكُمۡ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِي كُنتُم بِهِۦ تَسۡتَعۡجِلُونَ
51:14.en: (And it will be said unto them): Taste your torment (which ye inflicted). This is what ye sought to hasten

51:15.en: Lo! those who keep from evil will dwell amid gardens and watersprings

51:16.ar: ءَاخِذِينَ مَآ ءَاتَىٰهُمۡ رَبُّهُمۡۚ إِنَّهُمۡ كَانُواْ قَبۡلَ ذَٰلِكَ مُحۡسِنِينَ
51:16.en: Taking that which their Lord giveth them; for lo! aforetime they were doers of good

51:17.ar: كَانُواْ قَلِيلࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلَّيۡلِ مَا يَهۡجَعُونَ
51:17.en: They used to sleep but little of the night

51:18.en: And ere the dawning of each day would seek forgiveness

51:19.en: And in their wealth the beggar and the outcast had due share

51:20.en: And in the earth are portents for those whose faith is sure

51:21.en: And (also) in yourselves. Can ye then not see

51:22.en: And in the heaven is your providence and that which ye are promised

51:23.ar: فَوَرَبِّ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ إِنَّهُۥ لَحَقࣱّ مِّثۡلَ مَآ أَنَّكُمۡ تَنطِقُونَ
51:23.en: And by the Lord of the heavens and the earth, it is the truth, even as (it is true) that ye speak

51:24.ar: هَلۡ أَتَىٰكَ حَدِيثُ ضَيۡفِ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ ٱلۡمُكۡرَمِينَ
51:24.en: Hath the story of Abraham's honoured guests reached thee (O Muhammad)

51:25.ar: إِذۡ دَخَلُواْ عَلَيۡهِ فَقَالُواْ سَلَٰمࣰ اۖ قَالَ سَلَٰمࣱ قَوۡمࣱ مُّنكَرُونَ
51:25.en: When they came in unto him and said: Peace! he answered, Peace! (and thought): Folk unknown (to me)

51:26.ar: فَرَاغَ إِلَىٰٓ أَهۡلِهِۦ فَجَآءَ بِعِجۡلࣲ سَمِينࣲ‏
51:26.en: Then he went apart unto his housefolk so that they brought a fatted calf

51:27.en: And he set it before them, saying: Will ye not eat

51:28.ar: فَأَوۡجَسَ مِنۡهُمۡ خِيفَةࣰۖ قَالُواْ لَا تَخَفۡۖ وَبَشَّرُوهُ بِغُلَٰمٍ عَلِيمࣲ‏
51:28.en: Then he conceived a fear of them. They said: Fear not! and gave him tidings of (the birth of) a wise son

51:29.ar: فَأَقۡبَلَتِ ٱمۡرَأَتُهُۥ فِي صَرَّةࣲ فَصَكَّتۡ وَجۡهَهَا وَقَالَتۡ عَجُوزٌ عَقِيمࣱ‏
51:29.en: Then his wife came forward, making moan, and smote her face, and cried: A barren old woman

51:30.ar: قَالُواْ كَذَٰلِكِ قَالَ رَبُّكِۖ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ
51:30.en: They said: Even so saith thy Lord. Lo! He is the Wise, the Knower

51:31.en: (Abraham) said: And (afterward) what is your errand, O ye sent (from Allah)

51:32.ar: قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّآ أُرۡسِلۡنَآ إِلَىٰ قَوۡمࣲ مُّجۡرِمِينَ
51:32.en: They said: Lo! we are sent unto a guilty folk

51:33.en: That we may send upon them stones of clay

51:34.en: Marked by thy Lord for (the destruction of) the wanton

51:35.ar: فَأَخۡرَجۡنَا مَن كَانَ فِيهَا مِنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
51:35.en: Then we brought forth such believers as were there

51:36.ar: فَمَا وَجَدۡنَا فِيهَا غَيۡرَ بَيۡتࣲ مِّنَ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ
51:36.en: But We found there but one house of those surrendered (to Allah)

51:37.ar: وَتَرَكۡنَا فِيهَآ ءَايَةࣰ لِّلَّذِينَ يَخَافُونَ ٱلۡعَذَابَ ٱلۡأَلِيمَ
51:37.en: And We left behind therein a portent for those who fear a painful doom

51:38.ar: وَفِي مُوسَىٰٓ إِذۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَٰهُ إِلَىٰ فِرۡعَوۡنَ بِسُلۡطَٰنࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
51:38.en: And in Moses (too, there is a portent) when We sent him unto Pharaoh with clear warrant

51:39.ar: فَتَوَلَّىٰ بِرُكۡنِهِۦ وَقَالَ سَٰحِرٌ أَوۡ مَجۡنُونࣱ‏
51:39.en: But he withdrew (confiding) in his might, and said: A wizard or a madman

51:40.ar: فَأَخَذۡنَٰهُ وَجُنُودَهُۥ فَنَبَذۡنَٰهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡيَمِّ وَهُوَ مُلِيمࣱ‏
51:40.en: So We seized him and his hosts and flung them in the sea, for he was reprobate

51:41.ar: وَفِي عَادٍ إِذۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلرِّيحَ ٱلۡعَقِيمَ
51:41.en: And in (the tribe of) A'ad (there is a portent) when we sent the fatal wind against them

51:42.ar: مَا تَذَرُ مِن شَيۡءٍ أَتَتۡ عَلَيۡهِ إِلَّا جَعَلَتۡهُ كَٱلرَّمِيمِ
51:42.en: It spared naught that it reached, but made it (all) as dust

51:43.ar: وَفِي ثَمُودَ إِذۡ قِيلَ لَهُمۡ تَمَتَّعُواْ حَتَّىٰ حِينࣲ‏
51:43.en: And in (the tribe of) Thamud (there is a portent) when it was told them: Take your ease awhile

51:44.ar: فَعَتَوۡاْ عَنۡ أَمۡرِ رَبِّهِمۡ فَأَخَذَتۡهُمُ ٱلصَّٰعِقَةُ وَهُمۡ يَنظُرُونَ
51:44.en: But they rebelled against their Lord's decree, and so the thunderbolt overtook them even while they gazed

51:45.ar: فَمَا ٱسۡتَطَٰعُواْ مِن قِيَامࣲ وَمَا كَانُواْ مُنتَصِرِينَ
51:45.en: And they were unable to rise up, nor could they help themselves

51:46.ar: وَقَوۡمَ نُوحࣲ مِّن قَبۡلُۖ إِنَّهُمۡ كَانُواْ قَوۡمࣰ ا فَٰسِقِينَ
51:46.en: And the folk of Noah aforetime. Lo! they were licentious folk

51:47.en: We have built the heaven with might, and We it is Who make the vast extent (thereof)

51:48.en: And the earth have We laid out, how gracious is the Spreader (thereof)

51:49.ar: وَمِن كُلِّ شَيۡءٍ خَلَقۡنَا زَوۡجَيۡنِ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَذَكَّرُونَ
51:49.en: And all things We have created by pairs, that haply ye may reflect

51:50.ar: فَفِرُّوٓاْ إِلَى ٱللَّهِۖ إِنِّي لَكُم مِّنۡهُ نَذِيرࣱ مُّبِينࣱ‏
51:50.en: Therefor flee unto Allah; lo! I am a plain warner unto you from him

51:51.ar: وَلَا تَجۡعَلُواْ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا ءَاخَرَۖ إِنِّي لَكُم مِّنۡهُ نَذِيرࣱ مُّبِينࣱ‏
51:51.en: And set not any other god along with Allah; lo! I am a plain warner unto you from Him

51:52.ar: كَذَٰلِكَ مَآ أَتَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِم مِّن رَّسُولٍ إِلَّا قَالُواْ سَاحِرٌ أَوۡ مَجۡنُونٌ
51:52.en: Even so there came no messenger unto those before them but they said: A wizard or a madman

51:53.ar: أَتَوَاصَوۡاْ بِهِۦۚ بَلۡ هُمۡ قَوۡمࣱ طَاغُونَ
51:53.en: Have they handed down (the saying) as an heirloom one unto another? Nay, but they are froward folk

51:54.en: So withdraw from them (O Muhammad), for thou art in no wise blameworthy

51:55.en: And warn, for warning profiteth believers

51:56.ar: وَمَا خَلَقۡتُ ٱلۡجِنَّ وَٱلۡإِنسَ إِلَّا لِيَعۡبُدُونِ
51:56.en: I created the jinn and humankind only that they might worship Me

51:57.ar: مَآ أُرِيدُ مِنۡهُم مِّن رِّزۡقࣲ وَمَآ أُرِيدُ أَن يُطۡعِمُونِ
51:57.en: I seek no livelihood from them, nor do I ask that they should feed Me

51:58.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلرَّزَّاقُ ذُو ٱلۡقُوَّةِ ٱلۡمَتِينُ
51:58.en: Lo! Allah! He it is that giveth livelihood, the Lord of unbreakable might

51:59.ar: فَإِنَّ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ ذَنُوبࣰ ا مِّثۡلَ ذَنُوبِ أَصۡحَٰبِهِمۡ فَلَا يَسۡتَعۡجِلُونِ
51:59.en: And lo! for those who (now) do wrong there is an evil day like unto the evil day (which came for) their likes (of old); so let them not ask Me to hasten on (that day)

51:60.ar: فَوَيۡلࣱ لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِن يَوۡمِهِمُ ٱلَّذِي يُوعَدُونَ
51:60.en: And woe unto those who disbelieve, from (that) their day which they are promised

awV-LhH9300.title: Surat Adh-Dhariyat Summary
awV-LhH9300.one_line: Adh-Dhariyat compares a purposeful, functional life with an aimless one, building to the verse that we were created only to worship.
awV-LhH9300.summary: Adh-Dhariyat, the second surah of the cluster of comparisons, contrasts being purposeful and functional with living aimlessly. It opens with oaths by winds, clouds and ships, things that each play a role in stages toward a final goal, and swears that religion is reality. Against this stand those who lie for no purpose, drowning in distraction without noticing. The pious are described by both kinds of worship: night prayer and seeking forgiveness between them and Allah, and a share of their wealth for the asker and the deprived. Signs on earth, in ourselves and in the sky invite the big questions; everyone has a life philosophy, and without big questions there are no big answers. The aimless make wealth their focus, yet provision is guaranteed. The four short stories share a thread through the word 'aqim, barren: Ibrahim's wife called herself barren but was not, because she played her role, and childless women have done much for the ummah; the wind sent on 'Ad was the barren wind; the same clay that builds houses rained on Lut's people; Thamud's carved castles and Pharaoh's power did not make them functional. Flee to Allah toward a clearer life. The surah builds to the verse that jinn and humans were created only to worship, in its full sense, not for provision.

outline.heading: The second comparison: purpose versus aimlessness
outline.gist: The cluster from Qaf to Al-Hadid offers choices; this surah contrasts a functional, purposeful life with one whose goals are not those Allah gave.

outline.heading: A Makki surah holding perhaps the most important verse
outline.gist: It contains the verse that tells us why we exist, with stories and topics that explain it.

outline.heading: Oaths by winds, clouds and ships: roles in stages
outline.gist: Whatever the scholars take them to be, each plays a role one step at a time toward a final goal, and so must we.

outline.heading: Religion is reality
outline.gist: The answer to the oaths: what you are promised is true and the deen will be reality, fitting the sense of shared purpose.

outline.heading: Those who lie aimlessly, drowning in distraction
outline.gist: They lie for no goal and do not notice how close they are to complete loss.

outline.heading: The pious in gardens and springs
outline.gist: They take what Allah gives them because they lived with excellence.

outline.heading: Two kinds of worship
outline.gist: Little sleep and seeking forgiveness before dawn between them and Allah; a right in their wealth for the asker and the deprived serving others.

outline.heading: Signs on earth, in yourselves and in the sky
outline.gist: Be as certain of your provision as of your own speech.

outline.heading: Without big questions there are no big answers
outline.gist: Purpose begins with asking what the universe is for and whether I have a role in a larger plan.

outline.heading: Everyone has a life philosophy
outline.gist: Metacognition forces humans to hold a worldview; some settle early for a meaningless one, others reflect and reach the right answer.

outline.heading: You are not here for wealth
outline.gist: The aimless make money their focus; we work for provision, but Allah guarantees it and our purpose lies elsewhere.

outline.heading: Ibrahim's guests and the thread through four stories
outline.gist: The angels on their way to Lut's people refuse food and give news of a knowledgeable son.

outline.heading: Barren: present but not functioning
outline.gist: Ibrahim's wife struck her face and called herself an old barren woman; 'aqim means something that is there but does not do its job.

outline.heading: Not barren: childless women and their roles
outline.gist: Allah corrected her: she was playing her role; many women without children have done great things for the ummah.

outline.heading: The barren wind sent on 'Ad
outline.gist: Wind normally pollinates and carries rain, but this one only destroyed.

outline.heading: Clay that builds houses rains on Lut's people
outline.gist: The same thing can be used productively or destructively; what matters is how you use what you have.

outline.heading: Thamud's carved castles: busy is not functional
outline.gist: Doing a lot does not mean doing the right thing, and not doing what everyone does does not mean you have no role.

outline.heading: Pharaoh drowned in his distraction
outline.gist: Musa came with clear evidence but Pharaoh turned away in arrogance and drowned, the same drowning the surah warned of at its start.

outline.heading: Everything in pairs: this is going somewhere
outline.gist: The expanding heavens and spread earth point to a goal; Nuh and the prophets are recalled briefly.

outline.heading: Flee to Allah, toward a better reality
outline.gist: Knowing what you are here for makes life calmer, happier and more focused.

outline.heading: Created only to worship, in its full sense
outline.gist: The verse the surah builds to; worship includes rituals but is far wider than them.

outline.heading: I want no provision from you
outline.gist: Allah is the Provider; what are we chasing money for when our children will do the same?

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Purpose, meaning and the point of life
themes.note: The surah's comparison of a purposeful, functional life with an aimless one.

themes.label: Heedlessness, play and taking the deen lightly
themes.note: Aimless liars drowning in distraction without noticing.

themes.label: Salah: its meaning, etiquette and significance
themes.note: Night prayer and pre-dawn forgiveness as worship between you and Allah.

themes.label: Zakat, charity and giving
themes.note: A right in wealth for the asker and deprived as worship that serves others.

themes.label: Atheism, doubt and responding to disbelief
themes.note: Asking the big questions and holding a life philosophy is the start of finding purpose.

themes.label: Wealth, asceticism (zuhd), consumerism and money
themes.note: Provision is guaranteed, so wealth cannot be the goal of life.

themes.label: Quranic stories and their lessons
themes.note: Four stories linked by being functional or not: Ibrahim's wife, 'Ad, Lut, Thamud, Pharaoh.

themes.label: Gender relations, chastity and modesty
themes.note: Women without children are not barren in role; many served the ummah greatly.

themes.label: Tawhid and worship of Allah alone
themes.note: We were created for worship in its full sense, not for provision.

maxims: Religion is reality
Without big questions there are no big answers
Busy is not the same as functional
You are not here for wealth

stories.point: She thought herself barren, but anyone playing their role is productive; childlessness does not mean uselessness.
A wind that should bring life brought only destruction.
Building clay became stones of punishment; it depends how things are used.
Great building is not the same as doing what you are here for.
Pharaoh had the evidence but turned away in arrogance and drowned.

takeaways: Identify your role in the bigger goal Allah set and do it well
Ask the big questions about life and its purpose
Balance worship between you and Allah with worship that serves others
Work for provision without making wealth your purpose
Treat all of life as worship, not just rituals

54:1.en: The hour drew nigh and the moon was rent in twain

54:2.ar: وَإِن يَرَوۡاْ ءَايَةࣰ يُعۡرِضُواْ وَيَقُولُواْ سِحۡرࣱ مُّسۡتَمِرࣱّ‏
54:2.en: And if they behold a portent they turn away and say: Prolonged illusion

54:3.ar: وَكَذَّبُواْ وَٱتَّبَعُوٓاْ أَهۡوَآءَهُمۡۚ وَكُلُّ أَمۡرࣲ مُّسۡتَقِرࣱّ‏
54:3.en: They denied (the Truth) and followed their own lusts. Yet everything will come to a decision

54:4.ar: وَلَقَدۡ جَآءَهُم مِّنَ ٱلۡأَنۢبَآءِ مَا فِيهِ مُزۡدَجَرٌ
54:4.en: And surely there hath come unto them news whereof the purport should deter

54:5.en: Effective wisdom; but warnings avail not

54:6.ar: فَتَوَلَّ عَنۡهُمۡۘ يَوۡمَ يَدۡعُ ٱلدَّاعِ إِلَىٰ شَيۡءࣲ نُّكُرٍ
54:6.en: So withdraw from them (O Muhammad) on the day when the Summoner summoneth unto a painful thing

54:7.ar: خُشَّعًا أَبۡصَٰرُهُمۡ يَخۡرُجُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡأَجۡدَاثِ كَأَنَّهُمۡ جَرَادࣱ مُّنتَشِرࣱ‏
54:7.en: With downcast eyes, they come forth from the graves as they were locusts spread abroad

54:8.ar: مُّهۡطِعِينَ إِلَى ٱلدَّاعِۖ يَقُولُ ٱلۡكَٰفِرُونَ هَٰذَا يَوۡمٌ عَسِرࣱ‏
54:8.en: Hastening toward the summoner; the disbelievers say: This is a hard day

54:9.ar: ۞كَذَّبَتۡ قَبۡلَهُمۡ قَوۡمُ نُوحࣲ فَكَذَّبُواْ عَبۡدَنَا وَقَالُواْ مَجۡنُونࣱ وَٱزۡدُجِرَ
54:9.en: The folk of Noah denied before them, yea, they denied Our slave and said: A madman; and he was repulsed

54:10.en: So he cried unto his Lord, saying: I am vanquished, so give help

54:11.en: Then opened We the gates of heaven with pouring water

54:12.ar: وَفَجَّرۡنَا ٱلۡأَرۡضَ عُيُونࣰ ا فَٱلۡتَقَى ٱلۡمَآءُ عَلَىٰٓ أَمۡرࣲ قَدۡ قُدِرَ
54:12.en: And caused the earth to gush forth springs, so that the waters met for a predestined purpose

54:13.en: And We carried him upon a thing of planks and nails

54:14.ar: تَجۡرِي بِأَعۡيُنِنَا جَزَآءࣰ لِّمَن كَانَ كُفِرَ
54:14.en: That ran (upon the waters) in Our sight, as a reward for him who was rejected

54:15.ar: وَلَقَد تَّرَكۡنَٰهَآ ءَايَةࣰ فَهَلۡ مِن مُّدَّكِرࣲ‏
54:15.en: And verily We left it as a token; but is there any that remembereth

54:16.en: Then see how (dreadful) was My punishment after My warnings

54:17.ar: وَلَقَدۡ يَسَّرۡنَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ لِلذِّكۡرِ فَهَلۡ مِن مُّدَّكِرࣲ‏
54:17.en: And in truth We have made the Qur'an easy to remember; but is there any that remembereth

54:18.ar: كَذَّبَتۡ عَادࣱ فَكَيۡفَ كَانَ عَذَابِي وَنُذُرِ
54:18.en: (The tribe of) A'ad rejected warnings. Then how (dreadful) was My punishment after My warnings

54:19.ar: إِنَّآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ رِيحࣰ ا صَرۡصَرࣰ ا فِي يَوۡمِ نَحۡسࣲ مُّسۡتَمِرࣲّ‏
54:19.en: Lo! We let loose on them a raging wind on a day of constant calamity

54:20.ar: تَنزِعُ ٱلنَّاسَ كَأَنَّهُمۡ أَعۡجَازُ نَخۡلࣲ مُّنقَعِرࣲ‏
54:20.en: Sweeping men away as though they were uprooted trunks of palm-trees

54:21.en: Then see how (dreadful) was My punishment after My warnings

54:22.ar: وَلَقَدۡ يَسَّرۡنَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ لِلذِّكۡرِ فَهَلۡ مِن مُّدَّكِرࣲ‏
54:22.en: And in truth We have made the Qur'an easy to remember; but is there any that remembereth

54:24.ar: فَقَالُوٓاْ أَبَشَرࣰ ا مِّنَّا وَٰحِدࣰ ا نَّتَّبِعُهُۥٓ إِنَّآ إِذࣰ ا لَّفِي ضَلَٰلࣲ وَسُعُرٍ
54:24.en: For they said; Is it a mortal man, alone among us, that we are to follow? Then indeed we should fall into error and madness

54:25.ar: أَءُلۡقِيَ ٱلذِّكۡرُ عَلَيۡهِ مِنۢ بَيۡنِنَا بَلۡ هُوَ كَذَّابٌ أَشِرࣱ‏
54:25.en: Hath the remembrance been given unto him alone among us? Nay, but he is a rash liar

54:26.ar: سَيَعۡلَمُونَ غَدࣰ ا مَّنِ ٱلۡكَذَّابُ ٱلۡأَشِرُ
54:26.en: (Unto their warner it was said): To-morrow they will know who is the rash liar

54:27.ar: إِنَّا مُرۡسِلُواْ ٱلنَّاقَةِ فِتۡنَةࣰ لَّهُمۡ فَٱرۡتَقِبۡهُمۡ وَٱصۡطَبِرۡ
54:27.en: Lo! We are sending the she-camel as a test for them; so watch them and have patience

54:28.ar: وَنَبِّئۡهُمۡ أَنَّ ٱلۡمَآءَ قِسۡمَةُۢ بَيۡنَهُمۡۖ كُلُّ شِرۡبࣲ مُّحۡتَضَرࣱ‏
54:28.en: And inform them that the water is to be shared between (her and) them. Every drinking will be witnessed

54:29.en: But they call their comrade and he took and hamstrung (her)

54:30.en: Then see how (dreadful) was My punishment after My warnings

54:31.ar: إِنَّآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ صَيۡحَةࣰ وَٰحِدَةࣰ فَكَانُواْ كَهَشِيمِ ٱلۡمُحۡتَظِرِ
54:31.en: Lo! We sent upon them one Shout, and they became as the dry twigs (rejected by) the builder of a cattle-fold

54:32.ar: وَلَقَدۡ يَسَّرۡنَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ لِلذِّكۡرِ فَهَلۡ مِن مُّدَّكِرࣲ‏
54:32.en: And in truth We have made the Qur'an easy to remember; but is there any that remembereth

54:33.en: The folk of Lot rejected warnings

54:34.ar: إِنَّآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ حَاصِبًا إِلَّآ ءَالَ لُوطࣲۖ نَّجَّيۡنَٰهُم بِسَحَرࣲ‏
54:34.en: Lo! We sent a storm of stones upon them (all) save the family of Lot, whom We rescued in the last watch of the night

54:35.ar: نِّعۡمَةࣰ مِّنۡ عِندِنَاۚ كَذَٰلِكَ نَجۡزِي مَن شَكَرَ
54:35.en: As grace from Us. Thus We reward him who giveth thanks

54:36.en: And he indeed had warned them of Our blow, but they did doubt the warnings

54:37.ar: وَلَقَدۡ رَٰوَدُوهُ عَن ضَيۡفِهِۦ فَطَمَسۡنَآ أَعۡيُنَهُمۡ فَذُوقُواْ عَذَابِي وَنُذُرِ
54:37.en: They even asked of him his guests for an ill purpose. Then We blinded their eyes (and said): Taste now My punishment after My warnings

54:38.en: And in truth the punishment decreed befell them early in the morning

54:39.en: Now taste My punishment after My warnings

54:40.ar: وَلَقَدۡ يَسَّرۡنَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ لِلذِّكۡرِ فَهَلۡ مِن مُّدَّكِرࣲ‏
54:40.en: And in truth We have made the Qur'an easy to remember; but is there any that remembereth

54:41.en: And warnings came in truth unto the house of Pharaoh

54:42.ar: كَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا كُلِّهَا فَأَخَذۡنَٰهُمۡ أَخۡذَ عَزِيزࣲ مُّقۡتَدِرٍ
54:42.en: Who denied Our revelations, every one. Therefore We grasped them with the grasp of the Mighty, the Powerful

54:43.ar: أَكُفَّارُكُمۡ خَيۡرࣱ مِّنۡ أُوْلَٰٓئِكُمۡ أَمۡ لَكُم بَرَآءَةࣱ فِي ٱلزُّبُرِ
54:43.en: Are your disbelievers better than those, or have ye some immunity in the scriptures

54:44.en: Or say they: We are a host victorious

54:45.en: The hosts will all be routed and will turn and flee

54:46.ar: بَلِ ٱلسَّاعَةُ مَوۡعِدُهُمۡ وَٱلسَّاعَةُ أَدۡهَىٰ وَأَمَرُّ
54:46.en: Nay, but the Hour (of doom) is their appointed tryst, and the Hour will be more wretched and more bitter (than their earthly failure)

54:47.en: Lo! the guilty are in error and madness

54:48.ar: يَوۡمَ يُسۡحَبُونَ فِي ٱلنَّارِ عَلَىٰ وُجُوهِهِمۡ ذُوقُواْ مَسَّ سَقَرَ
54:48.en: On the day when they are dragged into the Fire upon their faces (it is said unto them): Feel the touch of hell

54:49.en: Lo! We have created every thing by measure

54:50.ar: وَمَآ أَمۡرُنَآ إِلَّا وَٰحِدَةࣱ كَلَمۡحِۭ بِٱلۡبَصَرِ
54:50.en: And Our commandment is but one (commandment), as the twinkling of an eye

54:51.ar: وَلَقَدۡ أَهۡلَكۡنَآ أَشۡيَاعَكُمۡ فَهَلۡ مِن مُّدَّكِرࣲ‏
54:51.en: And verily We have destroyed your fellows; but is there any that remembereth

54:52.en: And every thing they did is in the scriptures

54:53.en: And every small and great thing is recorded

54:54.en: Lo! the righteous will dwell among gardens and rivers

54:55.ar: فِي مَقۡعَدِ صِدۡقٍ عِندَ مَلِيكࣲ مُّقۡتَدِرِۭ
54:55.en: Firmly established in the favour of a Mighty King

55:5.en: The sun and the moon are made punctual

55:6.en: The stars and the trees prostrate

55:7.en: And the sky He hath uplifted; and He hath set the measure

55:8.en: That ye exceed not the measure

55:9.ar: وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلۡوَزۡنَ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِ وَلَا تُخۡسِرُواْ ٱلۡمِيزَانَ
55:9.en: But observe the measure strictly, nor fall short thereof

55:10.en: And the earth hath He appointed for (His) creatures

55:11.en: Wherein are fruit and sheathed palm-trees

55:13.en: Which is it, of the favours of your Lord, that ye deny

55:14.en: He created man of clay like the potter's

55:15.ar: وَخَلَقَ ٱلۡجَآنَّ مِن مَّارِجࣲ مِّن نَّارࣲ‏
55:15.en: And the jinn did He create of smokeless fire

55:16.en: Which is it, of the favours of your Lord, that ye deny

55:17.en: Lord of the two Easts, and Lord of the two Wests

55:18.en: Which is it, of the favours of your Lord, that ye deny

55:19.en: He hath loosed the two seas. They meet

55:20.en: There is a barrier between them. They encroach not (one upon the other)

55:21.en: Which is it, of the favours of your Lord, that ye deny

55:22.en: There cometh forth from both of them the pearl and coral-stone

55:23.en: Which is it, of the favours of your Lord, that ye deny

55:24.ar: وَلَهُ ٱلۡجَوَارِ ٱلۡمُنشَـَٔاتُ فِي ٱلۡبَحۡرِ كَٱلۡأَعۡلَٰمِ
55:24.en: His are the ships displayed upon the sea, like banners

55:25.en: Which is it, of the favours of your Lord, that ye deny

55:26.en: Everyone that is thereon will pass away

55:27.ar: وَيَبۡقَىٰ وَجۡهُ رَبِّكَ ذُو ٱلۡجَلَٰلِ وَٱلۡإِكۡرَامِ
55:27.en: There remaineth but the Countenance of thy Lord of Might and Glory

55:28.en: Which is it, of the favours of your Lord, that ye deny

55:29.ar: يَسۡـَٔلُهُۥ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ كُلَّ يَوۡمٍ هُوَ فِي شَأۡنࣲ‏
55:29.en: All that are in the heavens and the earth entreat Him. Every day He exerciseth (universal) power

55:30.en: Which is it, of the favours of your Lord, that ye deny

55:31.en: We shall dispose of you, O ye two dependents (man and jinn)

55:32.en: Which is it, of the favours of your Lord, that ye deny

55:33.ar: يَٰمَعۡشَرَ ٱلۡجِنِّ وَٱلۡإِنسِ إِنِ ٱسۡتَطَعۡتُمۡ أَن تَنفُذُواْ مِنۡ أَقۡطَارِ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَٱنفُذُواْۚ لَا تَنفُذُونَ إِلَّا بِسُلۡطَٰنࣲ‏
55:33.en: O company of jinn and men, if ye have power to penetrate (all) regions of the heavens and the earth, then penetrate (them)! Ye will never penetrate them save with (Our) sanction

55:34.en: Which is it, of the favours of your Lord, that ye deny

55:35.ar: يُرۡسَلُ عَلَيۡكُمَا شُوَاظࣱ مِّن نَّارࣲ وَنُحَاسࣱ فَلَا تَنتَصِرَانِ
55:35.en: There will be sent, against you both, heat of fire and flash of brass, and ye will not escape

55:36.en: Which is it, of the favours of your Lord, that ye deny

55:37.ar: فَإِذَا ٱنشَقَّتِ ٱلسَّمَآءُ فَكَانَتۡ وَرۡدَةࣰ كَٱلدِّهَانِ
55:37.en: And when the heaven splitteth asunder and becometh rosy like red hide

55:38.en: Which is it, of the favours of your Lord, that ye deny

55:39.ar: فَيَوۡمَئِذࣲ لَّا يُسۡـَٔلُ عَن ذَنۢبِهِۦٓ إِنسࣱ وَلَا جَآنࣱّ‏
55:39.en: On that day neither man nor jinni will be questioned of his sin

55:40.en: Which is it, of the favours of your Lord, that ye deny

55:41.ar: يُعۡرَفُ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمُونَ بِسِيمَٰهُمۡ فَيُؤۡخَذُ بِٱلنَّوَٰصِي وَٱلۡأَقۡدَامِ
55:41.en: The guilty will be known by their marks, and will be taken by the forelocks and the feet

55:42.en: Which is it, of the favours of your Lord, that ye deny

55:43.ar: هَٰذِهِۦ جَهَنَّمُ ٱلَّتِي يُكَذِّبُ بِهَا ٱلۡمُجۡرِمُونَ
55:43.en: This is hell which the guilty deny

55:44.en: They go circling round between it and fierce, boiling water

55:45.en: Which is it, of the favours of your Lord, that ye deny

55:46.en: But for him who feareth the standing before his Lord there are two gardens

55:47.en: Which is it, of the favours of your Lord, that ye deny

55:49.en: Which is it, of the favours of your Lord, that ye deny

55:51.en: Which is it, of the favours of your Lord, that ye deny

55:52.en: Wherein is every kind of fruit in pairs

55:53.en: Which is it, of the favours of your Lord, that ye deny

55:54.ar: مُتَّكِـِٔينَ عَلَىٰ فُرُشِۭ بَطَآئِنُهَا مِنۡ إِسۡتَبۡرَقࣲۚ وَجَنَى ٱلۡجَنَّتَيۡنِ دَانࣲ‏
55:54.en: Reclining upon couches lined with silk brocade, the fruit of both the gardens near to hand

55:55.en: Which is it, of the favours of your Lord, that ye deny

55:56.ar: فِيهِنَّ قَٰصِرَٰتُ ٱلطَّرۡفِ لَمۡ يَطۡمِثۡهُنَّ إِنسࣱ قَبۡلَهُمۡ وَلَا جَآنࣱّ‏
55:56.en: Therein are those of modest gaze, whom neither man nor jinni will have touched before them

55:57.en: Which is it, of the favours of your Lord, that ye deny

55:58.en: (In beauty) like the jacynth and the coral-stone

55:59.en: Which is it, of the favours of your Lord, that ye deny

55:60.en: Is the reward of goodness aught save goodness

55:61.en: Which is it, of the favours of your Lord, that ye deny

55:62.en: And beside them are two other gardens

wylB_W3bC2E.speaker: adnan
wylB_W3bC2E.speaker_note: his daily surah-summary series at MWN; continues the cluster from his previous session
wylB_W3bC2E.title: Surat Al-Qamar and Ar-Rahman Summaries
wylB_W3bC2E.one_line: Al-Qamar shows gifts like guidance turning into curses when misused; Ar-Rahman counts blessings and asks us to keep the balance.
wylB_W3bC2E.summary: He pairs two surahs as two sides of one idea. Al-Qamar shows how what Allah gives can become a curse, and Ar-Rahman shows blessings that stay blessings when met with gratitude. He reads the splitting of the moon as an event of the Last Day, calling the narrations placing it in the Prophet's lifetime disputed. The disbelievers dismiss every sign as passing magic, and nation after nation, the people of Nuh, Ad, Thamud, Lut and Pharaoh, refuse their prophets until the gift of guidance becomes the cause of their ruin. The refrain that the Quran is made easy for remembrance is a question to us: the Quran will either testify for us or against us. Since everything is created by measure, events reach us unlabelled; Allah makes them easy or hard, but we hold the label of good or bad in our own hands. Ar-Rahman, a soothing surah of repeated questions about Allah's favours, begins with the Most Merciful teaching the Quran and the power of expression, then commands that the balance not be violated. Among the descriptions of the two gardens he highlights the verse that the reward of excellence is excellence. Receiving so much while giving nothing back breaks the balance, so use blessings properly and keep them blessings.

outline.heading: Two surahs, two sides of one concept
outline.gist: Al-Qamar shows blessings turning into curses; Ar-Rahman shows blessings kept through gratitude.

outline.heading: Why the pair is so loved; the Hour draws near
outline.gist: He explains the balance between the two surahs and why Ar-Rahman is soothing, then begins Al-Qamar.

outline.heading: The splitting of the moon
outline.gist: He prefers reading it as an event of the Last Day over disputed narrations placing it in the Prophet's lifetime; they call every sign passing magic.

outline.heading: Enough warnings, yet denial
outline.gist: They were given enough stories and wisdom to deter them, but warnings do not help those who will not listen.

outline.heading: How were My punishment and My warnings?
outline.gist: The refrain after each nation: guidance offered and refused becomes a curse upon them.

outline.heading: The Quran made easy for remembrance
outline.gist: Repeated after each story as a question: will anyone take the Quran as a reminder?

outline.heading: The Quran testifies for you or against you
outline.gist: The same gift can be a blessing or the reason for punishment, depending on how it is used.

outline.heading: Interlude
Rising from the graves; the people of Nuh
outline.gist: A scene of people hurrying from their graves, then Nuh's call for help and the flood.

outline.heading: Ad, Thamud, Lut and Pharaoh
outline.gist: Every nation the surah mentions was punished after refusing its prophet; not every nation in the Quran was, but these turned their gift into a curse.

outline.heading: Are your disbelievers better than those?
outline.gist: Quraysh are no stronger than earlier nations; their crowd will be routed and the Hour is worse.

outline.heading: Everything created by measure
outline.gist: What Allah gives has a destiny and a purpose; used well it is a blessing, used badly a curse.

outline.heading: You hold the labelling device
outline.gist: Events come unlabelled; Allah makes them easy or hard, but we decide whether they become good or bad.

outline.heading: Everything recorded; the seat of truth
outline.gist: Small and large deeds are written; the pious are in gardens and rivers in a seat of truth.

outline.heading: From denial to honesty with oneself
outline.gist: The surah opens with denial and ends with the pious in a place of truth because they were honest with themselves.

outline.heading: Interlude
Ar-Rahman and its soothing refrain
outline.gist: Which of your Lord's favours will you deny, addressed to jinn and humans; the comforting name ar-Rahman.

outline.heading: Taught the Quran, created man, taught him expression
outline.gist: What makes humans unique; sun, stars and trees all follow Allah's system.

outline.heading: Do not transgress the balance
outline.gist: Weigh things fairly and give each its due; Al-Qamar warned about curses, Ar-Rahman encourages blessings.

outline.heading: Two seas and the barrier; even death is a favour
outline.gist: The counting of favours; everything perishes but the Face of your Lord remains, so even the end is a blessing.

outline.heading: Every surah balances warning and reward
outline.gist: Brief talk of the criminals known by their marks, then two gardens for whoever fears standing before his Lord.

outline.heading: The delights of the gardens, and the lower pair
outline.gist: Springs, fruit and couches; even those of lesser deeds receive gardens.

outline.heading: Is the reward of excellence anything but excellence?
outline.gist: Allah gave beyond what we asked or deserve, so our response must be excellence; show it once and He shows it to you twice.

outline.heading: Keep the scales: receiving requires giving
outline.gist: Receiving blessings while giving nothing back and making no effort kills the balance.

outline.heading: One concept, two tones
outline.gist: Al-Qamar is heavy with warnings, Ar-Rahman is gentle, but both teach handling Allah's gifts with balance.

outline.heading: Interlude
Outro

themes.label: Gratitude (shukr) and appreciation
themes.note: Allah's gifts become blessings or curses depending on how we use them and whether we show gratitude.

themes.label: Relationship with the Quran: reading, reflecting, living it
themes.note: The Quran is made easy for remembrance, and will testify for or against us.

themes.label: Stories of earlier prophets
themes.note: The nations of Nuh, Hud, Salih, Lut and Musa turned the gift of guidance into their ruin.

themes.label: Agency, responsibility and rejecting victim mentality
themes.note: Events come unlabelled; we decide whether they become good or bad.

themes.label: Self-honesty and self-accountability (muhasabah)
themes.note: The pious reach a seat of truth because they were honest with themselves.

themes.label: The Names and Attributes of Allah
themes.note: Ar-Rahman as a comforting name full of mercy.

themes.label: Moderation and balance (wasatiyyah)
themes.note: Do not transgress the balance; keep the scale fair.

themes.label: Ihsan and excellence in worship
themes.note: The reward of excellence is excellence: answer Allah's generosity with your own effort.

hadith.gist: Narrations that the moon split during the Prophet's lifetime, which he treats as disputed
The Quran is a proof for you or against you

maxims: What happens to you does not come stamped good or bad.
You carry the labelling device in your own hand.
Show excellence once and Allah shows it to you twice.

stories.who: The people of Nuh, Ad, Thamud, Lut and Pharaoh
stories.point: Each refused its prophet, so the gift of guidance became the cause of its destruction.

takeaways: Use the Quran as a reminder so it testifies for you, not against you.
Judge events by how you respond, not by whether they feel easy or hard.
Keep the balance: give back in proportion to the blessings you receive.
Answer Allah's generosity with excellence in your own work and worship.

46:2.ar: تَنزِيلُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلۡعَزِيزِ ٱلۡحَكِيمِ
46:2.en: The revelation of the Scripture is from Allah the Mighty, the Wise

46:3.ar: مَا خَلَقۡنَا ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَمَا بَيۡنَهُمَآ إِلَّا بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَأَجَلࣲ مُّسَمࣰّ ىۚ وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ عَمَّآ أُنذِرُواْ مُعۡرِضُونَ
46:3.en: We created not the heavens and the earth and all that is between them save with truth, and for a term appointed. But those who disbelieve turn away from that whereof they are warned

46:4.ar: قُلۡ أَرَءَيۡتُم مَّا تَدۡعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَرُونِي مَاذَا خَلَقُواْ مِنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ أَمۡ لَهُمۡ شِرۡكࣱ فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِۖ ٱئۡتُونِي بِكِتَٰبࣲ مِّن قَبۡلِ هَٰذَآ أَوۡ أَثَٰرَةࣲ مِّنۡ عِلۡمٍ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
46:4.en: Say (unto them, O Muhammad): Have ye thought on all that ye invoke beside Allah? Show me what they have created of the earth. Or have they any portion in the heavens? Bring me a scripture before this (Scripture), or some vestige of knowledge (in support of what ye say), if ye are truthful

46:5.ar: وَمَنۡ أَضَلُّ مِمَّن يَدۡعُواْ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَن لَّا يَسۡتَجِيبُ لَهُۥٓ إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ وَهُمۡ عَن دُعَآئِهِمۡ غَٰفِلُونَ
46:5.en: And who is further astray than those who, instead of Allah, pray unto such as hear not their prayer until the Day of Resurrection, and are unconscious of their prayer

46:6.ar: وَإِذَا حُشِرَ ٱلنَّاسُ كَانُواْ لَهُمۡ أَعۡدَآءࣰ وَكَانُواْ بِعِبَادَتِهِمۡ كَٰفِرِينَ
46:6.en: And when mankind are gathered (to the Judgment) will become enemies for them, and will become deniers of having been worshipped

46:7.ar: وَإِذَا تُتۡلَىٰ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَايَٰتُنَا بَيِّنَٰتࣲ قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لِلۡحَقِّ لَمَّا جَآءَهُمۡ هَٰذَا سِحۡرࣱ مُّبِينٌ
46:7.en: And when Our clear revelations are recited unto them, those who disbelieve say of the Truth when it reacheth them: This is mere magic

46:8.ar: أَمۡ يَقُولُونَ ٱفۡتَرَىٰهُۖ قُلۡ إِنِ ٱفۡتَرَيۡتُهُۥ فَلَا تَمۡلِكُونَ لِي مِنَ ٱللَّهِ شَيۡـًٔاۖ هُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَا تُفِيضُونَ فِيهِۚ كَفَىٰ بِهِۦ شَهِيدَۢا بَيۡنِي وَبَيۡنَكُمۡۖ وَهُوَ ٱلۡغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
46:8.en: Or say they: He hath invented it? Say (O Muhammad): If I have invented it, still ye have no power to support me against Allah. He is Best Aware of what ye say among yourselves concerning it. He sufficeth for a witness between me and you. And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful

46:9.ar: قُلۡ مَا كُنتُ بِدۡعࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلرُّسُلِ وَمَآ أَدۡرِي مَا يُفۡعَلُ بِي وَلَا بِكُمۡۖ إِنۡ أَتَّبِعُ إِلَّا مَا يُوحَىٰٓ إِلَيَّ وَمَآ أَنَا۠ إِلَّا نَذِيرࣱ مُّبِينࣱ‏
46:9.en: Say: I am no new thing among the messengers (of Allah), nor know I what will be done with me or with you. I do but follow that which is inspired in me, and I am but a plain warner

46:10.ar: قُلۡ أَرَءَيۡتُمۡ إِن كَانَ مِنۡ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ وَكَفَرۡتُم بِهِۦ وَشَهِدَ شَاهِدࣱ مِّنۢ بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ عَلَىٰ مِثۡلِهِۦ فَـَٔامَنَ وَٱسۡتَكۡبَرۡتُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهۡدِي ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
46:10.en: Bethink you: If it is from Allah and ye disbelieve therein, and a witness of the Children of Israel hath already testified to the like thereof and hath believed, and ye are too proud (what plight is yours)? Lo! Allah guideth not wrong-doing folk

46:11.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَوۡ كَانَ خَيۡرࣰ ا مَّا سَبَقُونَآ إِلَيۡهِۚ وَإِذۡ لَمۡ يَهۡتَدُواْ بِهِۦ فَسَيَقُولُونَ هَٰذَآ إِفۡكࣱ قَدِيمࣱ‏
46:11.en: And those who disbelieve say of those who believe: If it had been (any) good, they would not have been before us in attaining it. And since they will not be guided by it, they say: This is an ancient lie

46:12.ar: وَمِن قَبۡلِهِۦ كِتَٰبُ مُوسَىٰٓ إِمَامࣰ ا وَرَحۡمَةࣰۚ وَهَٰذَا كِتَٰبࣱ مُّصَدِّقࣱ لِّسَانًا عَرَبِيࣰّ ا لِّيُنذِرَ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ وَبُشۡرَىٰ لِلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
46:12.en: When before it there was the Scripture of Moses, an example and a mercy; and this is a confirming Scripture in the Arabic language, that it may warn those who do wrong and bring good tidings for the righteous

46:13.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُواْ رَبُّنَا ٱللَّهُ ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَقَٰمُواْ فَلَا خَوۡفٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَلَا هُمۡ يَحۡزَنُونَ
46:13.en: Lo! those who say: Our Lord is Allah, and thereafter walk aright, there shall no fear come upon them neither shall they grieve

46:14.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ أَصۡحَٰبُ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا جَزَآءَۢ بِمَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
46:14.en: Such are rightful owners of the Garden, immortal therein, as a reward for what they used to do

46:15.ar: وَوَصَّيۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ بِوَٰلِدَيۡهِ إِحۡسَٰنًاۖ حَمَلَتۡهُ أُمُّهُۥ كُرۡهࣰ ا وَوَضَعَتۡهُ كُرۡهࣰ اۖ وَحَمۡلُهُۥ وَفِصَٰلُهُۥ ثَلَٰثُونَ شَهۡرًاۚ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُۥ وَبَلَغَ أَرۡبَعِينَ سَنَةࣰ قَالَ رَبِّ أَوۡزِعۡنِيٓ أَنۡ أَشۡكُرَ نِعۡمَتَكَ ٱلَّتِيٓ أَنۡعَمۡتَ عَلَيَّ وَعَلَىٰ وَٰلِدَيَّ وَأَنۡ أَعۡمَلَ صَٰلِحࣰ ا تَرۡضَىٰهُ وَأَصۡلِحۡ لِي فِي ذُرِّيَّتِيٓۖ إِنِّي تُبۡتُ إِلَيۡكَ وَإِنِّي مِنَ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ
46:15.en: And We have commended unto man kindness toward parents. His mother beareth him with reluctance, and bringeth him forth with reluctance, and the bearing of him and the weaning of him is thirty months, till, when he attaineth full strength and reacheth forty years, he saith: My Lord! Arouse me that I may give thanks for the favour wherewith Thou hast favoured me and my parents, and that I may do right acceptable unto Thee. And be gracious unto me in the matter of my seed. Lo! I have turned unto Thee repentant, and lo! I am of those who surrender (unto Thee)

46:16.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ نَتَقَبَّلُ عَنۡهُمۡ أَحۡسَنَ مَا عَمِلُواْ وَنَتَجَاوَزُ عَن سَيِّـَٔاتِهِمۡ فِيٓ أَصۡحَٰبِ ٱلۡجَنَّةِۖ وَعۡدَ ٱلصِّدۡقِ ٱلَّذِي كَانُواْ يُوعَدُونَ
46:16.en: Those are they from whom We accept the best of what they do, and overlook their evil deeds. (They are) among the owners of the Garden. This is the true promise which they were promised (in the world)

46:17.ar: وَٱلَّذِي قَالَ لِوَٰلِدَيۡهِ أُفࣲّ لَّكُمَآ أَتَعِدَانِنِيٓ أَنۡ أُخۡرَجَ وَقَدۡ خَلَتِ ٱلۡقُرُونُ مِن قَبۡلِي وَهُمَا يَسۡتَغِيثَانِ ٱللَّهَ وَيۡلَكَ ءَامِنۡ إِنَّ وَعۡدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقࣱّ فَيَقُولُ مَا هَٰذَآ إِلَّآ أَسَٰطِيرُ ٱلۡأَوَّلِينَ
46:17.en: And whoso saith unto his parents: Fie upon you both! Do ye threaten me that I shall be brought forth (again) when generations before me have passed away? And they twain cry unto Allah for help (and say): Woe unto thee! Believe! Lo! the promise of Allah is true. But he saith: This is naught save fables of the men of old

46:18.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ حَقَّ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡقَوۡلُ فِيٓ أُمَمࣲ قَدۡ خَلَتۡ مِن قَبۡلِهِم مِّنَ ٱلۡجِنِّ وَٱلۡإِنسِۖ إِنَّهُمۡ كَانُواْ خَٰسِرِينَ
46:18.en: Such are those on whom the Word concerning nations of the jinn and mankind which have passed away before them hath effect. Lo! they are the losers

46:19.ar: وَلِكُلࣲّ دَرَجَٰتࣱ مِّمَّا عَمِلُواْۖ وَلِيُوَفِّيَهُمۡ أَعۡمَٰلَهُمۡ وَهُمۡ لَا يُظۡلَمُونَ
46:19.en: And for all there will be ranks from what they do, that He may pay them for their deeds; and they will not be wronged

46:20.ar: وَيَوۡمَ يُعۡرَضُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ عَلَى ٱلنَّارِ أَذۡهَبۡتُمۡ طَيِّبَٰتِكُمۡ فِي حَيَاتِكُمُ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَٱسۡتَمۡتَعۡتُم بِهَا فَٱلۡيَوۡمَ تُجۡزَوۡنَ عَذَابَ ٱلۡهُونِ بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَسۡتَكۡبِرُونَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ بِغَيۡرِ ٱلۡحَقِّ وَبِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَفۡسُقُونَ
46:20.en: And on the day when those who disbelieve are exposed to the Fire (it will be said): Ye squandered your good things in the life of the world and sought comfort therein. Now this day ye are rewarded with the doom of ignominy because ye were disdainful in the land without a right, and because ye used to transgress

46:21.ar: ۞وَٱذۡكُرۡ أَخَا عَادٍ إِذۡ أَنذَرَ قَوۡمَهُۥ بِٱلۡأَحۡقَافِ وَقَدۡ خَلَتِ ٱلنُّذُرُ مِنۢ بَيۡنِ يَدَيۡهِ وَمِنۡ خَلۡفِهِۦٓ أَلَّا تَعۡبُدُوٓاْ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَ إِنِّيٓ أَخَافُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ عَذَابَ يَوۡمٍ عَظِيمࣲ‏
46:21.en: And make mention (O Muhammad) of the brother of A'ad when he warned his folk among the wind-curved sandhills - and verily warners came and went before and after him - saying: Serve none but Allah. Lo! I fear for you the doom of a tremendous Day

46:22.ar: قَالُوٓاْ أَجِئۡتَنَا لِتَأۡفِكَنَا عَنۡ ءَالِهَتِنَا فَأۡتِنَا بِمَا تَعِدُنَآ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ
46:22.en: They said: Hast come to turn us away from our gods? Then bring upon us that wherewith thou threatenest us, if thou art of the truthful

46:23.ar: قَالَ إِنَّمَا ٱلۡعِلۡمُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَأُبَلِّغُكُم مَّآ أُرۡسِلۡتُ بِهِۦ وَلَٰكِنِّيٓ أَرَىٰكُمۡ قَوۡمࣰ ا تَجۡهَلُونَ
46:23.en: He said: The knowledge is with Allah only. I convey unto you that wherewith I have been sent, but I see you are a folk that know not

46:24.ar: فَلَمَّا رَأَوۡهُ عَارِضࣰ ا مُّسۡتَقۡبِلَ أَوۡدِيَتِهِمۡ قَالُواْ هَٰذَا عَارِضࣱ مُّمۡطِرُنَاۚ بَلۡ هُوَ مَا ٱسۡتَعۡجَلۡتُم بِهِۦۖ رِيحࣱ فِيهَا عَذَابٌ أَلِيمࣱ‏
46:24.en: Then, when they beheld it as a dense cloud coming toward their valleys, they said: Here is a cloud bringing us rain. Nay, but it is that which ye did seek to hasten, a wind wherein is painful torment

46:25.ar: تُدَمِّرُ كُلَّ شَيۡءِۭ بِأَمۡرِ رَبِّهَا فَأَصۡبَحُواْ لَا يُرَىٰٓ إِلَّا مَسَٰكِنُهُمۡۚ كَذَٰلِكَ نَجۡزِي ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمِينَ
46:25.en: Destroying all things by commandment of its Lord. And morning found them so that naught could be seen save their dwellings. Thus do We reward the guilty folk

46:26.ar: وَلَقَدۡ مَكَّنَّٰهُمۡ فِيمَآ إِن مَّكَّنَّٰكُمۡ فِيهِ وَجَعَلۡنَا لَهُمۡ سَمۡعࣰ ا وَأَبۡصَٰرࣰ ا وَأَفۡـِٔدَةࣰ فَمَآ أَغۡنَىٰ عَنۡهُمۡ سَمۡعُهُمۡ وَلَآ أَبۡصَٰرُهُمۡ وَلَآ أَفۡـِٔدَتُهُم مِّن شَيۡءٍ إِذۡ كَانُواْ يَجۡحَدُونَ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ وَحَاقَ بِهِم مَّا كَانُواْ بِهِۦ يَسۡتَهۡزِءُونَ
46:26.en: And verily We had empowered them with that wherewith We have not empowered you, and had assigned them ears and eyes and hearts; but their ears and eyes and hearts availed them naught since they denied the revelations of Allah; and what they used to mock befell them

46:27.ar: وَلَقَدۡ أَهۡلَكۡنَا مَا حَوۡلَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡقُرَىٰ وَصَرَّفۡنَا ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَرۡجِعُونَ
46:27.en: And verily We have destroyed townships round about you, and displayed (for them) Our revelation, that haply they might return

46:28.ar: فَلَوۡلَا نَصَرَهُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُواْ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ قُرۡبَانًا ءَالِهَةَۢۖ بَلۡ ضَلُّواْ عَنۡهُمۡۚ وَذَٰلِكَ إِفۡكُهُمۡ وَمَا كَانُواْ يَفۡتَرُونَ
46:28.en: Then why did those whom they had chosen for gods as a way of approach (unto Allah) not help them? Nay, but they did fail them utterly. And (all) that was their lie, and what they used to invent

46:29.ar: وَإِذۡ صَرَفۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَ نَفَرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡجِنِّ يَسۡتَمِعُونَ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ فَلَمَّا حَضَرُوهُ قَالُوٓاْ أَنصِتُواْۖ فَلَمَّا قُضِيَ وَلَّوۡاْ إِلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِم مُّنذِرِينَ
46:29.en: And when We inclined toward thee (Muhammad) certain of the jinn, who wished to hear the Qur'an and, when they were in its presence, said: Give ear! and, when it was finished, turned back to their people, warning

46:30.ar: قَالُواْ يَٰقَوۡمَنَآ إِنَّا سَمِعۡنَا كِتَٰبًا أُنزِلَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مُوسَىٰ مُصَدِّقࣰ ا لِّمَا بَيۡنَ يَدَيۡهِ يَهۡدِيٓ إِلَى ٱلۡحَقِّ وَإِلَىٰ طَرِيقࣲ مُّسۡتَقِيمࣲ‏
46:30.en: They said: O our people! Lo! we have heard a scripture which hath been revealed after Moses, confirming that which was before it, guiding unto the truth and a right road

46:31.ar: يَٰقَوۡمَنَآ أَجِيبُواْ دَاعِيَ ٱللَّهِ وَءَامِنُواْ بِهِۦ يَغۡفِرۡ لَكُم مِّن ذُنُوبِكُمۡ وَيُجِرۡكُم مِّنۡ عَذَابٍ أَلِيمࣲ‏
46:31.en: O our people! respond to Allah's summoner and believe in Him. He will forgive you some of your sins and guard you from a painful doom

46:32.ar: وَمَن لَّا يُجِبۡ دَاعِيَ ٱللَّهِ فَلَيۡسَ بِمُعۡجِزࣲ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَيۡسَ لَهُۥ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ أَوۡلِيَآءُۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ فِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينٍ
46:32.en: And whoso respondeth not to Allah's summoner he can nowise escape in the earth, and he hath no protecting friends instead of Him. Such are in error manifest

46:33.ar: أَوَلَمۡ يَرَوۡاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَلَمۡ يَعۡيَ بِخَلۡقِهِنَّ بِقَٰدِرٍ عَلَىٰٓ أَن يُحۡـِۧيَ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰۚ بَلَىٰٓۚ إِنَّهُۥ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ‏
46:33.en: Have they not seen that Allah, Who created the heavens and the earth and was not wearied by their creation, is Able to give life to the dead? Aye, He verily is Able to do all things

46:34.ar: وَيَوۡمَ يُعۡرَضُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ عَلَى ٱلنَّارِ أَلَيۡسَ هَٰذَا بِٱلۡحَقِّۖ قَالُواْ بَلَىٰ وَرَبِّنَاۚ قَالَ فَذُوقُواْ ٱلۡعَذَابَ بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَكۡفُرُونَ
46:34.en: And on the day when those who disbelieve are exposed to the Fire (they will be asked): Is not this real? They will say: Yea, by our Lord. He will say: Then taste the doom for that ye disbelieved

46:35.ar: فَٱصۡبِرۡ كَمَا صَبَرَ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡعَزۡمِ مِنَ ٱلرُّسُلِ وَلَا تَسۡتَعۡجِل لَّهُمۡۚ كَأَنَّهُمۡ يَوۡمَ يَرَوۡنَ مَا يُوعَدُونَ لَمۡ يَلۡبَثُوٓاْ إِلَّا سَاعَةࣰ مِّن نَّهَارِۭۚ بَلَٰغࣱۚ فَهَلۡ يُهۡلَكُ إِلَّا ٱلۡقَوۡمُ ٱلۡفَٰسِقُونَ
46:35.en: Then have patience (O Muhammad) even as the stout of heart among the messengers (of old) had patience, and seek not to hasten on (the doom) for them. On the day when they see that which they are promised (it will seem to them) as though they had tarried but an hour of daylight. A clear message. Shall any be destroyed save evil-living folk

BxO5Q_t0cEI.speaker: adnan
BxO5Q_t0cEI.speaker_note: his own surah-summary series; English explanation with an Arabic recap of each part
BxO5Q_t0cEI.title: Surat Al-Ahqaf Summary
BxO5Q_t0cEI.one_line: Al-Ahqaf closes the Ha-Mim cluster with a law: do your job fully and leave results to Allah, shown through parenting, 'Ad and the jinn.
BxO5Q_t0cEI.summary: Al-Ahqaf is the last surah of the Ha-Mim cluster and states a law everyone serving the deen must absorb: results are not in our hands. We cannot know why one people responds and another does not, so our task is to do what Allah commanded as well as we can and leave the rest to Him. The Prophet is told to argue well with the idolaters, yet they refuse with a flimsy excuse: had it been good, these believers would not have reached it first. Those who say our Lord is Allah and then stand firm have nothing to fear. He warns against turning this law into an excuse for failure when one has not truly done one's part. The first example is parenthood: two children raised by caring parents, one reaching forty grateful and righteous, the other scornful of his parents' pleading. No one knows why; parents can only give time, love, education and care. Each has degrees according to deeds, and we do not even know the outcome for the disbeliever. Then 'Ad, sheltered by vast crescent dunes, had every reason to believe, mistook the punishing cloud for rain and perished, while jinn who overheard the Quran believed without being invited. The surah ends by commanding patience like the resolute messengers and no hurry for people to respond.

outline.heading: Opening
The theme: do your job, results are not yours
outline.gist: We cannot know whether people will respond to the good we do; our part is the work.

outline.heading: The Prophet debates them properly, and still they refuse
outline.gist: He is told to challenge them: show what your idols created, bring a scripture or trace of knowledge; he is no novelty among messengers.

outline.heading: A flimsy excuse: they would not have beaten us to it
outline.gist: The disbelievers dismiss Islam because those who accepted it were people they looked down on.

outline.heading: Those who say our Lord is Allah and stand firm
outline.gist: The Book of Musa and this confirming Arabic Book; steadfastness, not results, removes fear and grief.

outline.heading: The cluster's final law: we do not control outcomes
outline.gist: We cannot know why some respond and others do not; we give our utmost and leave the matter to Allah.

outline.heading: Debating well and the weak excuse, restated
outline.gist: The Prophet argued in the best way and their reason for disbelief was hollow.

outline.heading: Standing firm: your task is to do your role
outline.gist: You will not be asked about results if you fulfilled what was on you.

outline.heading: Do not use this law as an excuse for failure
outline.gist: Blaming outcomes on Allah after not trying, not following His command and not using every good means is wrong.

outline.heading: Parenthood: the child who reaches forty grateful
outline.gist: He asks Allah to help him thank Him for blessings on him and his parents and to make his offspring righteous; his deeds are accepted.

outline.heading: The child who says uff to his parents
outline.gist: Same care and effort, yet he scorns their pleading; parents' work was done, the outcome is with Allah.

outline.heading: Just do your part with your children
outline.gist: Shower them with love, care and education; do not waste yourself trying to know how it will turn out.

outline.heading: Why one believes and the other does not: no one knows
outline.gist: You cannot know, but you can work: teach, guide, spend time, money and tenderness on them, and pray they turn out righteous.

outline.heading: Each has degrees according to what they did
outline.gist: Both the believer and the disbeliever have degrees; we do not know what anyone receives, so rest your head and do what is yours.

outline.heading: You used up your good things in worldly life
outline.gist: The companions feared this verse applied to them rather than reserving it for disbelievers.

outline.heading: 'Ad and the crescent dunes
outline.gist: The ahqaf were vast crescent-shaped shifting sands that 'Ad relied on as a fortress; Hud warned them.

outline.heading: The cloud they thought was rain
outline.gist: They welcomed the cloud as blessing and it was a destroying wind; we cannot know what is coming, only do what is right.

outline.heading: 'Ad were given more than Quraysh, and it did not help
outline.gist: Hearing, sight and hearts availed them nothing when they rejected the signs.

outline.heading: The jinn who believed without being invited
outline.gist: A group overheard the Quran and returned to warn their people, though the Prophet was not addressing them.

outline.heading: 'Ad versus the jinn: every reason, no reason
outline.gist: 'Ad had a brother from among them, signs and warners, yet refused; the jinn had no such reasons and believed; the outcome is Allah's.

outline.heading: Be patient like the resolute messengers
outline.gist: Do not hurry for them; on the day they see the promise, life will feel like an hour of a day.

outline.heading: Do not rush people to respond
outline.gist: Someone may ignore you for years and then surpass you; the early Arabs never imagined ruling the world in the Prophet's name.

outline.heading: The closing proclamation
outline.gist: Be patient, do not slacken or retreat, do not dictate when someone must listen; results are with Allah, the work is ours.

outline.heading: Outro

swLxwbJ4FNo.title: Surah Al-Balad Summary
swLxwbJ4FNo.one_line: Revealed after Ta'if, Al-Balad teaches that life is always hard and the real obstacle is keeping your values constant through it.
swLxwbJ4FNo.summary: He presents al-Balad as the fifth tool in his Juz Amma series: a constant value system. He sets the scene after Ta'if, when the Prophet could only re-enter Makkah under a polytheist's protection, his darkest hour. The opening oath by the sacred city, he explains, can be read as pointing out that everything in Makkah is treated as sacred except the Prophet, whose ancestors were all born there. One expects comfort, but the answer to the oaths is that every human is created in constant toil, like the liver that never stops filtering. No one's life is fine, so do not dwell on self-pity. The surah then reminds the person enjoying ease that he is seen and recorded, given eyes and a tongue, and shown two clear roads. The climax is the steep path: freeing a neck from any bondage, and feeding an orphaned relative or a destitute person on a day of hunger. Orphan and miskin stand for social and financial need. The obstacle is whether the Prophet can stay the generous person Khadijah described even now. He applies this to everyone: generosity or empathy that vanishes under pressure was never a value, and holding on to values is itself the way out of hardship.

outline.heading: Opening
Al-Balad as the fifth tool: a value system
outline.gist: After perseverance and a healthy perspective, this surah gives a constant set of values to carry through life.

outline.heading: After Ta'if: locked out of Makkah
outline.gist: Abused and stoned at Ta'if and labelled a traitor by Quraysh, the Prophet sent the young Zayd to seek a protector so he could reach his daughters and dependants.

outline.heading: Entering under al-Mut'im ibn Adi's protection
outline.gist: A Makkan leader with political ambitions granted protection without accepting Islam; the Prophet entered uneasily and the surah came to him at home.

outline.heading: The thesis: values are constant, not variable
outline.gist: The world is endless variables; if your ethics follow any of them, they are not ethics. Define your values and commit to them whatever happens.

outline.heading: The form of the oath
outline.gist: 'La uqsimu' emphasizes: I need not swear for this to be true, yet I swear by this city.

outline.heading: Haram means sacred: the lines you do not cross
outline.gist: Forbidden things are sacred boundaries protected by Allah; everything in Makkah is haram in that sense, the Prophet's ancestors were born there for generations.

outline.heading: You alone are not treated as sacred in this city
outline.gist: Of several valid readings he prefers this one: everything in Makkah is inviolable except the Prophet, who is abused and barred.

outline.heading: By every father and offspring: an apparent consolation
outline.gist: The oaths seem to soften the blow, since all his forefathers and children were born there.

outline.heading: Man is created in constant toil
outline.gist: The answer to the oaths is that every human lives in difficulty; ask anyone and no one says all is perfect.

outline.heading: Kabad and the liver
outline.gist: Like the liver that never stops filtering poisons, a person is always processing problems; do not waste time feeling sorry for yourself.

outline.heading: No one is fine, though the Prophet bore far more
outline.gist: His trials were vastly greater than ours, yet the message is that everyone struggles.

outline.heading: Why we miss childhood
outline.gist: Childhood felt simple because others carried our responsibilities; worries multiply with age.

outline.heading: Not a morale boost in his darkest hour
outline.gist: Other surahs promise him status and mercy, but here the Quran simply states that everyone is struggling.

outline.heading: Does he think no one has power over him? The Yunus parallel
outline.gist: Qadara here means to restrict or hold to account, as in Yunus, who did not think Allah would constrain him for leaving his people.

outline.heading: Boasting of spending, and the One who sees
outline.gist: The person at ease thinks nothing will change and nothing is recorded; how could the Creator who gave you eyes, a tongue and lips not see and record?

outline.heading: The two clear highways
outline.gist: Najdayn are raised, visible paths: good and its opposite; Allah gave the choice, and in ease remember your use of blessings is recorded.

outline.heading: Gathering the threads before the turn
outline.gist: Hardship is universal and deeds are recorded; now comes what you should do.

outline.heading: Iqtahama: plunge in despite fear
outline.gist: The verb means to enter with force, go all in on what you fear or feel unready for.

outline.heading: The steep path: freeing a neck
outline.gist: The obstacle is freeing a person from slavery, debt or anything that controls them.

outline.heading: Many ways to take freedom; feeding on a day of hunger
outline.gist: Slavery was among humanity's worst inventions but not the only bondage; feed others when hunger is at its worst, including your own.

outline.heading: The orphan and the destitute: social and financial need
outline.gist: The yatim symbolizes social need and the miskin financial need throughout the Quran; both deserve your money, time and affection.

outline.heading: Continue to be who you were: Khadijah's description
outline.gist: Before prophethood he freed slaves and carried the helpless, as Khadijah said; the obstacle is to keep doing it at his lowest point.

outline.heading: Is your generosity a constant or a variable?
outline.gist: You cannot give as much when you have little, but if you stop giving altogether the value was never constant.

outline.heading: Holding your values is the way out of the darkest moment
outline.gist: Values are not only to be kept through hardship; continuing to give is what gets you out of it.

outline.heading: Empathy only when it suits you?
outline.gist: Empathy is easy when life goes well; if circumstances can make you heartless and rude, your values are variable.

outline.heading: Life is never stable; only values can be
outline.gist: We keep planning for a plateau and life throws another curveball; the only stable thing is meant to be your ethics.

outline.heading: The hardest obstacle in life
outline.gist: Allah already named it the steep path and said life is always hard, so hold on to what you know is right.

outline.heading: Giving while you yourself are hungry
outline.gist: Even five percent of a little still helps someone; if you only do good when the world allows it, someone else controls your goodness.

outline.heading: Counselling patience and mercy
outline.gist: Believers since Adam urge one another to perseverance and compassion; the Prophet lived this at his lowest and Allah lifted him, and that is our way out too.

7xtVhJ-qJ84.speaker_note: continues his month-long Juz Amma series; mentions teaching children at local Islamic schools
7xtVhJ-qJ84.title: Surah Ad-Duha Summary
7xtVhJ-qJ84.one_line: Ad-Duha as a three-step remedy for distress: hold three certainties, remember how Allah rescued you, then do for others what you need.
7xtVhJ-qJ84.summary: He opens by calling the short surahs of Juz Amma concentrated pills: we recite them daily, so knowing their meaning lets each recitation reinforce an idea until it takes root. Ad-Duha came after revelation paused for months early in the dawah, while Quraysh mocked the Prophet with questions he could not answer without revelation. He stresses the surah is for distress and abandonment, not a charm for finding lost things, a practice he traced to no reliable source. The oaths by bright morning and dark night mirror how life swings, and feeling low without knowing why is normal. The first step is three certainties: your Lord has not abandoned you, what awaits in the hereafter is better than anything here, and Allah will give until you are fully satisfied, as in the narration of the most miserable person dipped once in Paradise. The second step is to recall how He sheltered, guided and provided for you, standing for social, spiritual and financial support; being in the masjid now is your most valuable possession. The third step is to go and do for others: do not mistreat the orphan, do not rebuke people who ask hard questions, and use and spread whatever blessings you were given.

outline.heading: Opening
Short yet detailed surahs as daily pills
outline.gist: Each short surah concentrates a value explained at length elsewhere; we recite them constantly in prayer, so their meaning matters.

outline.heading: Recitation reinforces ideas only if understood
outline.gist: Understood surahs root ideas in the subconscious; he used to teach children this way, and Arabic speakers miss the meaning as much as anyone.

outline.heading: Revelation pauses after the first surahs
outline.gist: After the first handful of surahs, Jibreel stopped coming, a period scholars call the slowing of revelation.

outline.heading: Selective, not secret, early dawah
outline.gist: Khadijah, Abu Bakr and others accepted; those who refused spread the word, so Quraysh knew what he claimed.

outline.heading: Months without Jibreel while Quraysh mocked
outline.gist: Questions and rumours mounted for weeks and months with only a few surahs and basic prayer revealed, and Quraysh had a field day.

outline.heading: Not allowed to answer without revelation
outline.gist: He knew more than we assume, but a messenger could not answer until revelation approved, which was exhausting to hold in.

outline.heading: Specific distress versus general tools
outline.gist: Earlier surahs gave general tools for hardship; this one tells you exactly what to do when you are at your lowest.

outline.heading: Know the meaning of your favourite surahs
outline.gist: Even if you only know three or four, know what they mean so every recitation reinforces the idea.

outline.heading: A surah for distress, not for finding lost things
outline.gist: It is for feeling abandoned and doubting everything; the cultural habit of reciting it to find lost items has no basis.

outline.heading: Oaths by the bright morning and the dark night
outline.gist: He traced the lost-items habit to one scholar's remark; the oaths mirror how life swings from bright to chaotic in a moment.

outline.heading: Feeling low without knowing why is human
outline.gist: Accumulated negativity can leave you depleted; nothing is wrong with you, and the remedy comes in three steps.

outline.heading: Certainty one: your Lord has not abandoned you
outline.gist: Whatever is happening is not because Allah stopped caring; you are not forgotten or neglected.

outline.heading: Certainty two: the hereafter is better
outline.gist: Whatever you were denied here, what is stored for you there is better beyond comparison.

outline.heading: You will wish you had not been given it here
outline.gist: Shown what was saved for you, you would prefer it over what you received in this world.

outline.heading: Certainty three: He will give until you are satisfied
outline.gist: Allah keeps asking what else you want and offering more until every pain of deprivation is remedied.

outline.heading: The greed you tamed here, unleashed there
outline.gist: Desire controlled in this life will be fulfilled until you say you want nothing more.

outline.heading: The most miserable person dipped once in Paradise
outline.gist: One moment in Paradise wipes out a lifetime of pain until he says he never saw misery.

outline.heading: Repeating the three certainties
outline.gist: Say them whenever you feel worst; that completes the first step.

outline.heading: Step two: remember how He rescued you
outline.gist: He found the Prophet orphaned, lost and poor and sheltered, guided and enriched him; count how often He did the same for you.

outline.heading: Why doubt Him now? Guidance is the greatest gift
outline.gist: He gave you carers and provision before; even if not, He brought you back to Him, and nothing is greater.

outline.heading: Being here is your most valuable possession
outline.gist: Wanting anything more than being someone who prays and comes to the masjid shows a lack of gratitude and clarity; all else is accessory.

outline.heading: Saved a hundred times before
outline.gist: Recount the times you nearly lost everything and He opened a way; one delay is no reason for bad assumptions.

outline.heading: Orphan, lost and poor: three kinds of support
outline.gist: They stand for social, spiritual and financial support; remember when you lacked each and received it.

outline.heading: Step three: do for others what you need done for you
outline.gist: The way out is not waiting or retreating but going out of your way to support others.

outline.heading: Do not mistreat the orphan
outline.gist: You were once like this; now give others the social support you received.

outline.heading: Do not rebuke the one who asks
outline.gist: Those raised in practising families take faith for granted; do not chastise lost people for questions that sound rude, pass them to someone who knows.

outline.heading: It is fine not to know every answer
outline.gist: Strong faith does not need every philosophical answer; tahdith, like hadith, means a way of life, not just words.

outline.heading: Proclaim your Lord's blessing by using and spreading it
outline.gist: Not boasting about what Allah gave you, but distributing it so others benefit, even at your worst moment.

outline.heading: Summary: the three certainties
outline.gist: Not forgotten, the hereafter is better, and He will satisfy you completely.

outline.heading: Summary: remember your history, then give
outline.gist: Recall every friend and guide He sent; doubting Him now is disrespectful; be for others what you hope they will be for you.
