iHrYNuJ1aSY.title: Surat At-Talaq and At-Tahrim Summaries
iHrYNuJ1aSY.one_line: At-Talaq as the civil law of a respectful divorce built on taqwa; at-Tahrim on marital trust, protecting families, and the decisive role of women.
iHrYNuJ1aSY.summary: He closes the 28th-juz cluster with two surahs that, unlike earlier ones, carry heavy legal content. At-Talaq treats divorce as a painful social reality whose rates in the Muslim world have caught up with everyone else. Taqwa is mentioned more densely here than anywhere in the Quran because divorce is where piety is truly tested. He argues that the verse requiring two witnesses means divorce should be a deliberate contract, not an angry outburst, and that scholars should move further in that direction. The surah obliges the husband to house and maintain his former wife, especially if pregnant or nursing, forbids harming her, and ends with a stern warning to those who ignore Allah's rulings. He pleads that children, money and the house never be used as weapons. At-Tahrim opens with the honey episode: the Prophet was told not to forbid himself something lawful to please his wives, since such deprivation harms a marriage long term. When a secret was disclosed, he raised only the breach of trust and never rubbed in the plot, a model of magnanimity. The command to protect families from the Fire is followed by four examples, all women, showing that a household and a society rise or fall with them.

outline.heading: Opening
The last two surahs of the organizing cluster carry heavy fiqh
outline.gist: Earlier surahs this year were value and creed based; these two have been used by scholars for legal rulings.

outline.heading: At-Talaq as the civil law of divorce
outline.gist: Divorce is something humanity has never agreed on how to handle, so it needs clear civil rules.

outline.heading: Divorce as a social catastrophe
outline.gist: It is agonizing for both spouses and both families, though sometimes two people try and simply cannot make it work.

outline.heading: Anger, foul play and children caught between families
outline.gist: Most divorces turn spouses and families disrespectful toward each other while sharing grandchildren.

outline.heading: Rising divorce rates and the density of taqwa in the surah
outline.gist: The Muslim world is no longer immune to high divorce rates; the surah mentions taqwa more frequently than any other.

outline.heading: Taqwa is tested at the moment of divorce
outline.gist: Allah promises a way out, forgiveness and ease for the pious; taqwa that vanishes at divorce did not really count.

outline.heading: Two witnesses: divorce should be a contract, not an outburst
outline.gist: Though most schools do not require witnesses, he argues the verse means leaving a marriage should be as formal as entering it, not driven by emotion.

outline.heading: Housing and care during the waiting period; do not harm her
outline.gist: The husband keeps providing a home and support until the divorce is final so she and her family can plan, and he must not make life hard for her.

outline.heading: Maintenance for the pregnant and nursing mother
outline.gist: He supports her until birth and pays for breastfeeding; the verses define his obligations after divorce.

outline.heading: A severe warning to those who defy the rulings
outline.gist: Nations that rejected Allah's rulings were punished; the warning targets men who handle divorce unjustly, and the Prophet brings people from darkness to light.

outline.heading: Seven heavens and as many earths
outline.gist: Seven signals vastness; Allah's command descends through all of creation so you know He is capable of and knows everything.

outline.heading: Good people losing their ethics in divorce
outline.gist: It is sad that Muslims struggle with marriage, one of the most basic human functions; if divorce happens, let it be with respect and piety.

outline.heading: Do not use children, money or the house as weapons
outline.gist: Part ways nicely and respectfully, or heed the warning at the end of the surah.

outline.heading: Interlude
At-Tahrim: relationships between spouses
outline.gist: The last surah of the cluster is about family and marriage, opening with a story.

outline.heading: The honey episode
outline.gist: Two wives claimed honey left a bad smell; the Prophet, careful about hygiene, forbade it for himself, and the Quran asked why.

outline.heading: Do not deprive yourself of the lawful to please a spouse
outline.gist: Pleasing a spouse is good, but giving up something lawful you love for no good reason harms the relationship over time.

outline.heading: A secret disclosed
outline.gist: The Prophet asked a wife to keep it private, she told another, and Allah informed him.

outline.heading: He addressed only the broken trust, not the plot
outline.gist: He spoke about keeping secrets and said nothing of the scheme, leaving them to realize it themselves.

outline.heading: Being the bigger person with full evidence
outline.gist: Not pointing out a spouse's mistake when you could prove it is a high level of selflessness; the verses call them to repent.

outline.heading: Protect yourselves and your families from the Fire
outline.gist: Its fuel is people and stones, guarded by stern angels; protection comes from building a pious family and treating one another at your best.

outline.heading: Four closing examples, all of them women
outline.gist: The ultimate examples of disbelief and of faith are women because a household is made or broken by them, and Allah does not take them for granted.

outline.heading: The wives of Nuh and Lut: a society is as good as its women
outline.gist: Their faith or disbelief spreads to children, husbands and society; Islam raised women's status, and regression on this must change.

outline.heading: The wife of Pharaoh and Maryam
outline.gist: Married to the worst tyrant, Asiyah held to faith; Maryam completes the pair, closing a juz about organizing society.

outline.heading: Relationships built on trust protect the family
outline.gist: The surah's concept is building and maintaining relationships on trust and protecting the family together.

outline.heading: Interlude
Outro

themes.label: Marriage and the relationship between spouses
themes.note: Divorce must be handled as a deliberate, witnessed contract with respect, maintenance and no weaponizing of children or money.

themes.label: Taqwa and God-consciousness
themes.note: Taqwa recurs most densely in at-Talaq because divorce is where it proves real.

themes.label: Jurisprudence rulings and how to approach fiqh
themes.note: He argues for taking the two-witness requirement seriously and sets out the husband's obligations after divorce.

themes.label: Marriage and the relationship between spouses
themes.note: The honey episode teaches not to demand a spouse give up lawful things, to guard trust, and to overlook a spouse's mistake gracefully.

themes.label: The Prophet's attributes, character and example
themes.note: He raised only the broken secret and never rubbed in the plot.

themes.label: Family: parents, relatives, kinship ties
themes.note: Protecting the family from the Fire through piety and good treatment.

themes.label: Gender relations, chastity and modesty
themes.note: All four closing examples are women because their influence shapes families and society; the status Islam gave women must be restored.

hadith.gist: The Prophet loved honey; two wives agreed to tell him it left a bad smell, so he vowed not to eat it again and asked one to keep it secret.

maxims: Taqwa should show itself when divorce occurs
If you enter with a contract, leave with a contract
Don't use kids as weapons
Society is only as good as the women in it

stories.point: Do not forbid yourself what is lawful to please a spouse; it harms the marriage.

stories.who: The Prophet and the disclosed secret
stories.point: Address the breach of trust and leave the rest; be the bigger person.
A woman's disbelief affects far beyond herself.

stories.who: Asiyah, wife of Pharaoh, and Maryam
stories.point: Faith can hold firm even beside a tyrant; women carry the weight of a believing society.

contemporary: Divorce rates in the Muslim world have risen to match global rates over the last decade
takeaways: If divorce comes, carry it out with taqwa, respect and the rulings, not in anger.
Never use children, money or the house as weapons against a former spouse.
Do not ask a spouse to give up something lawful they enjoy without good reason.
Keep a spouse's secrets, and overlook their mistakes without rubbing them in.
Protect your family from the Fire by building a pious home and treating each other at your best.

59:1.ar: سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
59:1.en: All that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth glorifieth Allah, and He is the Mighty, the Wise

59:2.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَخۡرَجَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ مِن دِيَٰرِهِمۡ لِأَوَّلِ ٱلۡحَشۡرِۚ مَا ظَنَنتُمۡ أَن يَخۡرُجُواْۖ وَظَنُّوٓاْ أَنَّهُم مَّانِعَتُهُمۡ حُصُونُهُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ فَأَتَىٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِنۡ حَيۡثُ لَمۡ يَحۡتَسِبُواْۖ وَقَذَفَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ ٱلرُّعۡبَۚ يُخۡرِبُونَ بُيُوتَهُم بِأَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَأَيۡدِي ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ فَٱعۡتَبِرُواْ يَٰٓأُوْلِي ٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرِ
59:2.en: He it is Who hath caused those of the People of the Scripture who disbelieved to go forth from their homes unto the first exile. Ye deemed not that they would go forth, while they deemed that their strongholds would protect them from Allah. But Allah reached them from a place whereof they recked not, and cast terror in their hearts so that they ruined their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers. So learn a lesson, O ye who have eyes

59:3.ar: وَلَوۡلَآ أَن كَتَبَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡجَلَآءَ لَعَذَّبَهُمۡ فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَاۖ وَلَهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ عَذَابُ ٱلنَّارِ
59:3.en: And if Allah had not decreed migration for them, He verily would have punished them in the world, and theirs in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire

59:4.ar: ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمۡ شَآقُّواْ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥۖ وَمَن يُشَآقِّ ٱللَّهَ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعِقَابِ
59:4.en: That is because they were opposed to Allah and His messenger; and whoso is opposed to Allah, (for him) verily Allah is stern in reprisal

59:5.ar: مَا قَطَعۡتُم مِّن لِّينَةٍ أَوۡ تَرَكۡتُمُوهَا قَآئِمَةً عَلَىٰٓ أُصُولِهَا فَبِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِ وَلِيُخۡزِيَ ٱلۡفَٰسِقِينَ
59:5.en: Whatsoever palm-trees ye cut down or left standing on their roots, it was by Allah's leave, in order that He might confound the evil-livers

59:6.ar: وَمَآ أَفَآءَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ رَسُولِهِۦ مِنۡهُمۡ فَمَآ أَوۡجَفۡتُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ مِنۡ خَيۡلࣲ وَلَا رِكَابࣲ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُسَلِّطُ رُسُلَهُۥ عَلَىٰ مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ‏
59:6.en: And that which Allah gave as spoil unto His messenger from them, ye urged not any horse or riding-camel for the sake thereof, but Allah giveth His messenger lordship over whom He will. Allah is Able to do all things

59:7.ar: مَّآ أَفَآءَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ رَسُولِهِۦ مِنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡقُرَىٰ فَلِلَّهِ وَلِلرَّسُولِ وَلِذِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡيَتَٰمَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَٰكِينِ وَٱبۡنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ كَيۡ لَا يَكُونَ دُولَةَۢ بَيۡنَ ٱلۡأَغۡنِيَآءِ مِنكُمۡۚ وَمَآ ءَاتَىٰكُمُ ٱلرَّسُولُ فَخُذُوهُ وَمَا نَهَىٰكُمۡ عَنۡهُ فَٱنتَهُواْۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعِقَابِ
59:7.en: That which Allah giveth as spoil unto His messenger from the people of the townships, it is for Allah and His messenger and for the near of kin and the orphans and the needy and the wayfarer, that it become not a commodity between the rich among you. And whatsoever the messenger giveth you, take it. And whatsoever he forbiddeth, abstain (from it). And keep your duty to Allah. Lo! Allah is stern in reprisal

59:8.ar: لِلۡفُقَرَآءِ ٱلۡمُهَٰجِرِينَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُخۡرِجُواْ مِن دِيَٰرِهِمۡ وَأَمۡوَٰلِهِمۡ يَبۡتَغُونَ فَضۡلࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرِضۡوَٰنࣰ ا وَيَنصُرُونَ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥٓۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلصَّٰدِقُونَ
59:8.en: And (it is) for the poor fugitives who have been driven out from their homes and their belongings, who seek bounty from Allah and help Allah and His messenger. They are the loyal

59:9.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ تَبَوَّءُو ٱلدَّارَ وَٱلۡإِيمَٰنَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡ يُحِبُّونَ مَنۡ هَاجَرَ إِلَيۡهِمۡ وَلَا يَجِدُونَ فِي صُدُورِهِمۡ حَاجَةࣰ مِّمَّآ أُوتُواْ وَيُؤۡثِرُونَ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ وَلَوۡ كَانَ بِهِمۡ خَصَاصَةࣱۚ وَمَن يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفۡسِهِۦ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ
59:9.en: Those who entered the city and the faith before them love those who flee unto them for refuge, and find in their breasts no need for that which hath been given them, but prefer (the fugitives) above themselves though poverty become their lot. And whoso is saved from his own avarice - such are they who are successful

59:10.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ جَآءُو مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِمۡ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا ٱغۡفِرۡ لَنَا وَلِإِخۡوَٰنِنَا ٱلَّذِينَ سَبَقُونَا بِٱلۡإِيمَٰنِ وَلَا تَجۡعَلۡ فِي قُلُوبِنَا غِلࣰّ ا لِّلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ رَبَّنَآ إِنَّكَ رَءُوفࣱ رَّحِيمٌ
59:10.en: And those who came (into the faith) after them say: Our Lord! Forgive us and our brethren who were before us in the faith, and place not in our hearts any rancour toward those who believe. Our Lord! Thou art Full of Pity, Merciful

59:11.ar: ۞أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ نَافَقُواْ يَقُولُونَ لِإِخۡوَٰنِهِمُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ لَئِنۡ أُخۡرِجۡتُمۡ لَنَخۡرُجَنَّ مَعَكُمۡ وَلَا نُطِيعُ فِيكُمۡ أَحَدًا أَبَدࣰ ا وَإِن قُوتِلۡتُمۡ لَنَنصُرَنَّكُمۡ وَٱللَّهُ يَشۡهَدُ إِنَّهُمۡ لَكَٰذِبُونَ
59:11.en: Hast thou not observed those who are hypocrites, (how) they tell their brethren who disbelieve among the People of the Scripture: If ye are driven out, we surely will go out with you, and we will never obey anyone against you, and if ye are attacked we verily will help you. And Allah beareth witness that they verily are liars

59:12.ar: لَئِنۡ أُخۡرِجُواْ لَا يَخۡرُجُونَ مَعَهُمۡ وَلَئِن قُوتِلُواْ لَا يَنصُرُونَهُمۡ وَلَئِن نَّصَرُوهُمۡ لَيُوَلُّنَّ ٱلۡأَدۡبَٰرَ ثُمَّ لَا يُنصَرُونَ
59:12.en: (For) indeed if they are driven out they go not out with them, and indeed if they are attacked they help them not, and indeed if they had helped them they would have turned and fled, and then they would not have been victorious

59:13.ar: لَأَنتُمۡ أَشَدُّ رَهۡبَةࣰ فِي صُدُورِهِم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِۚ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمۡ قَوۡمࣱ لَّا يَفۡقَهُونَ
59:13.en: Ye are more awful as a fear in their bosoms than Allah. That is because they are a folk who understand not

59:14.ar: لَا يُقَٰتِلُونَكُمۡ جَمِيعًا إِلَّا فِي قُرࣰ ى مُّحَصَّنَةٍ أَوۡ مِن وَرَآءِ جُدُرِۭۚ بَأۡسُهُم بَيۡنَهُمۡ شَدِيدࣱۚ تَحۡسَبُهُمۡ جَمِيعࣰ ا وَقُلُوبُهُمۡ شَتَّىٰۚ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمۡ قَوۡمࣱ لَّا يَعۡقِلُونَ
59:14.en: They will not fight against you in a body save in fortified villages or from behind walls. Their adversity among themselves is very great. Ye think of them as a whole whereas their hearts are divers. That is because they are a folk who have no sense

59:15.ar: كَمَثَلِ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡ قَرِيبࣰ اۖ ذَاقُواْ وَبَالَ أَمۡرِهِمۡ وَلَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمࣱ‏
59:15.en: On the likeness of those (who suffered) a short time before them, they taste the ill-effects of their own conduct, and theirs is painful punishment

59:16.ar: كَمَثَلِ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِ إِذۡ قَالَ لِلۡإِنسَٰنِ ٱكۡفُرۡ فَلَمَّا كَفَرَ قَالَ إِنِّي بَرِيٓءࣱ مِّنكَ إِنِّيٓ أَخَافُ ٱللَّهَ رَبَّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
59:16.en: (And the hypocrites are) on the likeness of the devil when he telleth man to disbelieve, then, when he disbelieveth saith: Lo! I am quit of thee. Lo! I fear Allah, the Lord of the Worlds

59:17.ar: فَكَانَ عَٰقِبَتَهُمَآ أَنَّهُمَا فِي ٱلنَّارِ خَٰلِدَيۡنِ فِيهَاۚ وَذَٰلِكَ جَزَٰٓؤُاْ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
59:17.en: And the consequence for both will be that they are in the Fire, therein abiding. Such is the reward of evil-doers

59:18.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَلۡتَنظُرۡ نَفۡسࣱ مَّا قَدَّمَتۡ لِغَدࣲۖ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ خَبِيرُۢ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ
59:18.en: O ye who believe! Observe your duty to Allah. And let every soul look to that which it sendeth on before for the morrow. And observe your duty to Allah. Lo! Allah is Informed of what ye do

59:19.ar: وَلَا تَكُونُواْ كَٱلَّذِينَ نَسُواْ ٱللَّهَ فَأَنسَىٰهُمۡ أَنفُسَهُمۡۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡفَٰسِقُونَ
59:19.en: And be not ye as those who forgot Allah, therefor He caused them to forget their souls. Such are the evil-doers

59:20.ar: لَا يَسۡتَوِيٓ أَصۡحَٰبُ ٱلنَّارِ وَأَصۡحَٰبُ ٱلۡجَنَّةِۚ أَصۡحَٰبُ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ هُمُ ٱلۡفَآئِزُونَ
59:20.en: Not equal are the owners of the Fire and the owners of the Garden. The owners of the Garden, they are the victorious

59:21.ar: لَوۡ أَنزَلۡنَا هَٰذَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ عَلَىٰ جَبَلࣲ لَّرَأَيۡتَهُۥ خَٰشِعࣰ ا مُّتَصَدِّعࣰ ا مِّنۡ خَشۡيَةِ ٱللَّهِۚ وَتِلۡكَ ٱلۡأَمۡثَٰلُ نَضۡرِبُهَا لِلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
59:21.en: If We had caused this Qur'an to descend upon a mountain, thou (O Muhammad) verily hadst seen it humbled, rent asunder by the fear of Allah. Such similitudes coin We for mankind that haply they may reflect

59:22.ar: هُوَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَۖ عَٰلِمُ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ وَٱلشَّهَٰدَةِۖ هُوَ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
59:22.en: He is Allah, than Whom there is no other Allah, the Knower of the Invisible and the Visible. He is the Beneficent, Merciful

59:23.ar: هُوَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلۡمَلِكُ ٱلۡقُدُّوسُ ٱلسَّلَٰمُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُ ٱلۡمُهَيۡمِنُ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡجَبَّارُ ٱلۡمُتَكَبِّرُۚ سُبۡحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ
59:23.en: He is Allah, than Whom there is no other Allah, the Sovereign Lord, the Holy One, Peace, the Keeper of Faith, the Guardian, the Majestic, the Compeller, the Superb. Glorified be Allah from all that they ascribe as partner (unto Him)

59:24.ar: هُوَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡخَٰلِقُ ٱلۡبَارِئُ ٱلۡمُصَوِّرُۖ لَهُ ٱلۡأَسۡمَآءُ ٱلۡحُسۡنَىٰۚ يُسَبِّحُ لَهُۥ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
59:24.en: He is Allah, the Creator, the Shaper out of naught, the Fashioner. His are the most beautiful names. All that is in the heavens and the earth glorifieth Him, and He is the Mighty, the Wise

if4wn2O8d2g.speaker: adnan
if4wn2O8d2g.speaker_note: his surah-summary series; continues the Juz 28 cluster from Al-Mujadilah
if4wn2O8d2g.title: Surat Al-Hashr Summary
if4wn2O8d2g.one_line: Al-Hashr organizes Muslims' relations with groups: treaty-breakers, the poor, allies and dissenters, and builds wealth circulation into the system.
if4wn2O8d2g.summary: He places Al-Hashr in the Juz 28 cluster of Medinan surahs that organize the new, diverse society of Madinah. Where Al-Mujadilah dealt with individuals, Al-Hashr deals with groups. Banu an-Nadir had signed the constitution as citizens, then attempted to assassinate the Prophet and refused to make amends, so they were expelled without battle. The lesson he draws is citizenship: whoever lives in a society must abide by its agreed rules and change them through proper channels, not break them; this holds for Muslims living in Canada today. The verse on the palm trees cut during the siege shows the companions' respect for nature. The rules on fay', wealth gained without war, gave it to relatives, orphans, the poor and stranded travellers, so that wealth would not circulate only among the rich. An Islamic economy, he argues, must have upward mobility built into the system, not left to charity. The Ansar's selfless love for the emigrants shows that success lies in being saved from the greed of the self. The hypocrites' false promises to Banu an-Nadir show that dissenters who keep the covenant are tolerated, not expelled. The surah closes by calling for taqwa and long-term planning, and with a concentrated dose of spirituality in the Names of Allah.

outline.heading: Opening
The mufassal clusters and how they summarize the Quran
outline.gist: He names the remaining clusters and explains that they compress what the earlier parts of the Quran discussed at length.

outline.heading: Madinah's new pluralistic society
outline.gist: People of different lineages, ethnicities and faiths living under one constitution, and the Quran addressing its challenges.

outline.heading: From individuals to groups
outline.gist: Al-Mujadilah organized individual relations; Al-Hashr organizes how Muslims deal with groups that betray, ally, suffer or differ.

outline.heading: Banu an-Nadir's assassination attempt
outline.gist: Citizens under the constitution tried to kill the Prophet, refused to make amends, and were told to leave Madinah.

outline.heading: Abide by the agreed rules or leave
outline.gist: Whoever lives in a society must follow its rules and change them through proper channels, not break them.

outline.heading: Forts that did not protect
outline.gist: They expected their fortresses to protect them, but fear filled their hearts and they gave up quickly.

outline.heading: Exile instead of war
outline.gist: Had expulsion not been decreed, the alternative was war, which neither Allah nor the Muslims wanted.

outline.heading: Living by the laws of your country
outline.gist: Not liking the rules does not make breaking them acceptable; shared rules make societies prosper.

outline.heading: The palm trees cut during the siege
outline.gist: Cold companions cut palm branches for firewood and feared punishment; the Quran permitted it for need, showing their respect for nature.

outline.heading: Fay': wealth gained without war
outline.gist: Customarily such wealth went to soldiers and elders; the Quran gave it to Allah and His Messenger to distribute.

outline.heading: Fay' for relatives, orphans, the poor and travellers
outline.gist: The bounty is directed to those in society who cannot take care of themselves.

outline.heading: So wealth does not circulate only among the rich
outline.gist: A system rigged so the poor get poorer and the rich richer is un-Islamic.

outline.heading: Mobility built into the system; take what the Prophet gives
outline.gist: Upward movement must be designed in, not left to outside aid; the command to obey the Prophet backed a ruling people disliked.

outline.heading: Lifting the poor without impoverishing the rich
outline.gist: The goal was to raise the poor to the middle class, not to deprive the wealthy.

outline.heading: Interlude
The poor emigrants
outline.gist: The needy in society must be sought out and served, since they share the same path.

outline.heading: The Ansar's selfless love
outline.gist: They loved the emigrants and shared with them even when they themselves were in need.

outline.heading: Saved from the greed of the self
outline.gist: Success belongs to those protected from their own selfishness; helping the needy must become something we enjoy.

outline.heading: The hypocrites' false promises
outline.gist: They promised Banu an-Nadir to leave or fight with them, but Allah says they lie and fear the Muslims.

outline.heading: Dissenters who keep the covenant are not expelled
outline.gist: Only those who broke the constitution were removed; others who disagreed but kept the agreement stayed.

outline.heading: Interlude
Taqwa and long-term planning
outline.gist: Look to what you send ahead; relations with allies, traitors and the poor need plans for decades ahead.

outline.heading: Hearts harder than a mountain; the Names of Allah
outline.gist: Had the Quran descended on a mountain it would shake; the dynamic surah ends with a concentrated dose of spirituality.

themes.label: Community building, cooperation and the ummah
themes.note: The Medinan surahs organize a diverse society and Muslims' relations with other groups.

themes.label: Oaths, promises, trust and loyalty
themes.note: Banu an-Nadir broke the constitution they had signed and were expelled.

themes.label: Muslim identity and life in the West / Canada
themes.note: Muslims must abide by the agreed laws of the country they live in and change them through proper channels.

themes.label: Environment and stewardship of the earth
themes.note: The companions' reluctance to cut trees except out of need.

themes.label: Wealth, asceticism (zuhd), consumerism and money
themes.note: Fay' and the principle that wealth must not circulate only among the rich; upward mobility built into the economy.

themes.label: Obedience to Allah and the Messenger
themes.note: Take what the Prophet gives you, revealed to back an unpopular ruling.

themes.label: Selfishness, greed of the soul (shuhh) and selflessness
themes.note: The Ansar's selflessness and being saved from the greed of the self.

themes.label: Tolerance, pluralism and dealing with difference
themes.note: Hypocrites who kept the covenant were left in the society.

themes.label: Taqwa and God-consciousness
themes.note: Taqwa as long-term planning for what we meet Allah with.

themes.label: Spirituality, khushoo and the inner life
themes.note: The Names of Allah as a spiritual dose amid practical rulings.

maxims: Not liking the rules doesn't mean you can break them.
Wealth must not circulate only among the rich.
Uplift must be built into the system, not an exception.

stories.point: Breaking a shared covenant and refusing to make amends forfeits one's place in society.

stories.who: Companions cutting palm branches for warmth during the siege
stories.point: Their respect for nature made them fear sin over a small tree.
True brotherhood is selfless sharing even in one's own need.

contemporary: Muslims living under the laws of Canada and other countries
Economic systems in which the poor get poorer and the rich richer
takeaways: Abide by the laws of the country you live in and seek change through proper channels.
Respect nature and use resources only when needed.
Support economic arrangements that let the poor move up, not just charity.
Fight your own selfishness so helping others becomes a joy.
Plan long-term for the community's relations and for meeting Allah.

52:7.en: Lo! the doom of thy Lord will surely come to pass

52:8.en: There is none that can ward it off

52:9.en: On the day when the heaven will heave with (awful) heaving

52:10.en: And the mountains move away with (awful) movement

52:11.en: Then woe that day unto the deniers

52:12.en: Who play in talk of grave matters

52:13.ar: يَوۡمَ يُدَعُّونَ إِلَىٰ نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ دَعًّا
52:13.en: The day when they are thrust with a (disdainful) thrust, into the fire of hell

52:14.ar: هَٰذِهِ ٱلنَّارُ ٱلَّتِي كُنتُم بِهَا تُكَذِّبُونَ
52:14.en: (And it is said unto them): This is the Fire which ye were wont to deny

52:15.ar: أَفَسِحۡرٌ هَٰذَآ أَمۡ أَنتُمۡ لَا تُبۡصِرُونَ
52:15.en: Is this magic, or do ye not see

52:16.ar: ٱصۡلَوۡهَا فَٱصۡبِرُوٓاْ أَوۡ لَا تَصۡبِرُواْ سَوَآءٌ عَلَيۡكُمۡۖ إِنَّمَا تُجۡزَوۡنَ مَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
52:16.en: Endure the heat thereof, and whether ye are patient of it or impatient of it is all one for you. Ye are only being paid for what ye used to do

52:17.en: Lo! those who kept their duty dwell in gardens and delight

52:18.ar: فَٰكِهِينَ بِمَآ ءَاتَىٰهُمۡ رَبُّهُمۡ وَوَقَىٰهُمۡ رَبُّهُمۡ عَذَابَ ٱلۡجَحِيمِ
52:18.en: Happy because of what their Lord hath given them, and (because) their Lord hath warded off from them the torment of hell-fire

52:19.ar: كُلُواْ وَٱشۡرَبُواْ هَنِيٓـَٔۢا بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
52:19.en: (And it is said unto them): Eat and drink in health (as a reward) for what ye used to do

52:20.ar: مُتَّكِـِٔينَ عَلَىٰ سُرُرࣲ مَّصۡفُوفَةࣲۖ وَزَوَّجۡنَٰهُم بِحُورٍ عِينࣲ‏
52:20.en: Reclining on ranged couches. And we wed them unto fair ones with wide, lovely eyes

52:21.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَٱتَّبَعَتۡهُمۡ ذُرِّيَّتُهُم بِإِيمَٰنٍ أَلۡحَقۡنَا بِهِمۡ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمۡ وَمَآ أَلَتۡنَٰهُم مِّنۡ عَمَلِهِم مِّن شَيۡءࣲۚ كُلُّ ٱمۡرِيِٕۭ بِمَا كَسَبَ رَهِينࣱ‏
52:21.en: And they who believe and whose seed follow them in faith, We cause their seed to join them (there), and We deprive them of nought of their (life's) work. Every man is a pledge for that which he hath earned

52:22.en: And We provide them with fruit and meat such as they desire

52:23.ar: يَتَنَٰزَعُونَ فِيهَا كَأۡسࣰ ا لَّا لَغۡوࣱ فِيهَا وَلَا تَأۡثِيمࣱ‏
52:23.en: There they pass from hand to hand a cup wherein is neither vanity nor cause of sin

52:24.ar: ۞وَيَطُوفُ عَلَيۡهِمۡ غِلۡمَانࣱ لَّهُمۡ كَأَنَّهُمۡ لُؤۡلُؤࣱ مَّكۡنُونࣱ‏
52:24.en: And there go round, waiting on them menservants of their own, as they were hidden pearls

52:25.en: And some of them draw near unto others, questioning

52:26.ar: قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا كُنَّا قَبۡلُ فِيٓ أَهۡلِنَا مُشۡفِقِينَ
52:26.en: Saying: Lo! of old, when we were with our families, we were ever anxious

52:27.ar: فَمَنَّ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡنَا وَوَقَىٰنَا عَذَابَ ٱلسَّمُومِ
52:27.en: But Allah hath been gracious unto us and hath preserved us from the torment of the breath of Fire

52:28.ar: إِنَّا كُنَّا مِن قَبۡلُ نَدۡعُوهُۖ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلۡبَرُّ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
52:28.en: Lo! we used to pray unto Him of old. Lo! He is the Benign, the Merciful

52:29.ar: فَذَكِّرۡ فَمَآ أَنتَ بِنِعۡمَتِ رَبِّكَ بِكَاهِنࣲ وَلَا مَجۡنُونٍ
52:29.en: Therefor warn (men, O Muhammad). By the grace of Allah thou art neither soothsayer nor madman

52:30.ar: أَمۡ يَقُولُونَ شَاعِرࣱ نَّتَرَبَّصُ بِهِۦ رَيۡبَ ٱلۡمَنُونِ
52:30.en: Or say they: (he is) a poet, (one) for whom we may expect the accident of time

52:31.ar: قُلۡ تَرَبَّصُواْ فَإِنِّي مَعَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡمُتَرَبِّصِينَ
52:31.en: Say (unto them): Except (your fill)! Lo! I am with you among the expectant

52:32.ar: أَمۡ تَأۡمُرُهُمۡ أَحۡلَٰمُهُم بِهَٰذَآۚ أَمۡ هُمۡ قَوۡمࣱ طَاغُونَ
52:32.en: Do their minds command them to do this, or are they an outrageous folk

52:33.ar: أَمۡ يَقُولُونَ تَقَوَّلَهُۥۚ بَل لَّا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
52:33.en: Or say they: He hath invented it? Nay, but they will not believe

52:34.ar: فَلۡيَأۡتُواْ بِحَدِيثࣲ مِّثۡلِهِۦٓ إِن كَانُواْ صَٰدِقِينَ
52:34.en: Then let them produce speech the like thereof, if they are truthful

52:35.ar: أَمۡ خُلِقُواْ مِنۡ غَيۡرِ شَيۡءٍ أَمۡ هُمُ ٱلۡخَٰلِقُونَ
52:35.en: Or were they created out of naught? Or are they the creators

52:36.ar: أَمۡ خَلَقُواْ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَۚ بَل لَّا يُوقِنُونَ
52:36.en: Or did they create the heavens and the earth? Nay, but they are sure of nothing

52:37.ar: أَمۡ عِندَهُمۡ خَزَآئِنُ رَبِّكَ أَمۡ هُمُ ٱلۡمُصَۜيۡطِرُونَ
52:37.en: Or do they own the treasures of thy Lord? Or have they been given charge (thereof)

52:38.ar: أَمۡ لَهُمۡ سُلَّمࣱ يَسۡتَمِعُونَ فِيهِۖ فَلۡيَأۡتِ مُسۡتَمِعُهُم بِسُلۡطَٰنࣲ مُّبِينٍ
52:38.en: Or have they any stairway (unto heaven) by means of which they overhear (decrees). Then let their listener produce some warrant manifest

52:39.en: Or hath He daughters whereas ye have sons

52:40.ar: أَمۡ تَسۡـَٔلُهُمۡ أَجۡرࣰ ا فَهُم مِّن مَّغۡرَمࣲ مُّثۡقَلُونَ
52:40.en: Or askest thou (Muhammad) a fee from them so that they are plunged in debt

52:41.en: Or possess they the Unseen so that they can write (it) down

52:42.ar: أَمۡ يُرِيدُونَ كَيۡدࣰ اۖ فَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ هُمُ ٱلۡمَكِيدُونَ
52:42.en: Or seek they to ensnare (the messenger)? But those who disbelieve, they are the ensnared

52:43.ar: أَمۡ لَهُمۡ إِلَٰهٌ غَيۡرُ ٱللَّهِۚ سُبۡحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ
52:43.en: Or have they any god beside Allah? Glorified be Allah from all that they ascribe as partner (unto Him)

52:44.ar: وَإِن يَرَوۡاْ كِسۡفࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ سَاقِطࣰ ا يَقُولُواْ سَحَابࣱ مَّرۡكُومࣱ‏
52:44.en: And if they were to see a fragment of the heaven falling, they would say: A heap of clouds

52:45.ar: فَذَرۡهُمۡ حَتَّىٰ يُلَٰقُواْ يَوۡمَهُمُ ٱلَّذِي فِيهِ يُصۡعَقُونَ
52:45.en: Then let them be (O Muhammad), till they meet their day, in which they will be thunder-stricken

52:46.ar: يَوۡمَ لَا يُغۡنِي عَنۡهُمۡ كَيۡدُهُمۡ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَلَا هُمۡ يُنصَرُونَ
52:46.en: A day in which their guile will naught avail them, nor will they be helped

52:47.ar: وَإِنَّ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ عَذَابࣰ ا دُونَ ذَٰلِكَ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَهُمۡ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
52:47.en: And verily, for those who do wrong, there is a punishment beyond that. But most of them know not

52:48.ar: وَٱصۡبِرۡ لِحُكۡمِ رَبِّكَ فَإِنَّكَ بِأَعۡيُنِنَاۖ وَسَبِّحۡ بِحَمۡدِ رَبِّكَ حِينَ تَقُومُ
52:48.en: So wait patiently (O Muhammad) for thy Lord's decree, for surely thou art in Our sight; and hymn the praise of thy Lord when thou uprisest

52:49.en: And in the night-time also hymn His praise, and at the setting of the stars

53:1.en: By the Star when it setteth

53:2.en: Your comrade erreth not, nor is deceived

53:3.en: Nor doth he speak of (his own) desire

53:4.en: It is naught save an inspiration that is inspired

53:5.en: Which one of mighty powers hath taught him

53:6.en: One vigorous; and he grew clear to view

53:7.en: When he was on the uppermost horizon

53:8.en: Then he drew nigh and came down

53:9.en: Till he was (distant) two bows' length or even nearer

53:10.en: And He revealed unto His slave that which He revealed

53:11.en: The heart lied not (in seeing) what it saw

53:12.en: Will ye then dispute with him concerning what he seeth

53:13.en: And verily he saw him yet another time

53:14.en: By the lote-tree of the utmost boundary

53:15.en: Nigh unto which is the Garden of Abode

53:16.en: When that which shroudeth did enshroud the lote-tree

53:17.en: The eye turned not aside nor yet was overbold

53:18.ar: لَقَدۡ رَأَىٰ مِنۡ ءَايَٰتِ رَبِّهِ ٱلۡكُبۡرَىٰٓ
53:18.en: Verily he saw one of the greater revelations of his Lord

53:19.en: Have ye thought upon Al-Lat and Al-'Uzza

53:20.en: And Manat, the third, the other

53:21.en: Are yours the males and His the females

53:22.en: That indeed were an unfair division

53:23.ar: إِنۡ هِيَ إِلَّآ أَسۡمَآءࣱ سَمَّيۡتُمُوهَآ أَنتُمۡ وَءَابَآؤُكُم مَّآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ بِهَا مِن سُلۡطَٰنٍۚ إِن يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا ٱلظَّنَّ وَمَا تَهۡوَى ٱلۡأَنفُسُۖ وَلَقَدۡ جَآءَهُم مِّن رَّبِّهِمُ ٱلۡهُدَىٰٓ
53:23.en: They are but names which ye have named, ye and your fathers, for which Allah hath revealed no warrant. They follow but a guess and that which (they) themselves desire. And now the guidance from their Lord hath come unto them

53:24.en: Or shall man have what he coveteth

53:25.en: But unto Allah belongeth the after (life), and the former

53:26.ar: ۞وَكَم مِّن مَّلَكࣲ فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ لَا تُغۡنِي شَفَٰعَتُهُمۡ شَيۡـًٔا إِلَّا مِنۢ بَعۡدِ أَن يَأۡذَنَ ٱللَّهُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيَرۡضَىٰٓ
53:26.en: And how many angels are in the heavens whose intercession availeth naught save after Allah giveth leave to whom He chooseth and accepteth

53:27.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ لَيُسَمُّونَ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةَ تَسۡمِيَةَ ٱلۡأُنثَىٰ
53:27.en: Lo! it is those who disbelieve in the Hereafter who name the angels with the names of females

53:28.ar: وَمَا لَهُم بِهِۦ مِنۡ عِلۡمٍۖ إِن يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا ٱلظَّنَّۖ وَإِنَّ ٱلظَّنَّ لَا يُغۡنِي مِنَ ٱلۡحَقِّ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا
53:28.en: And they have no knowledge thereof. They follow but a guess, and lo! a guess can never take the place of the truth

53:29.ar: فَأَعۡرِضۡ عَن مَّن تَوَلَّىٰ عَن ذِكۡرِنَا وَلَمۡ يُرِدۡ إِلَّا ٱلۡحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا
53:29.en: Then withdraw (O Muhammad) from him who fleeth from Our remembrance and desireth but the life of the world

53:30.ar: ذَٰلِكَ مَبۡلَغُهُم مِّنَ ٱلۡعِلۡمِۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَن ضَلَّ عَن سَبِيلِهِۦ وَهُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَنِ ٱهۡتَدَىٰ
53:30.en: Such is their sum of knowledge. Lo! thy Lord is Best Aware of him who strayeth, and He is Best Aware of him whom goeth right

53:31.ar: وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ لِيَجۡزِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَسَٰٓـُٔواْ بِمَا عَمِلُواْ وَيَجۡزِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَحۡسَنُواْ بِٱلۡحُسۡنَى
53:31.en: And unto Allah belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth, that He may reward those who do evil with that which they have done, and reward those who do good with goodness

53:32.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَجۡتَنِبُونَ كَبَٰٓئِرَ ٱلۡإِثۡمِ وَٱلۡفَوَٰحِشَ إِلَّا ٱللَّمَمَۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ وَٰسِعُ ٱلۡمَغۡفِرَةِۚ هُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِكُمۡ إِذۡ أَنشَأَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَإِذۡ أَنتُمۡ أَجِنَّةࣱ فِي بُطُونِ أُمَّهَٰتِكُمۡۖ فَلَا تُزَكُّوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۡۖ هُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَنِ ٱتَّقَىٰٓ
53:32.en: Those who avoid enormities of sin and abominations, save the unwilled offences - (for them) lo! thy Lord is of vast mercy. He is Best Aware of you (from the time) when He created you from the earth, and when ye were hidden in the bellies of your mothers. Therefor ascribe not purity unto yourselves. He is Best Aware of him who wardeth off (evil)

53:33.en: Didst thou (O Muhammad) observe him who turned away

53:34.en: And gave a little, then was grudging

53:35.en: Hath he knowledge of the Unseen so that he seeth

53:36.ar: أَمۡ لَمۡ يُنَبَّأۡ بِمَا فِي صُحُفِ مُوسَىٰ
53:36.en: Or hath he not had news of what is in the books of Moses

53:37.en: And Abraham who paid his debt

53:38.en: That no laden one shall bear another's load

53:39.ar: وَأَن لَّيۡسَ لِلۡإِنسَٰنِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَىٰ
53:39.en: And that man hath only that for which he maketh effort

53:40.en: And that his effort will be seen

53:41.en: And afterward he will be repaid for it with fullest payment

53:42.en: And that thy Lord, He is the goal

53:43.en: And that He it is who maketh laugh, and maketh weep

53:44.en: And that He it is Who giveth death and giveth life

53:45.en: And that He createth the two spouses, the male and the female

53:46.en: From a drop (of seed) when it is poured forth

53:47.en: And that He hath ordained the second bringing forth

53:48.en: And that He it is Who enricheth and contenteth

53:49.en: And that He it is Who is the Lord of Sirius

53:50.en: And that He destroyed the former (tribe of) A'ad

53:51.en: And (the tribe of) Thamud He spared not

53:52.ar: وَقَوۡمَ نُوحࣲ مِّن قَبۡلُۖ إِنَّهُمۡ كَانُواْ هُمۡ أَظۡلَمَ وَأَطۡغَىٰ
53:52.en: And the folk of Noah aforetime, Lo! they were more unjust and more rebellious

53:54.en: So that there covered them that which did cover

53:55.en: Concerning which then, of the bounties of thy Lord, canst thou dispute

53:56.en: This is a warner of the warners of old

53:58.ar: لَيۡسَ لَهَا مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ كَاشِفَةٌ
53:58.en: None beside Allah can disclose it

53:59.en: Marvel ye then at this statement

53:62.en: Rather prostrate yourselves before Allah and serve Him

rcyeKREsD9c.speaker: adnan
rcyeKREsD9c.speaker_note: his daily surah-summary series at MWN; refers back to his previous sessions in the cluster
rcyeKREsD9c.title: Surat At-Tur and An-Najm Summaries
rcyeKREsD9c.one_line: At-Tur contrasts guidance with stubborn disbelief; An-Najm contrasts certain, revealed knowledge with guesswork and ignorance.
rcyeKREsD9c.summary: Continuing the cluster of comparison surahs, he takes two surahs together. At-Tur sets guidance against disbelief. Its oaths place revelation inside the world we live in: the mountain where Musa received revelation, the written scripture, the House, the sky and the sea. It then warns those who play with the truth, shows the pious in Paradise, and promises that believing families who found guidance together will be joined at the level of their highest member. He dwells on the long run of questions beginning with 'or', which he calls one of the most structured theological arguments in the Quran: are they created from nothing, did they create themselves, can they produce something like it? Someone who refuses guidance will explain away even a falling sky. An-Najm sets knowledge against ignorance. The Prophet's night journey, his nearness to Allah and his vision at the Lote Tree are presented as witnessed knowledge, while idols, and the claim that angels are female, are names made up without evidence. His key lesson is that the biggest choice of your life cannot rest on probabilities; it needs certainty from a verified source, such as the scrolls of Ibrahim and Musa. He asks listeners to recite An-Najm, learn its story, and prostrate as the surah commands.

outline.heading: The cluster of comparison surahs
outline.gist: Each surah in the cluster compares two ways of living and points to their outcome, reward or punishment; he recaps Qaf and Adh-Dhariyat.

outline.heading: Oaths: Sinai, scripture, the House, sky and sea
outline.gist: Allah swears by the places and books of revelation, showing that guidance was sent within this world, and states that His punishment will surely come.

outline.heading: Woe to those who play with the truth
outline.gist: Disbelief is refusing what one knows is true; those absorbed in idle play are driven to the Fire on the Day of Judgment.

outline.heading: The pious in Paradise
outline.gist: A quick turn to the joy of the righteous in the gardens.

outline.heading: Families joined in Paradise; every soul pledged to its deeds
outline.gist: Believing families who found guidance together are raised to the level of their highest member without anyone losing reward, yet each person is held by his own deeds.

outline.heading: Interlude
You are neither soothsayer nor madman
outline.gist: Allah tells the Prophet to keep reminding, whatever names they call him.

outline.heading: The chain of 'or' questions
outline.gist: He describes the run of questions as a gold mine of theology: is he a poet, are they simply transgressors, did he invent it?

outline.heading: Produce something like it; created from nothing?
outline.gist: The challenge to produce a comparable book, and the questions of whether they came from nothing, created themselves or created the heavens and earth.

outline.heading: Those who will not be guided: the falling sky
outline.gist: Even seeing the sky fall they would call it heaped clouds; no sign moves one who refuses guidance, so leave them to their day.

outline.heading: Patience under Allah's watchful eye
outline.gist: 'You are in Our eyes' is an Arabic figure of speech for care, protection and love; glorify Allah morning and night.

outline.heading: The choice At-Tur offers
outline.gist: Be like those who deny every argument until they are shocked, or like the guided family joined in Paradise; either way, persevere.

outline.heading: An-Najm: knowledge versus ignorance
outline.gist: He introduces the second surah as a comparison between speaking from true knowledge and speaking from ignorance.

outline.heading: The night journey and the oath by the star
outline.gist: The surah opens with the Prophet's ascension; your companion has not strayed or erred.

outline.heading: He does not speak from desire
outline.gist: What the Prophet teaches is knowledge given to him by Allah, not his own invention.

outline.heading: As close as can be: two bow-lengths or nearer
outline.gist: An Arabic figure for the utmost nearness; whether he saw Allah is debated and not the point, the point is what he was taught.

outline.heading: The Lote Tree of the furthest boundary
outline.gist: He saw it again at a place no creation reached, where even Jibril did not go further, near the Garden of Refuge.

outline.heading: His sight did not swerve; idols are mere names
outline.gist: He saw the great signs of his Lord, while the idols are names they and their fathers made up with no authority.

outline.heading: Angels named as females: guesswork is not knowledge
outline.gist: Those who reject the Hereafter make up claims with no source, no chain and no evidence.

outline.heading: Certainty for the biggest choice; Allah knew you in the womb
outline.gist: The path you choose is a life-and-death decision that cannot rest on probability; do not claim purity, Allah knew you as a fetus.

outline.heading: A verified source: the scrolls of Ibrahim and Musa
outline.gist: Unlike the idolaters' made-up names, the revelation carries the knowledge of all earlier prophets.

outline.heading: No soul bears another's burden
outline.gist: You get only what you strove for; your efforts will be seen and fully repaid.

outline.heading: He makes laugh and weep, gives life and death
outline.gist: The surah lists Allah's power: creation, wealth, Lord of Sirius, destroyer of Ad, Thamud and the people of Nuh.

outline.heading: Which of your Lord's favours do you doubt?
outline.gist: Doubt comes from ignorance; the Quran even shares ancient words from the scrolls of Ibrahim.

outline.heading: The approaching Hour; laughing instead of weeping
outline.gist: The Hour has drawn near and nothing can hold it back; do you laugh and live aimlessly?

outline.heading: Prostrate to Allah and worship Him
outline.gist: The surah ends with a command to prostrate; he urges listeners to learn and recite An-Najm and see that none of it can be taken lightly.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Guidance (hidayah)
themes.note: At-Tur compares guidance with disbelief; those who refuse guidance will explain away every sign.

themes.label: Seeking knowledge, learning and scholars
themes.note: An-Najm sets knowledge from a verified source against conjecture and made-up names.

themes.label: Eman: faith, certainty, doubt
themes.note: Righteousness needs certainty, not probability; doubt grows out of ignorance.

themes.label: Family: parents, relatives, kinship ties
themes.note: Families who sought guidance together are reunited in Paradise at the level of their highest member.

themes.label: Atheism, doubt and responding to disbelief
themes.note: The chain of questions in At-Tur as a structured argument against disbelief.

themes.label: The Prophet's attributes, character and example
themes.note: The Prophet as truthful witness of the ascension; he did not stray, err or invent.

themes.label: Accountability before Allah and goals
themes.note: Each soul gets only what it worked for and is judged on its own efforts.

themes.label: Patience (sabr) and perseverance
themes.note: The Prophet is told to persevere, knowing Allah watches over him.

themes.label: Salah: its meaning, etiquette and significance
themes.note: An-Najm closes with the command to prostrate.

maxims: You can't make life's biggest choice on probabilities.
Those who don't want guidance will not be guided.
Just because you don't understand it doesn't mean it didn't happen.

stories.who: The Prophet's night journey and ascension (Isra and Miraj)
stories.point: The Prophet speaks from what he witnessed and was taught, so his knowledge is certain.

takeaways: Seek guidance as a family so you can be joined together in Paradise.
Base your religious convictions on certain, verified sources rather than guesses.
Do not claim purity for yourself; Allah knows you better than you do.
Recite and study Surat An-Najm and perform its prostration.

60:1.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَتَّخِذُواْ عَدُوِّي وَعَدُوَّكُمۡ أَوۡلِيَآءَ تُلۡقُونَ إِلَيۡهِم بِٱلۡمَوَدَّةِ وَقَدۡ كَفَرُواْ بِمَا جَآءَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡحَقِّ يُخۡرِجُونَ ٱلرَّسُولَ وَإِيَّاكُمۡ أَن تُؤۡمِنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ رَبِّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ خَرَجۡتُمۡ جِهَٰدࣰ ا فِي سَبِيلِي وَٱبۡتِغَآءَ مَرۡضَاتِيۚ تُسِرُّونَ إِلَيۡهِم بِٱلۡمَوَدَّةِ وَأَنَا۠ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَآ أَخۡفَيۡتُمۡ وَمَآ أَعۡلَنتُمۡۚ وَمَن يَفۡعَلۡهُ مِنكُمۡ فَقَدۡ ضَلَّ سَوَآءَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ
60:1.en: O ye who believe! Choose not My enemy and your enemy for allies. Do ye give them friendship when they disbelieve in that truth which hath come unto you, driving out the messenger and you because ye believe in Allah, your Lord? If ye have come forth to strive in My way and seeking My good pleasure, (show them not friendship). Do ye show friendship unto them in secret, when I am Best Aware of what ye hide and what ye proclaim? And whosoever doeth it among you, he verily hath strayed from the right way

60:2.ar: إِن يَثۡقَفُوكُمۡ يَكُونُواْ لَكُمۡ أَعۡدَآءࣰ وَيَبۡسُطُوٓاْ إِلَيۡكُمۡ أَيۡدِيَهُمۡ وَأَلۡسِنَتَهُم بِٱلسُّوٓءِ وَوَدُّواْ لَوۡ تَكۡفُرُونَ
60:2.en: If they have the upper hand of you, they will be your foes, and will stretch out their hands and their tongues toward you with evil (intent), and they long for you to disbelieve

60:3.ar: لَن تَنفَعَكُمۡ أَرۡحَامُكُمۡ وَلَآ أَوۡلَٰدُكُمۡۚ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ يَفۡصِلُ بَيۡنَكُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ بَصِيرࣱ‏
60:3.en: Your ties of kindred and your children will avail you naught upon the Day of Resurrection. He will part you. Allah is Seer of what ye do

60:4.ar: قَدۡ كَانَتۡ لَكُمۡ أُسۡوَةٌ حَسَنَةࣱ فِيٓ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ وَٱلَّذِينَ مَعَهُۥٓ إِذۡ قَالُواْ لِقَوۡمِهِمۡ إِنَّا بُرَءَٰٓؤُاْ مِنكُمۡ وَمِمَّا تَعۡبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ كَفَرۡنَا بِكُمۡ وَبَدَا بَيۡنَنَا وَبَيۡنَكُمُ ٱلۡعَدَٰوَةُ وَٱلۡبَغۡضَآءُ أَبَدًا حَتَّىٰ تُؤۡمِنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَحۡدَهُۥٓ إِلَّا قَوۡلَ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ لِأَبِيهِ لَأَسۡتَغۡفِرَنَّ لَكَ وَمَآ أَمۡلِكُ لَكَ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ مِن شَيۡءࣲۖ رَّبَّنَا عَلَيۡكَ تَوَكَّلۡنَا وَإِلَيۡكَ أَنَبۡنَا وَإِلَيۡكَ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
60:4.en: There is a goodly pattern for you in Abraham and those with him, when they told their folk: Lo! we are guiltless of you and all that ye worship beside Allah. We have done with you. And there hath arisen between us and you hostility and hate for ever until ye believe in Allah only - save that which Abraham promised his father (when he said): I will ask forgiveness for thee, though I own nothing for thee from Allah - Our Lord! In Thee we put our trust, and unto Thee we turn repentant, and unto Thee is the journeying

60:5.ar: رَبَّنَا لَا تَجۡعَلۡنَا فِتۡنَةࣰ لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَٱغۡفِرۡ لَنَا رَبَّنَآۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
60:5.en: Our Lord! Make us not a prey for those who disbelieve, and forgive us, our Lord! Lo! Thou, only Thou, are the Mighty, the Wise

60:6.ar: لَقَدۡ كَانَ لَكُمۡ فِيهِمۡ أُسۡوَةٌ حَسَنَةࣱ لِّمَن كَانَ يَرۡجُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلۡيَوۡمَ ٱلۡأٓخِرَۚ وَمَن يَتَوَلَّ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلۡغَنِيُّ ٱلۡحَمِيدُ
60:6.en: Verily ye have in them a goodly pattern for everyone who looketh to Allah and the Last Day. And whosoever may turn away, lo! still Allah, He is the Absolute, the Owner of Praise

60:7.ar: ۞عَسَى ٱللَّهُ أَن يَجۡعَلَ بَيۡنَكُمۡ وَبَيۡنَ ٱلَّذِينَ عَادَيۡتُم مِّنۡهُم مَّوَدَّةࣰۚ وَٱللَّهُ قَدِيرࣱۚ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
60:7.en: It may be that Allah will ordain love between you and those of them with whom ye are at enmity. Allah is Mighty, and Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

60:8.ar: لَّا يَنۡهَىٰكُمُ ٱللَّهُ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ لَمۡ يُقَٰتِلُوكُمۡ فِي ٱلدِّينِ وَلَمۡ يُخۡرِجُوكُم مِّن دِيَٰرِكُمۡ أَن تَبَرُّوهُمۡ وَتُقۡسِطُوٓاْ إِلَيۡهِمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُقۡسِطِينَ
60:8.en: Allah forbiddeth you not those who warred not against you on account of religion and drove you not out from your homes, that ye should show them kindness and deal justly with them. Lo! Allah loveth the just dealers

60:9.ar: إِنَّمَا يَنۡهَىٰكُمُ ٱللَّهُ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ قَٰتَلُوكُمۡ فِي ٱلدِّينِ وَأَخۡرَجُوكُم مِّن دِيَٰرِكُمۡ وَظَٰهَرُواْ عَلَىٰٓ إِخۡرَاجِكُمۡ أَن تَوَلَّوۡهُمۡۚ وَمَن يَتَوَلَّهُمۡ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ
60:9.en: Allah forbiddeth you only those who warred against you on account of religion and have driven you out from your homes and helped to drive you out, that ye make friends of them. Whosoever maketh friends of them - (All) such are wrong-doers

60:10.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِذَا جَآءَكُمُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتُ مُهَٰجِرَٰتࣲ فَٱمۡتَحِنُوهُنَّۖ ٱللَّهُ أَعۡلَمُ بِإِيمَٰنِهِنَّۖ فَإِنۡ عَلِمۡتُمُوهُنَّ مُؤۡمِنَٰتࣲ فَلَا تَرۡجِعُوهُنَّ إِلَى ٱلۡكُفَّارِۖ لَا هُنَّ حِلࣱّ لَّهُمۡ وَلَا هُمۡ يَحِلُّونَ لَهُنَّۖ وَءَاتُوهُم مَّآ أَنفَقُواْۚ وَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ أَن تَنكِحُوهُنَّ إِذَآ ءَاتَيۡتُمُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّۚ وَلَا تُمۡسِكُواْ بِعِصَمِ ٱلۡكَوَافِرِ وَسۡـَٔلُواْ مَآ أَنفَقۡتُمۡ وَلۡيَسۡـَٔلُواْ مَآ أَنفَقُواْۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ حُكۡمُ ٱللَّهِ يَحۡكُمُ بَيۡنَكُمۡۖ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمࣱ‏
60:10.en: O ye who believe! When believing women come unto you as fugitives, examine them. Allah is Best Aware of their faith. Then, if ye know them for true believers, send them not back unto the disbelievers. They are not lawful for them (the disbelievers), nor are they (the disbelievers) lawful for them. And give them (the disbelievers) that which they have spent (upon them). And it is no sin for you to marry such women when ye have given them their dues. And hold not to the ties of disbelieving women; and ask for (the return of) that which ye have spent; and let them (the disbelievers) ask for that which they have spent. That is the judgment of Allah. He judgeth between you. Allah is Knower, Wise

60:11.ar: وَإِن فَاتَكُمۡ شَيۡءࣱ مِّنۡ أَزۡوَٰجِكُمۡ إِلَى ٱلۡكُفَّارِ فَعَاقَبۡتُمۡ فَـَٔاتُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ ذَهَبَتۡ أَزۡوَٰجُهُم مِّثۡلَ مَآ أَنفَقُواْۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنتُم بِهِۦ مُؤۡمِنُونَ
60:11.en: And if any of your wives have gone from you unto the disbelievers and afterward ye have your turn (of triumph), then give unto those whose wives have gone the like of that which they have spent, and keep your duty to Allah in Whom ye are believers

60:12.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ إِذَا جَآءَكَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتُ يُبَايِعۡنَكَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن لَّا يُشۡرِكۡنَ بِٱللَّهِ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَلَا يَسۡرِقۡنَ وَلَا يَزۡنِينَ وَلَا يَقۡتُلۡنَ أَوۡلَٰدَهُنَّ وَلَا يَأۡتِينَ بِبُهۡتَٰنࣲ يَفۡتَرِينَهُۥ بَيۡنَ أَيۡدِيهِنَّ وَأَرۡجُلِهِنَّ وَلَا يَعۡصِينَكَ فِي مَعۡرُوفࣲ فَبَايِعۡهُنَّ وَٱسۡتَغۡفِرۡ لَهُنَّ ٱللَّهَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
60:12.en: O Prophet! If believing women come unto thee, taking oath of allegiance unto thee that they will ascribe no thing as partner unto Allah, and will neither steal nor commit adultery nor kill their children, nor produce any lie that they have devised between their hands and feet, nor disobey thee in what is right, then accept their allegiance and ask Allah to forgive them. Lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

60:13.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَتَوَلَّوۡاْ قَوۡمًا غَضِبَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِمۡ قَدۡ يَئِسُواْ مِنَ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ كَمَا يَئِسَ ٱلۡكُفَّارُ مِنۡ أَصۡحَٰبِ ٱلۡقُبُورِ
60:13.en: O ye who believe! Be not friendly with a folk with whom Allah is wroth, (a folk) who have despaired of the Hereafter as the disbelievers despair of those who are in the graves

RFOaj6FMlSs.speaker: adnan
RFOaj6FMlSs.speaker_note: Surah Summaries series at his centre; same voice and method as the rest of the series
RFOaj6FMlSs.title: Surat Al-Mumtahanah Summary
RFOaj6FMlSs.one_line: Al-Mumtahanah sets how Muslims treat non-Muslims at war with them, those at peace, and those who join Islam: love is the default.
RFOaj6FMlSs.summary: He places al-Mumtahanah as the third surah of the cluster in the 28th juz that organizes Muslim life with others. The opening command not to show affection to those who are Allah's enemies and yours, he argues, only makes sense if love toward everyone is the Muslim default; the single exception is a group actively fighting Muslims, expelling them and trying to destroy their faith. Ibrahim had to break with his own father on these terms, and even then the believers pray not to become a cause of trial for their opponents. He dwells on the verse promising that Allah may yet place love between the believers and their enemies, noting it says love, not truce or tolerance. Verses 8 and 9 then state plainly that kindness and more-than-justice are owed to non-Muslims who neither fought nor expelled Muslims, and he criticizes extremists who dismiss these verses as abrogated. The rulings on women who emigrate show that a woman chooses her own faith, with dowries settled fairly in both directions. The pledge taken from new Muslims is a short social contract of core ethics. He asks the audience to read the verses themselves and live by them.

outline.heading: Opening
Al-Mumtahanah in the organizing cluster of the 28th juz
outline.gist: The cluster condenses earlier long surahs; this one organizes relations with non-Muslims at war, non-Muslims at peace, and people who switch over to Islam.

outline.heading: An enemy who expelled you: no secret alliance
outline.gist: The enemy here fought the Muslims and drove them from their homes; siding with them in secret is a mistake, and kinship will not protect you from their harm.

outline.heading: Why 'do not show them love' proves love is the default
outline.gist: Feelings are not addressed, only conduct; the wording only makes sense if Muslims normally show love to all people, with one hostile group excepted.

outline.heading: The example of Ibrahim and his father
outline.gist: Ibrahim and his followers stood apart from a people trying to force them out of their faith; he kept praying for his father until told to stop while the father persisted in hostility.

outline.heading: Do not make us a trial for those who disbelieve
outline.gist: The Companions had learned to love all and needed convincing; the prayer asks that there be no fighting that would bring punishment upon the other side.

outline.heading: Allah may place love between you and your enemies
outline.gist: The verse says love, not peace or tolerance; keep behaving rightly and defending yourself, and Allah is able to turn enmity into love and forgive the past.

outline.heading: How the Quran asks Muslims to see non-Muslims
outline.gist: Unless people declare war on Islam they receive love; even from those who do, love is only withheld while praying for the day it returns.

outline.heading: Interlude
Extremists who call these verses abrogated
outline.gist: Those on the extreme side of behaviour simply declare these explicit verses no longer in force.

outline.heading: Birr and more-than-justice for peaceful non-Muslims
outline.gist: Birr is the word used for treatment of parents, and qist means justice with tenderness, giving what is owed and more; Allah loves those who do this.

outline.heading: No alliance with those who fought and expelled you
outline.gist: Only alliance is forbidden, and only with those who declared war, expelled Muslims or helped others do so; allying with them makes you an oppressor too.

outline.heading: Interlude
Believing women who emigrate: verify, then do not return them
outline.gist: Be careful about spies, but once a woman's faith is established she is not sent back to people who would oppress her.

outline.heading: Repaying the dowry to the hostile husband
outline.gist: Even a husband from a hostile camp is repaid his dowry, because she has the right to go where she wants and believe what she wants.

outline.heading: A wife who leaves Islam: claim the dowry, not her
outline.gist: The same principle runs the other way: she may leave, and only the financial right is pursued, which shows women's freedom of choice in religion.

outline.heading: The pledge of new Muslims and the closing verse
outline.gist: Newcomers agree to six points of basic ethics; the last verse repeats the ban on allying with those who show hostility.

outline.heading: Women's status recurs across this cluster
outline.gist: Organizing Muslim life requires addressing women's rights, which appear in nearly every surah of the cluster starting with al-Mujadilah.

outline.heading: The pledge as a minimum social contract
outline.gist: No shirk, no killing, stealing, zina or social sins, and support for whatever good the society promotes; rituals come later between them and Allah, but living together needs shared ethics.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Tolerance, pluralism and dealing with difference
themes.note: Love toward all people is the Muslim default; only an actively hostile group is excepted, and even then Muslims pray for love to return.

themes.label: Tolerance, pluralism and dealing with difference
themes.note: Verses 8 and 9 explicitly command birr and more-than-justice toward peaceful non-Muslims and forbid only alliance with aggressors.

themes.label: Extremism, bad religiosity and distorted practice
themes.note: Extremist behaviour rests on declaring these clear verses abrogated, which he rejects.

themes.label: Justice and refusing oppression
themes.note: Allying with oppressors makes you one of them; qist is justice plus kindness.

themes.label: Gender relations, chastity and modesty
themes.note: The emigrant women verses establish a woman's right to choose her faith and settle dowries fairly; women's status runs through the cluster.

themes.label: Stories of earlier prophets
themes.note: Ibrahim's break with his father shows the limit case of hostility over faith.

themes.label: Community building, cooperation and the ummah
themes.note: The pledge sets the shared ethical minimum people need to live together and support good initiatives in society.

maxims: The default for Muslims is to show love to everybody
Not peace, not a truce: the word was love

stories.point: Even a prophet had to stand apart from family who tried to coerce him out of his faith, while continuing to pray for him as long as he could.

takeaways: Treat non-Muslims who are not at war with Islam with kindness that goes beyond strict justice.
Withhold alliance only from those actively fighting or oppressing Muslims, and still pray that love replaces enmity.
Read verses 60:8-9 yourself rather than accepting claims that they are abrogated.
Respect a person's freedom to choose their faith and settle financial rights fairly.
Support the good initiatives of the society you live in.

47:1.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَصَدُّواْ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ أَضَلَّ أَعۡمَٰلَهُمۡ
47:1.en: Those who disbelieve and turn (men) from the way of Allah, He rendereth their actions vain

47:2.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَءَامَنُواْ بِمَا نُزِّلَ عَلَىٰ مُحَمَّدࣲ وَهُوَ ٱلۡحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّهِمۡ كَفَّرَ عَنۡهُمۡ سَيِّـَٔاتِهِمۡ وَأَصۡلَحَ بَالَهُمۡ
47:2.en: And those who believe and do good works and believe in that which is revealed unto Muhammad - and it is the truth from their Lord - He riddeth them of their ill-deeds and improveth their state

47:3.ar: ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ ٱتَّبَعُواْ ٱلۡبَٰطِلَ وَأَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱتَّبَعُواْ ٱلۡحَقَّ مِن رَّبِّهِمۡۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يَضۡرِبُ ٱللَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ أَمۡثَٰلَهُمۡ
47:3.en: That is because those who disbelieve follow falsehood and because those who believe follow the truth from their Lord. Thus Allah coineth their similitudes for mankind

47:4.ar: فَإِذَا لَقِيتُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ فَضَرۡبَ ٱلرِّقَابِ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَآ أَثۡخَنتُمُوهُمۡ فَشُدُّواْ ٱلۡوَثَاقَ فَإِمَّا مَنَّۢا بَعۡدُ وَإِمَّا فِدَآءً حَتَّىٰ تَضَعَ ٱلۡحَرۡبُ أَوۡزَارَهَاۚ ذَٰلِكَۖ وَلَوۡ يَشَآءُ ٱللَّهُ لَٱنتَصَرَ مِنۡهُمۡ وَلَٰكِن لِّيَبۡلُوَاْ بَعۡضَكُم بِبَعۡضࣲۗ وَٱلَّذِينَ قُتِلُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ فَلَن يُضِلَّ أَعۡمَٰلَهُمۡ
47:4.en: Now when ye meet in battle those who disbelieve, then it is smiting of the necks until, when ye have routed them, then making fast of bonds; and afterward either grace or ransom till the war lay down its burdens. That (is the ordinance). And if Allah willed He could have punished them (without you) but (thus it is ordained) that He may try some of you by means of others. And those who are slain in the way of Allah, He rendereth not their actions vain

47:5.en: He will guide them and improve their state

47:6.en: And bring them in unto the Garden which He hath made known to them

47:7.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِن تَنصُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ يَنصُرۡكُمۡ وَيُثَبِّتۡ أَقۡدَامَكُمۡ
47:7.en: O ye who believe! If ye help Allah, He will help you and will make your foothold firm

47:8.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ فَتَعۡسࣰ ا لَّهُمۡ وَأَضَلَّ أَعۡمَٰلَهُمۡ
47:8.en: And those who disbelieve, perdition is for them, and He will make their actions vain

47:9.ar: ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمۡ كَرِهُواْ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ فَأَحۡبَطَ أَعۡمَٰلَهُمۡ
47:9.en: That is because they are averse to that which Allah hath revealed, therefor maketh He their actions fruitless

47:10.ar: ۞أَفَلَمۡ يَسِيرُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَيَنظُرُواْ كَيۡفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡۖ دَمَّرَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِمۡۖ وَلِلۡكَٰفِرِينَ أَمۡثَٰلُهَا
47:10.en: Have they not travelled in the land to see the nature of the consequence for those who were before them? Allah wiped them out. And for the disbelievers there will be the like thereof

47:11.ar: ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَوۡلَى ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَأَنَّ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ لَا مَوۡلَىٰ لَهُمۡ
47:11.en: That is because Allah is patron of those who believe, and because the disbelievers have no patron

47:12.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُدۡخِلُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ جَنَّٰتࣲ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُۖ وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ يَتَمَتَّعُونَ وَيَأۡكُلُونَ كَمَا تَأۡكُلُ ٱلۡأَنۡعَٰمُ وَٱلنَّارُ مَثۡوࣰ ى لَّهُمۡ
47:12.en: Lo! Allah will cause those who believe and do good works to enter Gardens underneath which rivers flow; while those who disbelieve take their comfort in this life and eat even as the cattle eat, and the Fire is their habitation

47:13.ar: وَكَأَيِّن مِّن قَرۡيَةٍ هِيَ أَشَدُّ قُوَّةࣰ مِّن قَرۡيَتِكَ ٱلَّتِيٓ أَخۡرَجَتۡكَ أَهۡلَكۡنَٰهُمۡ فَلَا نَاصِرَ لَهُمۡ
47:13.en: And how many a township stronger than thy township (O Muhammad) which hath cast thee out, have We destroyed, and they had no helper

47:14.ar: أَفَمَن كَانَ عَلَىٰ بَيِّنَةࣲ مِّن رَّبِّهِۦ كَمَن زُيِّنَ لَهُۥ سُوٓءُ عَمَلِهِۦ وَٱتَّبَعُوٓاْ أَهۡوَآءَهُم
47:14.en: Is he who relieth on a clear proof from his Lord like those for whom the evil that they do is beautified while they follow their own lusts

47:15.ar: مَّثَلُ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ ٱلَّتِي وُعِدَ ٱلۡمُتَّقُونَۖ فِيهَآ أَنۡهَٰرࣱ مِّن مَّآءٍ غَيۡرِ ءَاسِنࣲ وَأَنۡهَٰرࣱ مِّن لَّبَنࣲ لَّمۡ يَتَغَيَّرۡ طَعۡمُهُۥ وَأَنۡهَٰرࣱ مِّنۡ خَمۡرࣲ لَّذَّةࣲ لِّلشَّٰرِبِينَ وَأَنۡهَٰرࣱ مِّنۡ عَسَلࣲ مُّصَفࣰّ ىۖ وَلَهُمۡ فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ وَمَغۡفِرَةࣱ مِّن رَّبِّهِمۡۖ كَمَنۡ هُوَ خَٰلِدࣱ فِي ٱلنَّارِ وَسُقُواْ مَآءً حَمِيمࣰ ا فَقَطَّعَ أَمۡعَآءَهُمۡ
47:15.en: A similitude of the Garden which those who keep their duty (to Allah) are promised: Therein are rivers of water unpolluted, and rivers of milk whereof the flavour changeth not, and rivers of wine delicious to the drinkers, and rivers of clear-run honey; therein for them is every kind of fruit, with pardon from their Lord. (Are those who enjoy all this) like those who are immortal in the Fire and are given boiling water to drink so that it teareth their bowels

47:16.ar: وَمِنۡهُم مَّن يَسۡتَمِعُ إِلَيۡكَ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا خَرَجُواْ مِنۡ عِندِكَ قَالُواْ لِلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡعِلۡمَ مَاذَا قَالَ ءَانِفًاۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ طَبَعَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمۡ وَٱتَّبَعُوٓاْ أَهۡوَآءَهُمۡ
47:16.en: Among them are some who give ear unto thee (Muhammad) till, when they go forth from thy presence they say unto those who have been given knowledge: What was that he said just now? Those are they whose hearts Allah hath sealed, and they follow their own lusts

47:17.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ ٱهۡتَدَوۡاْ زَادَهُمۡ هُدࣰ ى وَءَاتَىٰهُمۡ تَقۡوَىٰهُمۡ
47:17.en: While as for those who walk aright, He addeth to their guidance, and giveth them their protection (against evil)

47:18.ar: فَهَلۡ يَنظُرُونَ إِلَّا ٱلسَّاعَةَ أَن تَأۡتِيَهُم بَغۡتَةࣰۖ فَقَدۡ جَآءَ أَشۡرَاطُهَاۚ فَأَنَّىٰ لَهُمۡ إِذَا جَآءَتۡهُمۡ ذِكۡرَىٰهُمۡ
47:18.en: Await they aught save the Hour, that it should come upon them unawares? And the beginnings thereof have already come. But how, when it hath come upon them, can they take their warning

47:19.ar: فَٱعۡلَمۡ أَنَّهُۥ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ وَٱسۡتَغۡفِرۡ لِذَنۢبِكَ وَلِلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِۗ وَٱللَّهُ يَعۡلَمُ مُتَقَلَّبَكُمۡ وَمَثۡوَىٰكُمۡ
47:19.en: So know (O Muhammad) that there is no Allah save Allah, and ask forgiveness for thy sin and for believing men and believing women. Allah knoweth (both) your place of turmoil and your place of rest

47:20.ar: وَيَقُولُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَوۡلَا نُزِّلَتۡ سُورَةࣱۖ فَإِذَآ أُنزِلَتۡ سُورَةࣱ مُّحۡكَمَةࣱ وَذُكِرَ فِيهَا ٱلۡقِتَالُ رَأَيۡتَ ٱلَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضࣱ يَنظُرُونَ إِلَيۡكَ نَظَرَ ٱلۡمَغۡشِيِّ عَلَيۡهِ مِنَ ٱلۡمَوۡتِۖ فَأَوۡلَىٰ لَهُمۡ
47:20.en: And those who believe say: If only a surah were revealed! But when a decisive surah is revealed and war is mentioned therein, thou seest those in whose hearts is a disease looking at thee with the look of men fainting unto death. Therefor woe unto them

47:21.ar: طَاعَةࣱ وَقَوۡلࣱ مَّعۡرُوفࣱۚ فَإِذَا عَزَمَ ٱلۡأَمۡرُ فَلَوۡ صَدَقُواْ ٱللَّهَ لَكَانَ خَيۡرࣰ ا لَّهُمۡ
47:21.en: Obedience and a civil word. Then, when the matter is determined, if they are loyal to Allah it will be well for them

47:22.ar: فَهَلۡ عَسَيۡتُمۡ إِن تَوَلَّيۡتُمۡ أَن تُفۡسِدُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَتُقَطِّعُوٓاْ أَرۡحَامَكُمۡ
47:22.en: Would ye then, if ye were given the command, work corruption in the land and sever your ties of kinship

47:23.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ لَعَنَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ فَأَصَمَّهُمۡ وَأَعۡمَىٰٓ أَبۡصَٰرَهُمۡ
47:23.en: Such are they whom Allah curseth so that He deafeneth them and maketh blind their eyes

47:24.ar: أَفَلَا يَتَدَبَّرُونَ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ أَمۡ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبٍ أَقۡفَالُهَآ
47:24.en: Will they then not meditate on the Qur'an, or are there locks on the hearts

47:25.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱرۡتَدُّواْ عَلَىٰٓ أَدۡبَٰرِهِم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُمُ ٱلۡهُدَى ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ سَوَّلَ لَهُمۡ وَأَمۡلَىٰ لَهُمۡ
47:25.en: Lo! those who turn back after the guidance hath been manifested unto them, Satan hath seduced them, and He giveth them the rein

47:26.ar: ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمۡ قَالُواْ لِلَّذِينَ كَرِهُواْ مَا نَزَّلَ ٱللَّهُ سَنُطِيعُكُمۡ فِي بَعۡضِ ٱلۡأَمۡرِۖ وَٱللَّهُ يَعۡلَمُ إِسۡرَارَهُمۡ
47:26.en: That is because they say unto those who hate what Allah hath revealed: We will obey you in some matters; and Allah knoweth their secret talk

47:27.ar: فَكَيۡفَ إِذَا تَوَفَّتۡهُمُ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ يَضۡرِبُونَ وُجُوهَهُمۡ وَأَدۡبَٰرَهُمۡ
47:27.en: Then how (will it be with them) when the angels gather them, smiting their faces and their backs

47:28.ar: ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمُ ٱتَّبَعُواْ مَآ أَسۡخَطَ ٱللَّهَ وَكَرِهُواْ رِضۡوَٰنَهُۥ فَأَحۡبَطَ أَعۡمَٰلَهُمۡ
47:28.en: That will be because they followed that which angereth Allah, and hated that which pleaseth Him. Therefor He hath made their actions vain

47:29.ar: أَمۡ حَسِبَ ٱلَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضٌ أَن لَّن يُخۡرِجَ ٱللَّهُ أَضۡغَٰنَهُمۡ
47:29.en: Or do those in whose hearts is a disease deem that Allah will not bring to light their (secret) hates

47:30.ar: وَلَوۡ نَشَآءُ لَأَرَيۡنَٰكَهُمۡ فَلَعَرَفۡتَهُم بِسِيمَٰهُمۡۚ وَلَتَعۡرِفَنَّهُمۡ فِي لَحۡنِ ٱلۡقَوۡلِۚ وَٱللَّهُ يَعۡلَمُ أَعۡمَٰلَكُمۡ
47:30.en: And if We would, We could show them unto thee (Muhammad) so that thou shouldst know them surely by their marks. And thou shalt know them by the burden of their talk. And Allah knoweth your deeds

47:31.ar: وَلَنَبۡلُوَنَّكُمۡ حَتَّىٰ نَعۡلَمَ ٱلۡمُجَٰهِدِينَ مِنكُمۡ وَٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ وَنَبۡلُوَاْ أَخۡبَارَكُمۡ
47:31.en: And verily We shall try you till We know those of you who strive hard (for the cause of Allah) and the steadfast, and till We test your record

47:32.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَصَدُّواْ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَشَآقُّواْ ٱلرَّسُولَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُمُ ٱلۡهُدَىٰ لَن يَضُرُّواْ ٱللَّهَ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَسَيُحۡبِطُ أَعۡمَٰلَهُمۡ
47:32.en: Lo! those who disbelieve and turn from the way of Allah and oppose the messenger after the guidance hath been manifested unto them, they hurt Allah not a jot, and He will make their actions fruitless

47:33.ar: ۞يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ أَطِيعُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُواْ ٱلرَّسُولَ وَلَا تُبۡطِلُوٓاْ أَعۡمَٰلَكُمۡ
47:33.en: O ye who believe! Obey Allah and obey the messenger, and render not your actions vain

47:34.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَصَدُّواْ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ثُمَّ مَاتُواْ وَهُمۡ كُفَّارࣱ فَلَن يَغۡفِرَ ٱللَّهُ لَهُمۡ
47:34.en: Lo! those who disbelieve and turn from the way of Allah and then die disbelievers, Allah surely will not pardon them

47:35.ar: فَلَا تَهِنُواْ وَتَدۡعُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱلسَّلۡمِ وَأَنتُمُ ٱلۡأَعۡلَوۡنَ وَٱللَّهُ مَعَكُمۡ وَلَن يَتِرَكُمۡ أَعۡمَٰلَكُمۡ
47:35.en: So do not falter and cry out for peace when ye (will be) the uppermost, and Allah is with you, and He will not grudge (the reward of) your actions

47:36.ar: إِنَّمَا ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَا لَعِبࣱ وَلَهۡوࣱۚ وَإِن تُؤۡمِنُواْ وَتَتَّقُواْ يُؤۡتِكُمۡ أُجُورَكُمۡ وَلَا يَسۡـَٔلۡكُمۡ أَمۡوَٰلَكُمۡ
47:36.en: The life of the world is but a sport and a pastime. And if ye believe and ward off (evil). He will give you your wages, and will not ask of you your wordly wealth

47:37.ar: إِن يَسۡـَٔلۡكُمُوهَا فَيُحۡفِكُمۡ تَبۡخَلُواْ وَيُخۡرِجۡ أَضۡغَٰنَكُمۡ
47:37.en: If He should ask it of you and importune you, ye would hoard it, and He would bring to light your (secret) hates

47:38.ar: هَٰٓأَنتُمۡ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ تُدۡعَوۡنَ لِتُنفِقُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ فَمِنكُم مَّن يَبۡخَلُۖ وَمَن يَبۡخَلۡ فَإِنَّمَا يَبۡخَلُ عَن نَّفۡسِهِۦۚ وَٱللَّهُ ٱلۡغَنِيُّ وَأَنتُمُ ٱلۡفُقَرَآءُۚ وَإِن تَتَوَلَّوۡاْ يَسۡتَبۡدِلۡ قَوۡمًا غَيۡرَكُمۡ ثُمَّ لَا يَكُونُوٓاْ أَمۡثَٰلَكُم
47:38.en: Lo! ye are those who are called to spend in the way of Allah, yet among you there are some who hoard. And as for him who hoardeth, he hoardeth only from his soul. And Allah is the Rich, and ye are the poor. And if ye turn away He will exchange you for some other folk, and they will not be the likes of you

37:35.ar: إِنَّهُمۡ كَانُوٓاْ إِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمۡ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ يَسۡتَكۡبِرُونَ
37:35.en: For when it was said unto them, There is no Allah save Allah, they were scornful
