oVSqOIGTTZ0.title: Surat Muhammad Summary
oVSqOIGTTZ0.one_line: Surat Muhammad teaches that following the Prophet is what gets deeds accepted and lives made functional, tested by combat, money and honesty.
oVSqOIGTTZ0.summary: Surat Muhammad opens the ninth cluster, three surahs about the Prophet. Its theme is that following him is the only way to have deeds accepted and to make individuals and societies prosper. Acceptance is a forgotten part of good deeds: intention and effort are not enough. Disbelievers' deeds go astray, while believers who follow what Muhammad brought have their state set right, which he explains as being made functional. The surah is also called the surah of combat because the hardest test of following is being asked to risk your life; the rulings on fighting and captives show effort is the point, since Allah could grant victory instantly. At its centre stands the full phrase know that there is no god but Allah and seek forgiveness, a deep concept that should not become a cliche. When fighting was prescribed, those with diseased hearts panicked; believers today are not asked to fight, but must mean their commitment. Turning away corrupts the earth and severs ties, and Allah will expose hidden half-hearted following. The second test is money: Allah does not ask for all of it, because then people would refuse; everything He commands benefits us, as unhealthy food harms only after years. Whoever refuses will be replaced, and being used by Allah is the greatest blessing.

outline.heading: The ninth cluster: three surahs about the Prophet
outline.gist: Muhammad, Al-Fath and Al-Hujurat each present him from a different angle while turning the light on us.

outline.heading: The theme: following him is how deeds are accepted
outline.gist: His way is how individuals and societies prosper and how Allah accepts deeds.

outline.heading: Acceptance: the forgotten side of good deeds
outline.gist: Intention, time and effort are needed, but you must also ask whether the deed is accepted.

outline.heading: Deeds that go astray versus deeds that arrive
outline.gist: Disbelievers who obstruct his way lose their deeds; believers who follow what he brought are forgiven.

outline.heading: Setting their state right: made functional
outline.gist: The phrase means more than fixing affairs; it makes a person able to achieve their goals, because they followed truth.

outline.heading: Why it is called the surah of combat
outline.gist: Following someone is easy when it costs nothing; the pinnacle of following him is being willing to risk your life.

outline.heading: Rulings of battle and captives: the effort is the point
outline.gist: Fight with full strength, take captives, then free them by grace or ransom; Allah could give instant victory but wants you to prove you follow.

outline.heading: Allah is the protector of the believers
outline.gist: Commands come from care; those without Allah as their protector walk aimlessly.

outline.heading: What the people of Paradise will find
outline.gist: Following his way is how deeds are accepted and prosperity reached, leading to the rewards of Paradise.

outline.heading: The anchor verse: know there is no god but Allah
outline.gist: The full phrase appears only twice in the Quran; it is paired with seeking forgiveness because we are imperfect.

outline.heading: La ilaha illa Allah is not a cliche
outline.gist: It is a deep concept Islam is built on; connecting yourself to it is a lifetime's journey for individuals and communities.

outline.heading: Diseased hearts panic when fighting is prescribed
outline.gist: Half-hearted followers are terrified by the mere command; obedience and a right word would have been better for them.

outline.heading: Mean it: put your money where your mouth is
outline.gist: We are not being told to fight, but to be sincerely willing to follow him to the full extent of belief.

outline.heading: Turning away corrupts the earth and severs ties
outline.gist: Abandoning his way has natural long-term consequences: ruin on earth and broken relationships.

outline.heading: Do they not reflect on the Quran?
outline.gist: Everything commanded is for our benefit; a locked heart cannot see it.

outline.heading: Life will expose what is hidden
outline.gist: Those with half-hearted following think they will stay under the radar, but Allah tests until the truth comes out.

outline.heading: The surah as a mirror for self-honesty
outline.gist: Look inside honestly, and if your following is not real, work to change it.

outline.heading: Do not void your deeds
outline.gist: The believer's nightmare is arriving to find none of his deeds accepted because he did not follow properly.

outline.heading: Life is play, and He did not ask for all your wealth
outline.gist: Faith brings reward beyond imagination; had He asked for everything, people would have refused and been exposed.

outline.heading: Nothing commanded harms you; holding back deprives you
outline.gist: He could have commanded anything, yet asked only what benefits us; the stingy deprive only themselves.

outline.heading: Harm from not following comes slowly, like fried food
outline.gist: Combat and money are the two tests; the damage of abandoning his way may not appear for decades, but it comes.

outline.heading: If you turn away, you will be replaced
outline.gist: Being used by Allah to teach His deen is the greatest blessing; no one is essential, and the replacement will not be like you.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Obedience to Allah and the Messenger
themes.note: Following the Prophet is the condition for accepted deeds and a functional life.

themes.label: Intention and sincerity (niyyah, ikhlas)
themes.note: Acceptance of deeds is the forgotten dimension beyond intention and effort.

themes.label: Courage and commitment
themes.note: Willingness to give one's life is the pinnacle of following him.

themes.label: Tawhid and worship of Allah alone
themes.note: La ilaha illa Allah as the anchor of the surah and the foundation of Islam, not a cliche.

themes.label: Hypocrisy (nifaq)
themes.note: Half-hearted followers with diseased hearts panic at hard commands and will be exposed.

themes.label: Self-honesty and self-accountability (muhasabah)
themes.note: The surah holds a mirror up to how truly we follow him.

themes.label: Zakat, charity and giving
themes.note: Giving part of one's wealth is the second test of following, and holding back harms only oneself.

themes.label: Humility vs vanity and arrogance
themes.note: No one is essential to Islam; whoever turns away is replaced.

quran.point: The only other place the full phrase 'no god but Allah' appears.

maxims: Follow him so your deeds are accepted
Life will expose you
You will be replaced, no problem
Being Allah's tool is the best thing that can happen
takeaways: Ask whether your deeds are accepted, not just whether you did them
Reflect on what la ilaha illa Allah means for you and your community
Be honestly willing to follow the Prophet fully, even in what is costly
Give from your wealth; holding back deprives only you
Hold on to any role Allah gives you in serving His deen

57:1.ar: سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
57:1.en: All that is in the heavens and the earth glorifieth Allah; and He is the Mighty, the Wise

57:2.ar: لَهُۥ مُلۡكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ يُحۡيِۦ وَيُمِيتُۖ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرٌ
57:2.en: His is the Sovereignty of the heavens and the earth; He quickeneth and He giveth death; and He is Able to do all things

57:3.ar: هُوَ ٱلۡأَوَّلُ وَٱلۡأٓخِرُ وَٱلظَّٰهِرُ وَٱلۡبَاطِنُۖ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءٍ عَلِيمٌ
57:3.en: He is the First and the Last, and the Outward and the Inward; and He is Knower of all things

57:4.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامࣲ ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَوَىٰ عَلَى ٱلۡعَرۡشِۖ يَعۡلَمُ مَا يَلِجُ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا يَخۡرُجُ مِنۡهَا وَمَا يَنزِلُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَمَا يَعۡرُجُ فِيهَاۖ وَهُوَ مَعَكُمۡ أَيۡنَ مَا كُنتُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ بَصِيرࣱ‏
57:4.en: He it is Who created the heavens and the earth in six Days; then He mounted the Throne. He knoweth all that entereth the earth and all that emergeth therefrom and all that cometh down from the sky and all that ascendeth therein; and He is with you wheresoever ye may be. And Allah is Seer of what ye do

57:5.ar: لَّهُۥ مُلۡكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ وَإِلَى ٱللَّهِ تُرۡجَعُ ٱلۡأُمُورُ
57:5.en: His is the Sovereignty of the heavens and the earth, and unto Allah (all) things are brought back

57:6.ar: يُولِجُ ٱلَّيۡلَ فِي ٱلنَّهَارِ وَيُولِجُ ٱلنَّهَارَ فِي ٱلَّيۡلِۚ وَهُوَ عَلِيمُۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ
57:6.en: He causeth the night to pass into the day, and He causeth the day to pass into the night, and He is knower of all that is in the breasts

57:7.ar: ءَامِنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ وَأَنفِقُواْ مِمَّا جَعَلَكُم مُّسۡتَخۡلَفِينَ فِيهِۖ فَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مِنكُمۡ وَأَنفَقُواْ لَهُمۡ أَجۡرࣱ كَبِيرࣱ‏
57:7.en: Believe in Allah and His messenger, and spend of that whereof He hath made you trustees; and such of you as believe and spend (aright), theirs will be a great reward

57:8.ar: وَمَا لَكُمۡ لَا تُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلرَّسُولُ يَدۡعُوكُمۡ لِتُؤۡمِنُواْ بِرَبِّكُمۡ وَقَدۡ أَخَذَ مِيثَٰقَكُمۡ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ
57:8.en: What aileth you that ye believe not in Allah, when the messenger calleth you to believe in your Lord, and He hath already made a covenant with you, if ye are believers

57:9.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِي يُنَزِّلُ عَلَىٰ عَبۡدِهِۦٓ ءَايَٰتِۭ بَيِّنَٰتࣲ لِّيُخۡرِجَكُم مِّنَ ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ إِلَى ٱلنُّورِۚ وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِكُمۡ لَرَءُوفࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
57:9.en: He it is Who sendeth down clear revelations unto His slave, that He may bring you forth from darkness unto light; and lo! for you, Allah is Full of Pity, Merciful

57:10.ar: وَمَا لَكُمۡ أَلَّا تُنفِقُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَلِلَّهِ مِيرَٰثُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ لَا يَسۡتَوِي مِنكُم مَّنۡ أَنفَقَ مِن قَبۡلِ ٱلۡفَتۡحِ وَقَٰتَلَۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ أَعۡظَمُ دَرَجَةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَنفَقُواْ مِنۢ بَعۡدُ وَقَٰتَلُواْۚ وَكُلࣰّ ا وَعَدَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡحُسۡنَىٰۚ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ خَبِيرࣱ‏
57:10.en: And what aileth you that ye spend not in the way of Allah when unto Allah belongeth the inheritance of the heavens and the earth? Those who spent and fought before the victory are not upon a level (with the rest of you). Such are greater in rank than those who spent and fought afterwards. Unto each hath Allah promised good. And Allah is Informed of what ye do

57:11.ar: مَّن ذَا ٱلَّذِي يُقۡرِضُ ٱللَّهَ قَرۡضًا حَسَنࣰ ا فَيُضَٰعِفَهُۥ لَهُۥ وَلَهُۥٓ أَجۡرࣱ كَرِيمࣱ‏
57:11.en: Who is he that will lend unto Allah a goodly loan, that He may double it for him and his may be a rich reward

57:12.ar: يَوۡمَ تَرَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِ يَسۡعَىٰ نُورُهُم بَيۡنَ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَبِأَيۡمَٰنِهِمۖ بُشۡرَىٰكُمُ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ جَنَّٰتࣱ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَاۚ ذَٰلِكَ هُوَ ٱلۡفَوۡزُ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ
57:12.en: On the day when thou (Muhammad) wilt see the believers, men and women, their light shining forth before them and on their right hands, (and wilt hear it said unto them): Glad news for you this day: Gardens underneath which rivers flow, wherein ye are immortal. That is the supreme triumph

57:13.ar: يَوۡمَ يَقُولُ ٱلۡمُنَٰفِقُونَ وَٱلۡمُنَٰفِقَٰتُ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱنظُرُونَا نَقۡتَبِسۡ مِن نُّورِكُمۡ قِيلَ ٱرۡجِعُواْ وَرَآءَكُمۡ فَٱلۡتَمِسُواْ نُورࣰ اۖ فَضُرِبَ بَيۡنَهُم بِسُورࣲ لَّهُۥ بَابُۢ بَاطِنُهُۥ فِيهِ ٱلرَّحۡمَةُ وَظَٰهِرُهُۥ مِن قِبَلِهِ ٱلۡعَذَابُ
57:13.en: On the day when the hypocritical men and the hypocritical women will say unto those who believe: Look on us that we may borrow from your light! it will be said: Go back and seek for light! Then there will separate them a wall wherein is a gate, the inner side whereof containeth mercy, while the outer side thereof is toward the doom

57:14.ar: يُنَادُونَهُمۡ أَلَمۡ نَكُن مَّعَكُمۡۖ قَالُواْ بَلَىٰ وَلَٰكِنَّكُمۡ فَتَنتُمۡ أَنفُسَكُمۡ وَتَرَبَّصۡتُمۡ وَٱرۡتَبۡتُمۡ وَغَرَّتۡكُمُ ٱلۡأَمَانِيُّ حَتَّىٰ جَآءَ أَمۡرُ ٱللَّهِ وَغَرَّكُم بِٱللَّهِ ٱلۡغَرُورُ
57:14.en: They will cry unto them (saying): Were we not with you? They will say: Yea, verily; but ye tempted one another, and hesitated, and doubted, and vain desires beguiled you till the ordinance of Allah came to pass; and the deceiver deceived you concerning Allah

57:15.ar: فَٱلۡيَوۡمَ لَا يُؤۡخَذُ مِنكُمۡ فِدۡيَةࣱ وَلَا مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْۚ مَأۡوَىٰكُمُ ٱلنَّارُۖ هِيَ مَوۡلَىٰكُمۡۖ وَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
57:15.en: So this day no ransom can be taken from you nor from those who disbelieved. Your home is the Fire; that is your patron, and a hapless journey's end

57:16.ar: ۞أَلَمۡ يَأۡنِ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ أَن تَخۡشَعَ قُلُوبُهُمۡ لِذِكۡرِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا نَزَلَ مِنَ ٱلۡحَقِّ وَلَا يَكُونُواْ كَٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ مِن قَبۡلُ فَطَالَ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡأَمَدُ فَقَسَتۡ قُلُوبُهُمۡۖ وَكَثِيرࣱ مِّنۡهُمۡ فَٰسِقُونَ
57:16.en: Is not the time ripe for the hearts of those who believe to submit to Allah's reminder and to the truth which is revealed, that they become not as those who received the scripture of old but the term was prolonged for them and so their hearts were hardened, and many of them are evil-livers

57:17.ar: ٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحۡيِ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ بَعۡدَ مَوۡتِهَاۚ قَدۡ بَيَّنَّا لَكُمُ ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَعۡقِلُونَ
57:17.en: Know that Allah quickeneth the earth after its death. We have made clear Our revelations for you, that haply ye may understand

57:18.ar: إِنَّ ٱلۡمُصَّدِّقِينَ وَٱلۡمُصَّدِّقَٰتِ وَأَقۡرَضُواْ ٱللَّهَ قَرۡضًا حَسَنࣰ ا يُضَٰعَفُ لَهُمۡ وَلَهُمۡ أَجۡرࣱ كَرِيمࣱ‏
57:18.en: Lo! those who give alms, both men and women, and lend unto Allah a goodly loan, it will be doubled for them, and theirs will be a rich reward

57:19.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِۦٓ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلصِّدِّيقُونَۖ وَٱلشُّهَدَآءُ عِندَ رَبِّهِمۡ لَهُمۡ أَجۡرُهُمۡ وَنُورُهُمۡۖ وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَكَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ أَصۡحَٰبُ ٱلۡجَحِيمِ
57:19.en: And those who believe in Allah and His messengers, they are the loyal, and the martyrs are with their Lord; they have their reward and their light; while as for those who disbelieve and deny Our revelations, they are owners of hell-fire

57:20.ar: ٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّمَا ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَا لَعِبࣱ وَلَهۡوࣱ وَزِينَةࣱ وَتَفَاخُرُۢ بَيۡنَكُمۡ وَتَكَاثُرࣱ فِي ٱلۡأَمۡوَٰلِ وَٱلۡأَوۡلَٰدِۖ كَمَثَلِ غَيۡثٍ أَعۡجَبَ ٱلۡكُفَّارَ نَبَاتُهُۥ ثُمَّ يَهِيجُ فَتَرَىٰهُ مُصۡفَرࣰّ ا ثُمَّ يَكُونُ حُطَٰمࣰ اۖ وَفِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ عَذَابࣱ شَدِيدࣱ وَمَغۡفِرَةࣱ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرِضۡوَٰنࣱۚ وَمَا ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَآ إِلَّا مَتَٰعُ ٱلۡغُرُورِ
57:20.en: Know that the life of the world is only play, and idle talk, and pageantry, and boasting among you, and rivalry in respect of wealth and children; as the likeness of vegetation after rain, whereof the growth is pleasing to the husbandman, but afterward it drieth up and thou seest it turning yellow, then it becometh straw. And in the Hereafter there is grievous punishment, and (also) forgiveness from Allah and His good pleasure, whereas the life of the world is but matter of illusion

57:21.ar: سَابِقُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ مَغۡفِرَةࣲ مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡ وَجَنَّةٍ عَرۡضُهَا كَعَرۡضِ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ أُعِدَّتۡ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِۦۚ ذَٰلِكَ فَضۡلُ ٱللَّهِ يُؤۡتِيهِ مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَٱللَّهُ ذُو ٱلۡفَضۡلِ ٱلۡعَظِيمِ
57:21.en: Race one with another for forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden whereof the breadth is as the breadth of the heavens and the earth, which is in store for those who believe in Allah and His messengers. Such is the bounty of Allah, which He bestoweth upon whom He will, and Allah is of Infinite Bounty

57:22.ar: مَآ أَصَابَ مِن مُّصِيبَةࣲ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَا فِيٓ أَنفُسِكُمۡ إِلَّا فِي كِتَٰبࣲ مِّن قَبۡلِ أَن نَّبۡرَأَهَآۚ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ يَسِيرࣱ‏
57:22.en: Naught of disaster befalleth in the earth or in yourselves but it is in a Book before we bring it into being - Lo! that is easy for Allah

57:23.ar: لِّكَيۡلَا تَأۡسَوۡاْ عَلَىٰ مَا فَاتَكُمۡ وَلَا تَفۡرَحُواْ بِمَآ ءَاتَىٰكُمۡۗ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ مُخۡتَالࣲ فَخُورٍ
57:23.en: That ye grieve not for the sake of that which hath escaped you, nor yet exult because of that which hath been given. Allah loveth not all prideful boasters

57:24.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَبۡخَلُونَ وَيَأۡمُرُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ بِٱلۡبُخۡلِۗ وَمَن يَتَوَلَّ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلۡغَنِيُّ ٱلۡحَمِيدُ
57:24.en: Who hoard and who enjoin upon the people avarice. And whosoever turneth away, still Allah is the Absolute, the Owner of Praise

57:25.ar: لَقَدۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا رُسُلَنَا بِٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتِ وَأَنزَلۡنَا مَعَهُمُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَٱلۡمِيزَانَ لِيَقُومَ ٱلنَّاسُ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِۖ وَأَنزَلۡنَا ٱلۡحَدِيدَ فِيهِ بَأۡسࣱ شَدِيدࣱ وَمَنَٰفِعُ لِلنَّاسِ وَلِيَعۡلَمَ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَنصُرُهُۥ وَرُسُلَهُۥ بِٱلۡغَيۡبِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَوِيٌّ عَزِيزࣱ‏
57:25.en: We verily sent Our messengers with clear proofs, and revealed with them the Scripture and the Balance, that mankind may observe right measure; and He revealed iron, wherein is mighty power and (many) uses for mankind, and that Allah may know him who helpeth Him and His messengers, though unseen. Lo! Allah is Strong, Almighty

57:26.ar: وَلَقَدۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا نُوحࣰ ا وَإِبۡرَٰهِيمَ وَجَعَلۡنَا فِي ذُرِّيَّتِهِمَا ٱلنُّبُوَّةَ وَٱلۡكِتَٰبَۖ فَمِنۡهُم مُّهۡتَدࣲۖ وَكَثِيرࣱ مِّنۡهُمۡ فَٰسِقُونَ
57:26.en: And We verily sent Noah and Abraham and placed the prophethood and the scripture among their seed, and among them there is he who goeth right, but many of them are evil-livers

57:27.ar: ثُمَّ قَفَّيۡنَا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَٰرِهِم بِرُسُلِنَا وَقَفَّيۡنَا بِعِيسَى ٱبۡنِ مَرۡيَمَ وَءَاتَيۡنَٰهُ ٱلۡإِنجِيلَۖ وَجَعَلۡنَا فِي قُلُوبِ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّبَعُوهُ رَأۡفَةࣰ وَرَحۡمَةࣰۚ وَرَهۡبَانِيَّةً ٱبۡتَدَعُوهَا مَا كَتَبۡنَٰهَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ إِلَّا ٱبۡتِغَآءَ رِضۡوَٰنِ ٱللَّهِ فَمَا رَعَوۡهَا حَقَّ رِعَايَتِهَاۖ فَـَٔاتَيۡنَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مِنۡهُمۡ أَجۡرَهُمۡۖ وَكَثِيرࣱ مِّنۡهُمۡ فَٰسِقُونَ
57:27.en: Then We caused Our messengers to follow in their footsteps; and We caused Jesus, son of Mary, to follow, and gave him the Gospel, and placed compassion and mercy in the hearts of those who followed him. But monasticism they invented - We ordained it not for them - only seeking Allah's pleasure, and they observed it not with right observance. So We give those of them who believe their reward, but many of them are evil-livers

57:28.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَءَامِنُواْ بِرَسُولِهِۦ يُؤۡتِكُمۡ كِفۡلَيۡنِ مِن رَّحۡمَتِهِۦ وَيَجۡعَل لَّكُمۡ نُورࣰ ا تَمۡشُونَ بِهِۦ وَيَغۡفِرۡ لَكُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
57:28.en: O ye who believe! Be mindful of your duty to Allah and put faith in His messenger. He will give you twofold of His mercy and will appoint for you a light wherein ye shall walk, and will forgive you. Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

57:29.ar: لِّئَلَّا يَعۡلَمَ أَهۡلُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ أَلَّا يَقۡدِرُونَ عَلَىٰ شَيۡءࣲ مِّن فَضۡلِ ٱللَّهِ وَأَنَّ ٱلۡفَضۡلَ بِيَدِ ٱللَّهِ يُؤۡتِيهِ مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَٱللَّهُ ذُو ٱلۡفَضۡلِ ٱلۡعَظِيمِ
57:29.en: That the People of the Scripture may know that they control naught of the bounty of Allah, but that the bounty is in Allah's hand to give to whom He will. And Allah is of Infinite Bounty

7:32.ar: قُلۡ مَنۡ حَرَّمَ زِينَةَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّتِيٓ أَخۡرَجَ لِعِبَادِهِۦ وَٱلطَّيِّبَٰتِ مِنَ ٱلرِّزۡقِۚ قُلۡ هِيَ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ فِي ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا خَالِصَةࣰ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِۗ كَذَٰلِكَ نُفَصِّلُ ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ لِقَوۡمࣲ يَعۡلَمُونَ
7:32.en: Say: Who hath forbidden the adornment of Allah which He hath brought forth for His bondmen, and the good things of His providing? Say: Such, on the Day of Resurrection, will be only for those who believed during the life of the world. Thus do we detail Our revelations for people who have knowledge

w0ykYu3KNgQ.title: Surat Al-Hadid Summary
w0ykYu3KNgQ.one_line: Al-Hadid closes the cluster by asking not for a choice but for a balance between the spiritual and the material.
w0ykYu3KNgQ.summary: Al-Hadid is the last surah of the cluster from Qaf, and unlike the others it does not ask us to choose one side over another. It asks us to balance spirituality and materialism, which people treat as opposites but which belong together. The opening verses describe Allah as the First and the Last, the Outward and the Inward, and say He is with us wherever we are, by His knowledge and attributes rather than physically. The command to believe and to spend from what you hold in trust pairs a spiritual act with a material one. Two men giving the same 200 dinars before and after the conquest of Makkah are not equal, because the earlier one gave in poverty and fear. On the Day of Judgment the believers' light reflects what settled in their hearts, while the hypocrites, who were with them in body but not in spirit, are shut out behind a wall. He calls the verse saying Allah revives the earth after its death the most hopeful in the Quran, since He can revive a dead heart too. Worldly play, adornment and rivalry are not forbidden, but absorption in them hardens hearts. The surah ends with iron and the balance, and rejects monasticism, because neglecting either body or soul breaks the balance.

outline.heading: Opening
The last surah of the cluster: a balance, not a choice
outline.gist: Unlike the earlier surahs, Al-Hadid asks us to balance two things rather than pick one.

outline.heading: The First and the Last, the Outward and the Inward
outline.gist: The opening glorification and names of Allah, which look like opposites but meet in Him.

outline.heading: Materialism and spirituality are not opposites
outline.gist: He is with you wherever you are; the two sides are closer than people treat them.

outline.heading: Believe and spend from what you hold in trust
outline.gist: Wealth is in your hands only for a while before it passes to others.

outline.heading: Why not spend? Before and after the conquest
outline.gist: Allah inherits the heavens and earth; those who spent and fought before the conquest are greater in rank.

outline.heading: Same amount, different weight
outline.gist: The spiritual state behind giving changes its value, even with no inflation in a gold currency.

outline.heading: The believers' light and the wall
outline.gist: Hypocrites beg to borrow light, are told to go back, and a wall with a gate separates mercy from punishment.

outline.heading: Were we not with you?
outline.gist: They were with the believers physically but not spiritually.

outline.heading: The Qaf to Al-Hadid cluster recapped in Arabic
outline.gist: Each surah raised deep questions that call for years of reflection and a change in thought and behaviour; Al-Hadid asks for balance.

outline.heading: Opposites in Allah's names; with you by His knowledge
outline.gist: There is a material and a spiritual understanding of these names; His being with us is by knowledge and attributes.

outline.heading: The first six verses and the trust of wealth
outline.gist: People of spiritual training dwell on these verses for years; your wealth belongs to Allah and you are a trustee.

outline.heading: Faith and spending paired
outline.gist: Here faith is paired with spending rather than prayer and zakah, joining a spiritual act with a material one.

outline.heading: Two hundred dinars before and after the conquest
outline.gist: The earlier giver gave in poverty, fear and weakness, the later in victory, so they are not equal.

outline.heading: Light as the reflection of the heart
outline.gist: The believers' light reflects what settled in their hearts; the wall's inner and outer sides echo the Outward and the Inward.

outline.heading: With them in body, not in spirit
outline.gist: Loving Allah without praying, or praying without love, does not benefit; body and spirit must go together.

outline.heading: Has the time not come for hearts to humble?
outline.gist: Hearts can die spiritually, and Allah who revives dead earth can revive them.

outline.heading: Interlude
The verse that troubled the companions
outline.gist: The rebuke in 'has the time not come' unsettled even the companions, so what of us?

outline.heading: The most hopeful verse
outline.gist: As Allah revives the earth with a little water, He revives a heart that no longer feels near or far.

outline.heading: Life as play, adornment and rivalry
outline.gist: None of these is forbidden; they are the reality of material life, beside which stands the spiritual side.

outline.heading: Hearts hardened like stone
outline.gist: Absorption in play and accumulation leaves people unmoved by the Quran, the suffering of orphans and widows, or long prayer.

outline.heading: Messengers, scripture, the balance and iron
outline.gist: Revelation and the balance were sent so people uphold justice; iron brings strength and benefit.

outline.heading: Isa's followers: compassion and invented monasticism
outline.gist: Allah placed compassion and mercy in their hearts, but monasticism was their own innovation.

outline.heading: Monasticism cannot be sustained
outline.gist: Refusing the physical side of life, such as marriage, is impossible to observe properly; ignoring either side breaks life.

outline.heading: The surah's close: iron for defence and benefit
outline.gist: After urging spirituality, the surah reminds us it is about balance, not preferring one thing over another.

outline.heading: The starving soul
outline.gist: A body dies after weeks without food; a soul starved for years produces hardness, envy and backbiting, yet Allah revives dead earth.

themes.label: Moderation and balance (wasatiyyah)
themes.note: The surah asks for a balance between spirituality and materialism rather than a choice.

themes.label: Moderation and balance (wasatiyyah)
themes.note: Iron, the balance and the rejection of monasticism show that neglecting body or soul breaks the balance.

themes.label: Spirituality, khushoo and the inner life
themes.note: Hearts can die and harden; Allah revives them as He revives dead earth.

themes.label: The Names and Attributes of Allah
themes.note: The First, the Last, the Outward and the Inward, and His being with us by knowledge.

themes.label: Zakat, charity and giving
themes.note: Spending as a trustee; the inner state behind giving changes its worth.

themes.label: Hypocrisy (nifaq)
themes.note: The hypocrites were with the believers in body but not in spirit.

themes.label: Wealth, asceticism (zuhd), consumerism and money
themes.note: Worldly adornment and rivalry are permitted but absorb and harden the heart.

themes.label: Extremism, bad religiosity and distorted practice
themes.note: Monasticism as excessive spirituality that Allah did not prescribe.

quran.point: Adornment is not forbidden: who has forbidden the adornment Allah brought forth?

hadith.gist: The companions blamed one another after 'has the time not come' was revealed, asking what they had done to deserve it

maxims: Not a choice, but a balance.
With them in body, not in spirit.
Allah revives a dead heart as He revives dead earth.

stories.who: Two men giving 200 dinars before and after the conquest of Makkah
stories.point: The spiritual state behind a deed changes its value even when the amount is the same.

stories.who: The followers of Isa and monasticism
stories.point: Over-spirituality that rejects the body cannot be sustained and was not prescribed.

takeaways: Pair faith with real spending from your wealth.
Be present with the community in spirit, not only in body.
If your heart feels dead, turn back: Allah revives hearts as He revives the earth.
Enjoy the permitted parts of life without letting them harden your heart.
Do not neglect either your body or your soul.

63:1.ar: إِذَا جَآءَكَ ٱلۡمُنَٰفِقُونَ قَالُواْ نَشۡهَدُ إِنَّكَ لَرَسُولُ ٱللَّهِۗ وَٱللَّهُ يَعۡلَمُ إِنَّكَ لَرَسُولُهُۥ وَٱللَّهُ يَشۡهَدُ إِنَّ ٱلۡمُنَٰفِقِينَ لَكَٰذِبُونَ
63:1.en: When the hypocrites come unto thee (O Muhammad), they say: We bear witness that thou art indeed Allah's messenger. And Allah knoweth that thou art indeed His messenger, and Allah beareth witness that the hypocrites indeed are speaking falsely

63:2.ar: ٱتَّخَذُوٓاْ أَيۡمَٰنَهُمۡ جُنَّةࣰ فَصَدُّواْ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِۚ إِنَّهُمۡ سَآءَ مَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
63:2.en: They make their faith a pretext so that they may turn (men) from the way of Allah. Verily evil is that which they are wont to do

63:3.ar: ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمۡ ءَامَنُواْ ثُمَّ كَفَرُواْ فَطُبِعَ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمۡ فَهُمۡ لَا يَفۡقَهُونَ
63:3.en: That is because they believed, then disbelieved, therefore their hearts are sealed so that they understand not

63:4.ar: ۞وَإِذَا رَأَيۡتَهُمۡ تُعۡجِبُكَ أَجۡسَامُهُمۡۖ وَإِن يَقُولُواْ تَسۡمَعۡ لِقَوۡلِهِمۡۖ كَأَنَّهُمۡ خُشُبࣱ مُّسَنَّدَةࣱۖ يَحۡسَبُونَ كُلَّ صَيۡحَةٍ عَلَيۡهِمۡۚ هُمُ ٱلۡعَدُوُّ فَٱحۡذَرۡهُمۡۚ قَٰتَلَهُمُ ٱللَّهُۖ أَنَّىٰ يُؤۡفَكُونَ
63:4.en: And when thou seest them their figures please thee; and if they speak thou givest ear unto their speech. (They are) as though they were blocks of wood in striped cloaks. They deem every shout to be against them. They are the enemy, so beware of them. Allah confound them! How they are perverted

63:5.ar: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمۡ تَعَالَوۡاْ يَسۡتَغۡفِرۡ لَكُمۡ رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ لَوَّوۡاْ رُءُوسَهُمۡ وَرَأَيۡتَهُمۡ يَصُدُّونَ وَهُم مُّسۡتَكۡبِرُونَ
63:5.en: And when it is said unto them: Come! The messenger of Allah will ask forgiveness for you! they avert their faces and thou seest them turning away, disdainful

63:6.ar: سَوَآءٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡ أَسۡتَغۡفَرۡتَ لَهُمۡ أَمۡ لَمۡ تَسۡتَغۡفِرۡ لَهُمۡ لَن يَغۡفِرَ ٱللَّهُ لَهُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهۡدِي ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلۡفَٰسِقِينَ
63:6.en: Whether thou ask forgiveness for them or ask not forgiveness for them is all one for them; Allah will not forgive them. Lo! Allah guideth not the evil-living folk

63:7.ar: هُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ لَا تُنفِقُواْ عَلَىٰ مَنۡ عِندَ رَسُولِ ٱللَّهِ حَتَّىٰ يَنفَضُّواْۗ وَلِلَّهِ خَزَآئِنُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱلۡمُنَٰفِقِينَ لَا يَفۡقَهُونَ
63:7.en: They it is who say: Spend not on behalf of those (who dwell) with Allah's messenger that they may disperse (and go away from you); when Allah's are the treasures of the heavens and the earth; but the hypocrites comprehend not

63:8.ar: يَقُولُونَ لَئِن رَّجَعۡنَآ إِلَى ٱلۡمَدِينَةِ لَيُخۡرِجَنَّ ٱلۡأَعَزُّ مِنۡهَا ٱلۡأَذَلَّۚ وَلِلَّهِ ٱلۡعِزَّةُ وَلِرَسُولِهِۦ وَلِلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱلۡمُنَٰفِقِينَ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
63:8.en: They say: Surely, if we return to Al-Madinah the mightier will soon drive out the weaker; when might belongeth to Allah and to His messenger and to the believers; but the hypocrites know not

63:9.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تُلۡهِكُمۡ أَمۡوَٰلُكُمۡ وَلَآ أَوۡلَٰدُكُمۡ عَن ذِكۡرِ ٱللَّهِۚ وَمَن يَفۡعَلۡ ذَٰلِكَ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡخَٰسِرُونَ
63:9.en: O ye who believe! Let not your wealth nor your children distract you from remembrance of Allah. Those who do so, they are the losers

63:10.ar: وَأَنفِقُواْ مِن مَّا رَزَقۡنَٰكُم مِّن قَبۡلِ أَن يَأۡتِيَ أَحَدَكُمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ فَيَقُولَ رَبِّ لَوۡلَآ أَخَّرۡتَنِيٓ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلࣲ قَرِيبࣲ فَأَصَّدَّقَ وَأَكُن مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
63:10.en: And spend of that wherewith We have provided you before death cometh unto one of you and he saith: My Lord! If only thou wouldst reprieve me for a little while, then I would give alms and be among the righteous

63:11.ar: وَلَن يُؤَخِّرَ ٱللَّهُ نَفۡسًا إِذَا جَآءَ أَجَلُهَاۚ وَٱللَّهُ خَبِيرُۢ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ
63:11.en: But Allah reprieveth no soul when its term cometh, and Allah is Informed of what ye do

64:1.ar: يُسَبِّحُ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ لَهُ ٱلۡمُلۡكُ وَلَهُ ٱلۡحَمۡدُۖ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرٌ
64:1.en: All that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth glorifieth Allah; unto Him belongeth Sovereignty and unto Him belongeth praise, and He is Able to do all things

64:2.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَكُمۡ فَمِنكُمۡ كَافِرࣱ وَمِنكُم مُّؤۡمِنࣱۚ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ
64:2.en: He it is Who created you, but one of you is a disbeliever and one of you is a believer, and Allah is Seer of what ye do

64:3.ar: خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَصَوَّرَكُمۡ فَأَحۡسَنَ صُوَرَكُمۡۖ وَإِلَيۡهِ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
64:3.en: He created the heavens and the earth with truth, and He shaped you and made good your shapes, and unto Him is the journeying

64:4.ar: يَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَيَعۡلَمُ مَا تُسِرُّونَ وَمَا تُعۡلِنُونَۚ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمُۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ
64:4.en: He knoweth all that is in the heavens and the earth, and He knoweth what ye conceal and what ye publish. And Allah is Aware of what is in the breasts (of men)

64:5.ar: أَلَمۡ يَأۡتِكُمۡ نَبَؤُاْ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِن قَبۡلُ فَذَاقُواْ وَبَالَ أَمۡرِهِمۡ وَلَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمࣱ‏
64:5.en: Hath not the story reached you of those who disbelieved of old and so did taste the ill-effects of their conduct, and theirs will be a painful doom

64:6.ar: ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُۥ كَانَت تَّأۡتِيهِمۡ رُسُلُهُم بِٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتِ فَقَالُوٓاْ أَبَشَرࣱ يَهۡدُونَنَا فَكَفَرُواْ وَتَوَلَّواْۖ وَّٱسۡتَغۡنَى ٱللَّهُۚ وَٱللَّهُ غَنِيٌّ حَمِيدࣱ‏
64:6.en: That was because their messengers (from Allah) kept coming unto them with clear proofs (of Allah's Sovereignty), but they said: Shall mere mortals guide us? So they disbelieved and turned away, and Allah was independent (of them). Allah is Absolute, Owner of Praise

64:7.ar: زَعَمَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓاْ أَن لَّن يُبۡعَثُواْۚ قُلۡ بَلَىٰ وَرَبِّي لَتُبۡعَثُنَّ ثُمَّ لَتُنَبَّؤُنَّ بِمَا عَمِلۡتُمۡۚ وَذَٰلِكَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ يَسِيرࣱ‏
64:7.en: Those who disbelieve assert that they will not be raised again. Say (unto them, O Muhammad): Yea, verily, by my Lord! ye will be raised again and then ye will be informed of what ye did; and that is easy for Allah

64:8.ar: فَـَٔامِنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ وَٱلنُّورِ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنزَلۡنَاۚ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ خَبِيرࣱ‏
64:8.en: So believe in Allah and His messenger and the light which We have revealed. And Allah is Informed of what ye do

64:9.ar: يَوۡمَ يَجۡمَعُكُمۡ لِيَوۡمِ ٱلۡجَمۡعِۖ ذَٰلِكَ يَوۡمُ ٱلتَّغَابُنِۗ وَمَن يُؤۡمِنۢ بِٱللَّهِ وَيَعۡمَلۡ صَٰلِحࣰ ا يُكَفِّرۡ عَنۡهُ سَيِّـَٔاتِهِۦ وَيُدۡخِلۡهُ جَنَّٰتࣲ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَآ أَبَدࣰ اۚ ذَٰلِكَ ٱلۡفَوۡزُ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ
64:9.en: The day when He shall gather you unto the Day of Assembling, that will be a day of mutual disillusion. And whoso believeth in Allah and doeth right, He will remit from him his evil deeds and will bring him unto Gardens underneath which rivers flow, therein to abide for ever. That is the supreme triumph

64:10.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَكَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ أَصۡحَٰبُ ٱلنَّارِ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَاۖ وَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
64:10.en: But those who disbelieve and deny Our revelations, such are owners of the Fire; they will abide therein - a hapless journey's end

64:11.ar: مَآ أَصَابَ مِن مُّصِيبَةٍ إِلَّا بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِۗ وَمَن يُؤۡمِنۢ بِٱللَّهِ يَهۡدِ قَلۡبَهُۥۚ وَٱللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءٍ عَلِيمࣱ‏
64:11.en: No calamity befalleth save by Allah's leave. And whosoever believeth in Allah, He guideth his heart. And Allah is Knower of all things

64:12.ar: وَأَطِيعُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُواْ ٱلرَّسُولَۚ فَإِن تَوَلَّيۡتُمۡ فَإِنَّمَا عَلَىٰ رَسُولِنَا ٱلۡبَلَٰغُ ٱلۡمُبِينُ
64:12.en: Obey Allah and obey His messenger; but if ye turn away, then the duty of Our messenger is only to convey (the message) plainly

64:13.ar: ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَۚ وَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَلۡيَتَوَكَّلِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ
64:13.en: Allah! There is no Allah save Him. In Allah, therefore, let believers put their trust

64:14.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِنَّ مِنۡ أَزۡوَٰجِكُمۡ وَأَوۡلَٰدِكُمۡ عَدُوࣰّ ا لَّكُمۡ فَٱحۡذَرُوهُمۡۚ وَإِن تَعۡفُواْ وَتَصۡفَحُواْ وَتَغۡفِرُواْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمٌ
64:14.en: O ye who believe! Lo! among your wives and your children there are enemies for you, therefor beware of them. And if ye efface and overlook and forgive, then lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

64:15.ar: إِنَّمَآ أَمۡوَٰلُكُمۡ وَأَوۡلَٰدُكُمۡ فِتۡنَةࣱۚ وَٱللَّهُ عِندَهُۥٓ أَجۡرٌ عَظِيمࣱ‏
64:15.en: Your wealth and your children are only a temptation, whereas Allah! with Him is an immense reward

64:16.ar: فَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ مَا ٱسۡتَطَعۡتُمۡ وَٱسۡمَعُواْ وَأَطِيعُواْ وَأَنفِقُواْ خَيۡرࣰ ا لِّأَنفُسِكُمۡۗ وَمَن يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفۡسِهِۦ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ
64:16.en: So keep your duty to Allah as best ye can, and listen, and obey, and spend; that is better for your souls. And whoso is saved from his own greed, such are the successful

64:17.ar: إِن تُقۡرِضُواْ ٱللَّهَ قَرۡضًا حَسَنࣰ ا يُضَٰعِفۡهُ لَكُمۡ وَيَغۡفِرۡ لَكُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ شَكُورٌ حَلِيمٌ
64:17.en: If ye lend unto Allah a goodly loan, He will double it for you and will forgive you, for Allah is Responsive, Clement

64:18.en: Knower of the Invisible and the Visible, the Mighty, the Wise

9VM5DfVsc-0.speaker_note: Surah Summaries series; refers back to yesterday's lecture in the same cluster and to his own explanations elsewhere
9VM5DfVsc-0.title: Surat Al-Munafiqun and At-Taghabun Summaries
9VM5DfVsc-0.one_line: Two warnings for a Muslim society: hypocrisy that hollows it from within, and losing sight of Allah amid wealth, family and disputes.
9VM5DfVsc-0.summary: He presents al-Munafiqun and at-Taghabun as two warnings within the cluster that organizes Muslim communal life. Hypocrites look impressive and speak well but are hollow, and the surah names them the real enemy. Yet the Prophet's handling of Abdullah ibn Ubayy shows there is no aggression against them: he refused to punish him, even when Ibn Ubayy's own son offered to do it, because turning on your own citizens is a downward spiral. He then widens hypocrisy to its milder form: Muslims on paper, distracted by wealth and children, who never give back their time, knowledge or money. This, he says, is the community's actual problem, fixed by good services and engagement, and he forbids labelling anyone a hypocrite; these verses are mirrors for oneself. At-Taghabun, a Medinan surah with a Makkan flavour, reminds people buried in institutional work and disputes why they serve. The day of mutual loss strips away illusions. Spouses and children can be distractions or even enemies, yet the response is to pardon, forgive and keep working. Wealth and family are only a test. He urges giving what you have as a loan to Allah and not letting side battles slow you down.

outline.heading: Opening
Two surahs on what must not happen in a Muslim society
outline.gist: The cluster organizes Muslim life inside and outside the community; these two surahs focus on dangers to avoid.

outline.heading: Hypocrites who testify to the Messenger and lie
outline.gist: They claim belief to get close to the community and run their own agenda behind it.

outline.heading: Impressive looks and words, like propped-up timber
outline.gist: Their appearance and speech are a show, compared to ornamental wooden beams that hold nothing up.

outline.heading: Living in fear: they are the enemy
outline.gist: A gap between outside and inside breeds unhappiness and fear; Allah calls them the real enemy to beware of, more than any external foe.

outline.heading: No aggression toward exposed hypocrites
outline.gist: Muslims do not fight, kill or expel them; Allah takes on their punishment while they are treated with the same respect as everyone.

outline.heading: Abdullah ibn Ubayy and not turning on your own citizens
outline.gist: Despite plots and withdrawing 300 men at Uhud, the Prophet would not punish him; every society will have citizens who do not share its goals.

outline.heading: Turning away from the Prophet's prayer for forgiveness
outline.gist: Forgiveness cannot be sought for someone who does not want it; it is private between a servant and his Lord.

outline.heading: Starving the believers to scatter them
outline.gist: Hypocrites urged people to stop giving to poor Muslims so they would leave the Prophet.

outline.heading: A tribal brawl and the Prophet's anger at tribalism
outline.gist: When Muhajirun and Ansar called on their own groups during a dispute, the Prophet ended it abruptly and called it disgusting.

outline.heading: Ibn Ubayy's insult and his son's offer
outline.gist: Ibn Ubayy said the honourable would expel the lowly; his believing son asked to carry out any execution himself, and the Prophet told him to be the best son instead, so no one would say Muhammad kills his companions.

outline.heading: Lower levels of hypocrisy
outline.gist: Beyond those working against Islam are Muslims who commit to nothing in the religion.

outline.heading: Do not let wealth and children distract you
outline.gist: Letting status, money or family distract you from the remembrance of Allah is a level of hypocrisy.

outline.heading: Give before death arrives
outline.gist: Give from everything you were given, time, knowledge, empathy and money, before you beg for more time on your deathbed and are refused.

outline.heading: Muslims on paper: the community's real problem
outline.gist: Indifferent, distracted Muslims are everywhere in our families; the remedy is proper services, engagement and reminders, since they do not hate the deen.

outline.heading: Never label anyone a hypocrite
outline.gist: Hypocrisy is inside and only Allah sees it; these verses and hadith are for self-examination, as Umar feared it in himself, not formulas for judging others.

outline.heading: Interlude
At-Taghabun: the day the deceptions fall away
outline.gist: From the root for being fooled in a sale, the name points to Judgment Day when lies and illusions vanish and the truth prevails.

outline.heading: A Medinan surah with a Makkan flavour
outline.gist: Its verses are full of creed and creation, placed in the middle of the juz to reset what matters.

outline.heading: Losing sight amid institutional work and disputes
outline.gist: Community work, social problems and differences of opinion can make you forget you are doing it for Allah and will be held accountable.

outline.heading: Longing for early spirituality; you will be resurrected
outline.gist: People look back wishing for the sujood and dua they once felt; too much life piled on. The verse swears resurrection and full reminder of deeds.

outline.heading: The day of gathering exposes reality
outline.gist: Believe in the light that was sent; facing reality without our comforting illusions will be painful.

outline.heading: Belief and right deeds are all that count
outline.gist: If you believed and did good for Allah you succeed, otherwise not; everything else is irrelevant.

outline.heading: Spouses and children who become enemies: pardon and forgive
outline.gist: Family can pull you from Allah's way despite your effort; respond with pardon and keep your enthusiasm for working for Allah.

outline.heading: Wealth and children are a test; taqwa as you are able; a good loan
outline.gist: Draw close to Allah to your capacity, listen, obey and give; whoever is saved from his own selfishness succeeds, and what you give is a loan Allah multiplies.

outline.heading: Two paired warnings for a community
outline.gist: Al-Munafiqun warns of a social danger that can ruin what you build; at-Taghabun warns from the other side against forgetting whom you serve.

outline.heading: Do not get caught in side wars
outline.gist: Disputes that go nowhere hold you back; listen, obey, give and do not let anything stop you.

outline.heading: When family does not turn out as hoped: it is the test
outline.gist: You tried your best with marriage and children; forgive, do your best and draw closer to Allah, which is all you were asked.

outline.heading: The goal is serving Allah, not the perfect life
outline.gist: Houses, cars, status and a perfect family are not the goal; Medinan clusters carry Makkan-like verses to remind you where you are going.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Hypocrisy (nifaq)
themes.note: Hypocrites are the real internal enemy, yet are treated with respect and never targeted; milder hypocrisy is distracted, uncommitted Islam, and no one may be labelled a hypocrite.

themes.label: The Prophet's attributes, character and example
themes.note: The Prophet's restraint with Ibn Ubayy and his anger at tribalism model how to treat dissenting citizens.

themes.label: Zakat, charity and giving
themes.note: Give time, knowledge, love and money before death; giving is a hallmark of a good Muslim.

themes.label: Self-honesty and self-accountability (muhasabah)
themes.note: Verses on hypocrisy are for checking oneself, not for judging others.

themes.label: Purpose, meaning and the point of life
themes.note: At-Taghabun resets focus: do not let community work and life's pile-up make you forget why you serve.

themes.label: Family: parents, relatives, kinship ties
themes.note: Spouses and children can become enemies to one's deen; the response is pardon and continued effort.

themes.label: Trials, hardship and resilience
themes.note: Family and wealth are a test; when things do not work out, you are judged only on your effort.

themes.label: Human equality and racism
themes.note: The Prophet condemned tribal calls during a brawl as disgusting.

hadith.gist: During a dispute between Muhajirun and Ansar, the Prophet condemned the tribal rallying calls as foul.
Abdullah, son of Ibn Ubayy, asked to execute his father himself if ordered; the Prophet refused and told him to treat his father well, so people would not say Muhammad kills his companions.

maxims: Use these verses so that you don't become the problem
Just a part of the test
Don't get caught up in side wars

stories.point: Even an open plotter was not punished, because a state that turns on its own citizens spirals downward.
Loyalty to the Prophet did not override being a good son; the Prophet protected the community's reputation for justice.
He feared hypocrisy in himself, showing these texts are for self-examination.

takeaways: Never accuse anyone of hypocrisy; use these verses to check yourself.
Reach indifferent Muslims through good services and engagement rather than condemnation.
Give your time, knowledge, love and money now, before death closes the door.
When family or community disputes weigh on you, pardon, forgive and keep working for Allah.
Remind yourself regularly why you do community work so it does not swallow your spirituality.
